title.zh: 卷十三 魏書十三 鍾繇華歆王朗傳
title.en: Volume 13: Book of Wei 13: Biographies of Zhong Yao, Hua Xin, and Wang Lang
title.raw: 卷十三 魏書十三 鍾繇華歆王朗傳 Volume 13: Book of Wei 13: Biographies of Zhong Yao, Hua Xin, and Wang Lang

sentences.zh: 鍾繇字元常，頴川長社人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao, courtesy name Yuanchang, was a man of Changshe in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao, whose courtesy name was Yuanchang, came from Changshe in Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》曰：鍾皓字季明，溫良篤慎，博學詩律，教授門生千有餘人，爲郡功曹。

translations.literal: 〈The Accounts of Worthies of Antiquity states: Zhong Hao, courtesy name Jiming, was gentle, kind, sincere, and cautious; he was broadly learned in the Odes and statutes; he taught more than a thousand disciples and served as merit clerk for the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 〈According to the Accounts of Worthies of Antiquity, Zhong Hao, style Jiming, was mild, trustworthy, and careful, well read in the Classic of Poetry and the law, instructed over a thousand students, and held the post of commandery merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 時太丘長陳寔爲西門亭長，皓深獨敬異。

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Taiqiu, Chen Shi, was west-gate pavilion chief, and Hao alone among them deeply respected him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen Shi, magistrate of Taiqiu, also served as chief of the west-gate pavilion; Zhong Hao alone held him in singular esteem.

sentences.zh: 寔少皓十七歲，常禮待與同分義。

translations.literal: Shi was seventeen years younger than Hao, yet always treated him with ritual courtesy and shared obligation with him as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi was seventeen years Zhong Hao’s junior, yet he habitually showed him the courtesy due an elder and treated him as a peer in duty and friendship.

sentences.zh: 會辟公府，臨辭，太守問：「誰可代君？」

translations.literal: When he was summoned to the Excellencies’ offices, on the eve of his departure the grand administrator asked, “Who can replace you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shi was called to serve in the central government and came to take his leave, the grand administrator asked him, “Whom can we appoint in your place?"

sentences.zh: 皓曰：「明府欲必得其人，西門亭長可用。」

translations.literal: Hao said, “If my lord must have the right man, the west-gate pavilion chief will do."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hao replied, “If you insist on a worthy successor, the chief of the west-gate pavilion will serve."

sentences.zh: 寔曰：「鍾君似不察人爲意，不知何獨識我？」

translations.literal: Shi said, “Lord Zhong does not seem to take judging men as his concern; I do not know why he alone recognized me."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi said, “Master Zhong hardly makes a habit of sizing people up—why should he have singled me out?"

sentences.zh: 皓爲司徒掾，公出，道路泥濘，導從惡其相灑，去公車絕遠。

translations.literal: Hao was a clerk under the Minister of Education; when the minister went out, the roads were mired in mud; the escorts disliked splattering one another and kept themselves very far from the official carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hao served as an aide to the Minister of Education. One day the minister went abroad on roads turned to mud; his attendants, loath to splash one another, fell far behind the carriage.

sentences.zh: 公椎軾言：「司徒今日爲獨行耳！」

translations.literal: The minister struck the carriage crossbar and said, “The Minister of Education walks alone today!"
translations.idiomatic: The minister rapped the carriage rail and exclaimed, “So the Minister of Education travels alone today!"

sentences.zh: 還府向閤，鈴下不扶，令揖掾屬，公奮手不顧。

translations.literal: Returning to the office and approaching the gate tower, the bell attendants did not assist him; he ordered the aides to bow; the minister waved his hand and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to headquarters he reached the inner gate, but the runners did not steady him; when he told his staff to bow in salute, he brushed them off with a wave and strode past without a glance.

sentences.zh: 時舉府掾屬皆投劾出，皓爲西曹掾，即開府門分布曉語已出者，曰：「臣下不能得自直於君，若司隷舉繩墨，以公失宰相之禮，又不勝任，諸君終身何所任邪？」

translations.literal: Then all the office aides submitted resignations and left; Hao was west-bureau clerk; he immediately opened the main gate, posted notices, and spoke to those who had already gone out, saying, “As subjects we cannot make ourselves right before our lord; if the Metropolitan Superintendent applies the cord and ink line, charging the minister with losing the deportment of a chief minister and being unfit for office, where in your lives will you ever serve?"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every aide in the ministry handed in his resignation and walked out. Zhong Hao, a clerk in the west bureau, threw open the headquarters gate, sent word around, and addressed those who had already left: “If we cannot justify ourselves to our superiors, and the Metropolitan Superintendent cites the minister for breach of protocol and incompetence, what career will any of you ever have?"

sentences.zh: 掾屬以故皆止。

translations.literal: For this reason the aides all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On that account they all stayed.

sentences.zh: 都官果移西曹掾，問空府去意，皓召都官吏，以見掾屬名示之，乃止。

translations.literal: The capital officials indeed sent a document to the west-bureau clerk asking the meaning of the empty office’s departure; Hao summoned the capital clerks and showed them the register of aides’ names, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The capital bureau did send a query to the west-bureau clerk about the mass walkout; Zhong Hao assembled the clerks, showed them the roster of aides, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 前後九辟三府，遷南鄉、林慮長，不之官。

translations.literal: Nine times in all he was summoned to the Three Offices; he was promoted to magistrate of Nanxiang and Linyu but did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned nine times to serve in the Three Excellencies’ administrations and was appointed magistrate of Nanxiang and of Linyu, yet he never went to take up those posts.

sentences.zh: 時郡中先輩爲海內所歸者，蒼梧太守定陵陳稚叔、故黎陽令潁陰荀淑及皓。

translations.literal: At that time among the commandery’s elders whom the realm looked up to were the Administrator of Cangwu, Chen Zhishu of Dingling; the former magistrate of Liyang, Xun Shu of Yingyin; and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery’s senior figures whom the empire admired were Chen Zhishu of Dingling, then governor of Cangwu; Xun Shu of Yingyin, once magistrate of Liyang; and Zhong Hao.

sentences.zh: 少府李膺常宗此三人，曰：「荀君清識難尚，陳、鍾至德可師。」

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Household Li Ying always took these three as models, saying, “Lord Xun’s clear judgment is hard to match; Chen and Zhong’s supreme virtue may be taken as teachers."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying of the Superintendent’s office regularly held up these three as exemplars, remarking, “Master Xun’s discernment is second to none; the moral stature of Chen and Zhong is fit to be our teachers."

sentences.zh: 膺之姑爲皓兄之妻，生子覲，與膺年齊，並有令名。

translations.literal: Ying’s aunt was the wife of Hao’s elder brother; she bore a son, Jin, who was the same age as Ying; both had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying’s aunt had married Zhong Hao’s elder brother and bore a son, Zhong Jin, who was Li Ying’s contemporary; both young men were widely esteemed.

sentences.zh: 覲又好學慕古，有退讓之行。

translations.literal: Jin also loved learning and admired antiquity; he had conduct of yielding and deference.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jin loved learning and looked to the ancients for a model, and he carried himself with modest reserve.

sentences.zh: 爲童幼時，膺祖太尉脩言：「覲似我家性，國有道不廢，國無道免於刑戮者也。」

translations.literal: When he was still a child, Ying’s grandfather, Grand Commandant Xiu, said, “Jin resembles the nature of our house: when the state has the Way he will not be cast aside; when the state lacks the Way he will escape execution and mutilation."
translations.idiomatic: While Jin was still a boy, Li Ying’s grandfather, the Grand Commandant Li Xiu, observed, “The boy has our family’s temperament: in an ordered age he will not be overlooked; in a chaotic one he will avoid the headsman’s block."

sentences.zh: 復以膺妹妻之。

translations.literal: Again he gave Ying’s younger sister to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Li Ying’s sister to Zhong Jin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 覲辟州宰，未甞屈就。

translations.literal: Jin was summoned by the provincial chief; he never condescended to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the provincial governor tried to recruit him, Zhong Jin refused to lower himself to an appointment he did not want.

sentences.zh: 膺謂覲曰：「孟軻以爲人無好惡是非之心，非人也。

translations.literal: Ying said to Jin, “Meng Ke held that a person who lacks a mind for liking and disliking, right and wrong, is not a person.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying said to him, “Mencius taught that without a sense of likes and dislikes, of right and wrong, one hardly counts as human.

sentences.zh: 弟於人何太無皂白邪！」

translations.literal: Younger brother, toward others why are you utterly without black and white!"
translations.idiomatic: Brother, why do you refuse to see any difference between good men and bad?"

sentences.zh: 覲甞以膺之言白皓，皓曰：「元禮，祖公在位，諸父並盛，韓公之甥，故得然耳。

translations.literal: Jin once reported Ying’s words to Hao; Hao said, “Yuanli—with his grandfather in office, his uncles all flourishing, and himself the nephew of Lord Han—therefore can be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jin once repeated Li Ying’s words to Zhong Hao, who replied, “Yuanli can afford such talk: his grandfather still holds high rank, his uncles are all influential, and he is related to the Han grandees—that is why he may judge others so freely.

sentences.zh: 國武子好昭人過，以爲怨本，今豈其時！

translations.literal: Guo Wuzi liked to display others’ faults; he took it as the root of resentment—is this now the time!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wuzi made a sport of exposing people’s shortcomings and reaped hatred for it. These are not days for that sort of conduct.

sentences.zh: 保身全家，汝道是也。」

translations.literal: Preserving the body and keeping the whole family—that is your way."
translations.idiomatic: To keep yourself and your household safe—that is the course I commend to you."

sentences.zh: 覲早亡，膺雖荷功名，位至卿佐，而卒隕身世禍。

translations.literal: Jin died early; although Ying bore fame and merit and rose to ministerial aide rank, in the end he fell to disaster of body and age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jin died young. Li Ying won renown and rose to high ministerial office, yet he still perished in the disasters that overtook his family and his generation.

sentences.zh: 皓年六十九，終於家。

translations.literal: Hao, age sixty-nine, ended at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hao died at home at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 皓二子迪、敷，並以黨錮不仕。

translations.literal: Hao’s two sons, Di and Fu, both because of the partisan proscriptions did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hao’s sons, Di and Fu, were barred from office throughout the partisan proscriptions.

sentences.zh: 繇則迪之孫。〉

translations.literal: Yao then was Di’s grandson.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was the grandson of Zhong Di.〉

sentences.zh: 甞與族父瑜俱至洛陽，道遇相者，曰：「此童有貴相，然當厄於水，努力慎之！」

translations.literal: He once went with his clansman uncle Yu to Luoyang; on the road they met a physiognomist who said, “This boy has a noble face, yet he will meet calamity in water; strive to be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, traveling to Luoyang with his kinsman Zhong Yu, he met a fortune-teller who told them, “The lad is marked for greatness, but water will nearly undo him—take every care."

sentences.zh: 行未十里，度橋，馬驚，墯水幾死。

translations.literal: They had not gone ten li when crossing a bridge the horse shied and he fell into the water and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: They had not covered ten li when their mount shied on a bridge and threw him into the river; he barely escaped drowning.

sentences.zh: 瑜以相者言中，益貴繇，而供給資費，使得專學。

translations.literal: Yu because the physiognomist’s words hit the mark valued Yao all the more and supplied funds so that he was able to devote himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu, seeing the prophecy fulfilled, set even greater store by Zhong Yao and paid his expenses so that the boy could study without distraction.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，

translations.literal: He was recommended Filial and Incorrupt,
translations.idiomatic: He received the Filial and Incorrupt recommendation,

sentences.zh: 〈謝承漢書曰：南陽陰脩爲潁川太守，以旌賢擢俊爲務，舉五官掾張仲方正，察功曹鍾繇、主簿荀彧、主記掾張禮、賊曹掾杜祐、孝廉荀攸、計吏郭圖爲吏，以光國朝。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xie Cheng’s Book of Han states: Yin Xiu of Nanyang was Administrator of Yingchuan; he made promoting the worthy and elevating the talented his task; he recommended chief clerk of the five bureaus Zhang Zhong as upright; he inspected merit clerk Zhong Yao, chief secretary Xun Yu, chief registrar Zhang Li, clerk of the bandit bureau Du You, Filial and Incorrupt Xun You, and accounting clerk Guo Tu as officials, in order to brighten the court of the state.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xie Cheng’s Han history records that when Yin Xiu of Nanyang governed Yingchuan he made a point of honoring talent: he nominated Zhang Zhong for integrity, advanced Zhong Yao as merit clerk, Xun Yu as chief secretary, Zhang Li as registrar, Du You for the bandit bureau, Xun You as a recommended scholar, and Guo Tu as clerk of accounts—appointments meant to bring luster to the Han administration.〉

sentences.zh: 除尚書郎、陽陵令，以疾去。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the Masters of Writing and magistrate of Yangling; because of illness he left.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a gentleman of the Masters of Writing and magistrate of Yangling, then resigned on grounds of ill health.

sentences.zh: 辟三府，爲廷尉正、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Three Offices and served as rectifier under the Commandant of Justice and gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned repeatedly to the Three Excellencies’ staffs, he rose to rectifier of the Commandant of Justice and gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢帝在西京，李傕、郭汜等亂長安中，與關東斷絕。

translations.literal: At this time the Han emperor was in the western capital; Li Jue, Guo Si, and others threw Chang’an into turmoil, and communication with east of the passes was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven still resided in the western capital while Li Jue, Guo Si, and their allies turned Chang’an into a battleground, severing ties with the lands east of the passes.

sentences.zh: 太祖領兖州牧，始遣使上書。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor held concurrent office as Governor of Yan Province and for the first time sent envoys to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, as Governor of Yan Province, at last began dispatching envoys with memorials to the court.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：太祖遣使從事王必致命天子。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Tales states: the Grand Progenitor sent attendant clerk Wang Bi to deliver his charge to the Son of Heaven.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu relates that Cao Cao sent his aide Wang Bi to bear his message to the emperor.〉

sentences.zh: 傕、汜等以爲「關東欲自立天子，今曹操雖有使命，非其至實」，議留太祖使，拒絕其意。

translations.literal: Jue, Si, and others thought, “East of the passes they wish to set up their own Son of Heaven; now although Cao Cao has a mission, it is not his utmost sincerity,” and deliberated detaining the Grand Progenitor’s envoy and rejecting his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jue, Si, and the others thought, “Those east of the passes wish to set up a Son of Heaven for themselves. Although Cao Cao now comes with a commission, he is not acting with complete sincerity,” and they discussed detaining Taizu's envoy and rejecting his proposal.

sentences.zh: 繇說傕、汜等曰：「方今英雄並起，各矯命專制，唯曹兖州乃心王室，而逆其忠款，非所以副將來之望也。」

translations.literal: Yao persuaded Jue, Si, and others, saying, “At present heroes rise together; each counterfeits orders and acts on his own authority; only Governor Cao of Yan sets his heart on the royal house—yet to thwart his loyal sincerity is not the means to answer what the future hopes for."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao urged them: “Warlords everywhere forge edicts and rule as they please; Cao Cao of Yan alone still looks to the Han throne. To spurn his loyal gesture would disappoint everyone who still hopes for restoration."

sentences.zh: 傕、汜等用繇言，厚加荅報，由是太祖使命遂得通。

translations.literal: Jue, Si, and others used Yao’s words and replied generously; thereby the Grand Progenitor’s missions were able to get through.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si accepted his advice and returned a generous answer, so Cao Cao’s envoys could reach the court at last.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣數聽荀彧之稱繇，又聞其說傕、汜，益虛心。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had repeatedly heard Xun Yu praise Yao and also heard of his persuading Jue and Si; he became all the more open-minded toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had often heard Xun Yu praise Zhong Yao and now learned how he had swayed Li Jue and Guo Si; he grew still more eager to win him over.

sentences.zh: 後傕脅天子，繇與尚書郎韓斌同策謀。

translations.literal: Later when Jue coerced the Son of Heaven, Yao together with gentleman of the Masters of Writing Han Bin jointly planned strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jue later coerced the Son of Heaven, Zhong Yao and Han Bin, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, planned strategy together.

sentences.zh: 天子得出長安，繇有力焉。

translations.literal: That the Son of Heaven was able to get out of Chang’an—Yao had strength therein.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao played a major part in the emperor’s escape from Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，遷侍中尚書僕射，并錄前功封東武亭侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace assistant secretary; he was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and supervisor of the Masters of Writing; concurrently recording former merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his former achievements were also recorded, and he was enfeoffed as Village Marquis of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 時關中諸將馬騰、韓遂等，各擁彊兵相與爭。

translations.literal: At that time the generals within the passes, Ma Teng, Han Sui, and others, each held strong troops and contended with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Within the passes, Ma Teng, Han Sui, and the other warlords each commanded a powerful army and fought one another for supremacy.

sentences.zh: 太祖方有事山東，以關右爲憂。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was then occupied with affairs east of the mountains and took the right of the passes as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was tied down in the east and worried constantly about his western flank.

sentences.zh: 乃表繇以侍中守司隷校尉，持節督關中諸軍，委之以後事，特使不拘科制。

translations.literal: Therefore he memorialized Yao as attendant-in-ordinary acting Metropolitan Superintendent, bearing credentials to supervise all armies within the passes, entrusting him with rear affairs, specially ordering that he not be bound by statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized to appoint Zhong Yao as Palace Attendant and acting Colonel-Director of Retainers, with credentials to supervise the armies in Guanzhong. He entrusted him with rear affairs and specially allowed him not to be bound by statutory regulations.

sentences.zh: 繇至長安，移書騰、遂等，爲陳禍福，騰、遂各遣子入侍。

translations.literal: When Yao reached Chang’an he sent documents to Teng, Sui, and others, setting forth fortune and disaster for them; Teng and Sui each sent sons to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao reached Chang’an and wrote to Ma Teng, Han Sui, and their peers, explaining the stakes; each commander sent a son to the capital as hostage.

sentences.zh: 太祖在官渡，與袁紹相持，繇送馬二千餘匹給軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was at Guandu, locked with Yuan Shao; Yao sent more than two thousand horses to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held the line against Yuan Shao at Guandu, Zhong Yao forwarded over two thousand horses to his camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖與繇書曰：「得所送馬，甚應其急。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wrote to Yao, saying, “Receiving the horses you sent greatly meets the urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote to him, “Your horses arrived just when we needed them most.

sentences.zh: 關右平定，朝廷無西顧之憂，足下之勳也。

translations.literal: The right of the passes being pacified, the court has no worry of looking west—that is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: The west is quiet and the court need no longer glance nervously over its shoulder—that is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭何鎮守關中，足食成軍，亦適當爾。」

translations.literal: In the past Xiao He guarded the passes within, fully feeding and completing the army—it also fit just thus."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Xiao He held the Guanzhong heartland and fed the armies until they could fight; you have done no less."

sentences.zh: 其後匈奴單于作亂平陽，繇帥諸軍圍之，未拔；

translations.literal: Afterward the Xiongnu Shanyu made rebellion at Pingyang; Yao led the various armies and besieged him; he had not yet taken him;
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xiongnu chanyu rose at Pingyang; Zhong Yao invested the city but had not yet reduced it when—

sentences.zh: 而袁尚所置河東太守郭援到河東，衆甚盛。

translations.literal: but Guo Yuan, whom Yuan Shang had appointed Administrator of Hedong, arrived in Hedong; his host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: —Yuan Shao’s son Yuan Shang sent his appointee Guo Yuan into Hedong with a massive force.

sentences.zh: 諸將議欲釋之去，繇曰：「袁氏方彊，援之來，關中陰與之通，所以未悉叛者，顧吾威名故耳。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated wishing to release it and depart; Yao said, “The Yuan clan is just now strong; Yuan’s coming—the interior of the passes secretly communicates with them—the reason they have not all rebelled is only because of our awe-inspiring name.
translations.idiomatic: Some generals urged lifting the siege and withdrawing. Zhong Yao objected: “The Yuans are still formidable. Guo Yuan’s advance means the western lords are colluding with them in secret. They have not risen as one only because they still fear our reputation.

sentences.zh: 若棄而去，示之以弱，所在之民，誰非寇讎？

translations.literal: If we abandon and go away, showing them weakness—among the people wherever they are, who is not bandit-enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If we walk away now we advertise weakness, and every village will turn against us as though we were the enemy.

sentences.zh: 縱吾欲歸，其得至乎！

translations.literal: Even if we wish to return, can we get there!
translations.idiomatic: Even if we tried to retreat, could we hope to get home alive?

sentences.zh: 此爲未戰先自敗也。

translations.literal: This is to defeat ourselves before we have even fought.
translations.idiomatic: We would be routing ourselves before the enemy lifts a finger.

sentences.zh: 且援剛愎好勝，必易吾軍，若渡汾爲營，及其未濟擊之，可大克也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Guo Yuan is obstinate and fond of victory; he is sure to despise our army; if he crosses the Fen and makes camp, strike him before he has finished crossing and you can win a great victory."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Guo Yuan is stubborn and vain; he will underestimate us. If he tries to ford the Fen and pitch camp, we should hit him midstream and win a crushing victory."

sentences.zh: 張旣說馬騰會擊援，騰遣子超將精兵逆之。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji persuaded Ma Teng to join in striking Yuan; Teng sent his son Chao leading picked troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji persuaded Ma Teng to join the attack; Ma Teng sent his son Ma Chao at the head of picked troops to intercept Guo Yuan.

sentences.zh: 援至，果輕渡汾，衆止之，不從。

translations.literal: When Yuan arrived, he indeed lightly crossed the Fen; the host tried to stop him; he did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan arrived and, just as predicted, made a reckless crossing of the Fen; his officers warned him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 濟水未半，擊，大破之，

translations.literal: When the crossing of the water was not yet half, they struck and greatly broke them,
translations.idiomatic: They attacked before half his force had reached the far bank and shattered his army,

sentences.zh: 〈司馬彪戰略曰：袁尚遣高幹、郭援將兵數萬人，與匈奴單于寇河東，遣使與馬騰、韓遂等連和，騰等陰許之。

translations.literal: 〈Sima Biao’s Strategic Writings states: Yuan Shang sent Gao Gan and Guo Yuan leading troops numbering tens of thousands, together with the Xiongnu Shanyu, to raid Hedong; he sent envoys to ally with Ma Teng, Han Sui, and others; Teng and the rest secretly promised them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sima Biao’s Zhanlüe records that Yuan Shang dispatched Gao Gan and Guo Yuan with tens of thousands of men, together with the Xiongnu chanyu, to ravage Hedong, and sent envoys to Ma Teng and Han Sui proposing an alliance, which they secretly accepted.

sentences.zh: 傅幹說騰曰：「古人有言『順道者昌，逆德者亡』。

translations.literal: Fu Gan persuaded Teng, saying, “The ancients had a saying, ‘Those who accord with the Way flourish; those who oppose virtue perish.’
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan urged Ma Teng: “The old proverb runs, ‘He who follows the Way will thrive; he who defies right principle will fall.

sentences.zh: 曹公奉天子誅暴亂，法明國治，上下用命，有義必賞，無義必罰，可謂順道矣。

translations.literal: Lord Cao upholds the Son of Heaven and punishes violence and disorder; laws are clear and the state is ordered; high and low obey commands; there is righteousness—surely reward; there is no righteousness—surely punishment; it may be called according with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao upholds the Son of Heaven and punishes violence and disorder; his laws are clear, the state is well governed, and high and low obey commands. Righteous conduct is always rewarded, and unrighteous conduct is always punished; this may be called following the Way.

sentences.zh: 袁氏背王命，驅胡虜以陵中國，寬而多忌，仁而無斷，兵雖彊，實失天下心，可謂逆德矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan turns its back on the king’s commands, drives Hu captives to oppress the Central States; they are lenient yet full of suspicion, benevolent yet without decision; although troops are strong, in truth they have lost the heart of the realm—it may be called opposing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans defy the throne, set northern tribes on the heartland, affect generosity while nursing endless suspicions, talk of benevolence yet cannot decide a policy. Their armies may be large, but they have forfeited the world’s goodwill—that is what it means to defy moral order.

sentences.zh: 今將軍旣事有道，不盡其力，陰懷兩端，欲以坐觀成敗，吾恐成敗旣定，奉辭責罪，將軍先爲誅首矣。」

translations.literal: Now, General, although you already serve one who has the Way, you do not exhaust your strength; secretly you harbor two ends, wishing by sitting to watch success and failure—I fear when success and failure are already settled, presenting phrases and assigning guilt, the General will first be the chief executed.”
translations.idiomatic: You already acknowledge a legitimate sovereign yet hold back your strength and play both sides, hoping to watch from the sidelines. Once the victor is decided, he will call you to account—and you will be the first head on the block.”

sentences.zh: 於是騰懼。

translations.literal: Thereupon Teng feared.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng was frightened into compliance.

sentences.zh: 幹曰：「智者轉禍爲福。

translations.literal: Gan said, “The wise turn misfortune into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan added, “A wise man turns danger into opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今曹公與袁氏相持，而高幹、郭援獨制河東，曹公雖有萬全之計，不能禁河東之不危也。

translations.literal: Now Lord Cao and the Yuan clan are locked together, yet Gao Gan and Guo Yuan alone control Hedong; although Lord Cao has a myriad-complete plan, he cannot forbid Hedong from not being endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao is locked with the Yuans while Gao Gan and Guo Yuan hold Hedong. No matter how flawless Cao’s strategy, he cannot keep that region from slipping into crisis.

sentences.zh: 將軍誠能引兵討援，內外擊之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: If the General truly can lead troops to punish Yuan, inside and outside striking him, that momentum must be raised.
translations.idiomatic: If you march against Guo Yuan and strike him in concert with Cao’s forces, the enemy cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 是將軍一舉，斷袁氏之臂，解一方之急，曹公必重德將軍。

translations.literal: This is the General’s one stroke—severing the Yuan clan’s arm, relieving one side’s urgency—Lord Cao is sure heavily to honor virtue toward the General.
translations.idiomatic: One blow from you would sever the Yuan arm, lift the siege on our western flank, and earn you Cao Cao’s lasting gratitude.

sentences.zh: 將軍功名，竹帛不能盡載也。

translations.literal: The General’s merit and fame—bamboo and silk cannot exhaust recording them.
translations.idiomatic: Your deeds would overflow every chronicle the historians could write.

sentences.zh: 唯將軍審所擇！」

translations.literal: Only, General, examine what you choose."
translations.idiomatic: General, weigh your choice with care."

sentences.zh: 騰曰：「敬從教。」

translations.literal: Teng said, “Respectfully I follow your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng answered, “I shall do as you advise."

sentences.zh: 於是遣子超將精兵萬餘人，并將遂等兵，與繇會擊援等，大破之。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his son Chao leading more than ten thousand picked troops, and also led Sui and others’ troops, and joined with Yao in striking Yuan and the rest, greatly breaking them.〉
translations.idiomatic: He therefore dispatched Ma Chao with over ten thousand elite horsemen, together with Han Sui’s contingent, to join Zhong Yao against Guo Yuan and crush him utterly.〉

sentences.zh: 斬援，降單于。

translations.literal: They beheaded Yuan and made the Shanyu surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan was beheaded and the chanyu submitted.

sentences.zh: 語在《旣傳》。

translations.literal: The words are in Zhang Ji’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the biography of Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 其後河東衞固作亂，與張晟、張琰及高幹等並爲寇，繇又率諸將討破之。

translations.literal: Afterward Wei Gu of Hedong made rebellion; together with Zhang Sheng, Zhang Yan, and Gao Gan and others they all became bandits; Yao again led the generals to attack and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Gu of Hedong rebelled alongside Zhang Sheng, Zhang Yan, Gao Gan, and others; Zhong Yao once more led the generals and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：詔徵河東太守王邑。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: an edict summoned Hedong Administrator Wang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe records that an imperial summons recalled Wang Yi from the governorship of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 邑以天下未定，心不願徵，而吏民亦戀邑，郡掾衞固及中郎將范先等各詣繇求乞邑。

translations.literal: Yi because the realm was not yet settled, in his heart was unwilling to answer the summons, and the clerks and people also were attached to Yi; commandery aide Wei Gu and General of the Household Gentlemen Fan Xian and others each went to Yao begging for Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was reluctant to leave while the empire remained unsettled, and the officials and commoners of Hedong wanted to keep him. Wei Gu, a commandery aide, Fan Xian, a general of the household, and others went in a body to Zhong Yao to plead that Wang be allowed to stay.

sentences.zh: 而詔已拜杜畿爲太守，畿已入界。

translations.literal: But the edict had already appointed Du Ji as administrator, and Ji had already entered the border.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already named Du Ji governor, and Du had crossed into the commandery.

sentences.zh: 繇不聽先等，促邑交符。

translations.literal: Yao did not listen to Xian and the rest; he urged Yi to hand over the seal-cord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao ignored Fan Xian’s party and ordered Wang Yi to surrender his seal of office at once.

sentences.zh: 邑佩印綬，徑從河北詣許自歸。

translations.literal: Yi wearing seal and ribbon went straight from north of the River to Xu to return himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, still wearing his official insignia, slipped north across the Yellow River and made his own way to the capital at Xu.

sentences.zh: 繇時治在洛陽，自以威禁失督司之法，乃上書自劾曰；

translations.literal: Yao at that time had his administration at Luoyang; he himself thought awe and prohibition had lost the law of supervising the Metropolitan Superintendent; therefore he submitted a memorial impeaching himself, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was then administering from Luoyang. Believing he had failed in the Metropolitan Superintendent’s duty to uphold authority and discipline, he memorialized the throne to impeach himself. He wrote:

sentences.zh: 「臣前上言故鎮北將軍領河東太守安陽亭侯王邑巧辟治官，犯突科條，事當推劾，檢實姦詐。

translations.literal: “Your subject previously submitted words that the former General Who Guards the North concurrently Hedong Administrator Village Marquis of Anyang Wang Yi craftily avoided governing officials, violated and burst through statute articles; the matter ought to be pushed for impeachment, investigating the reality of treacherous deceit.
translations.idiomatic: “I recently reported that Wang Yi, the former General Who Guards the North and concurrent governor of Hedong, Marquis of Anyang village, had evaded lawful supervision and breached the statutes—charges that warranted a full inquiry into his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 被詔書當如所糾。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict document ought to be as what was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: An edict confirmed that the investigation should proceed as I had urged.

sentences.zh: 以其歸罪，故加寬赦。

translations.literal: Because he returned guilt, therefore was added lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Because he confessed his fault, he was granted clemency instead.

sentences.zh: 又臣上言吏民大小，各懷顧望，謂邑當還，拒太守杜畿，今皆反悔，共迎畿之官。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject submitted words that clerks and people great and small each harbored looking-back expectation, saying Yi ought to return, rejecting Administrator Du Ji; now all have turned in repentance and together welcome Ji’s taking office.
translations.idiomatic: I also reported that every rank in Hedong expected Wang Yi’s return and therefore resisted Du Ji; they have since thought better of it and are welcoming Du Ji to his post.

sentences.zh: 謹按文書，臣以空虛，被蒙拔擢，入充近侍，兼典機衡，忝膺重任，總統偏方。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to documents, your subject by emptiness has received elevation, entered to fill near attendance, concurrently superintended the pivot and steelyard, shamefully bore heavy responsibility, overall presided over a partial region.
translations.idiomatic: The record shows that I, unworthy as I am, was raised to serve at court, given charge of the machinery of state, and entrusted with command of a distant quarter.

sentences.zh: 旣無德政以惠民物，又無威刑以檢不恪，至使邑違犯詔書，郡掾衞固誑迫吏民，訟訴之言，交驛道路，漸失其禮，不虔王命。

translations.literal: Having neither virtuous government to benefit the people and things, nor awe-inspiring punishments to restrain the not-reverent, to the extent of causing Yi to violate and offend the edict document, commandery aide Wei Gu deceitfully coerced clerks and people, words of litigation and complaint crossed post-stations on the roads, gradually losing their ritual, not reverent toward the king’s commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I brought neither benevolent rule to comfort the people nor stern justice to curb misconduct, with the result that Wang Yi defied an imperial edict, Wei Gu intimidated officials and commoners, petitions clogged the highways, propriety collapsed, and reverence for the throne evaporated.

sentences.zh: 今雖反悔，醜聲流聞，咎皆由繇威刑不攝。

translations.literal: Now although they have turned in repentance, ugly sound flows and is heard; the fault all comes from Yao’s awe punishments not gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Even though they have reversed course, the scandal is public knowledge, and the blame lies entirely with my failure to enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 臣又疾病，前後歷年，氣力日微，尸素重祿，曠廢職任，罪明法正。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject is also sick; front and back passing years; breath and strength daily slight; corpse-white heavy salary; vast-abandoned office duty; crime clear, law correct.
translations.idiomatic: I have moreover been ill for years; my strength fails daily while I continue to draw a generous stipend without performing my duties—a clear breach of statute.

sentences.zh: 謹按侍中守司隷校尉東武亭侯鍾繇，幸得蒙恩，以斗筲之才，仍見拔擢，顯從近密，銜命督使。

translations.literal: Respectfully: Attendant-in-ordinary acting Metropolitan Superintendent Village Marquis of Dongwu Zhong Yao, having received grace beyond his meager ability, was repeatedly promoted, kept close to the throne, and charged with supervisory missions.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Zhong Yao, attendant-in-ordinary, acting Metropolitan Superintendent, Marquis of Dongwu village, has enjoyed undeserved favor despite talents no greater than a peck measure, and has been kept close to the throne and sent forth with commissions of oversight.

sentences.zh: 明知詔書深疾長吏政教寬弱，檢下無刑，乆病淹滯，衆職荒頓，法令失張。

translations.literal: He clearly knew that edicts sternly rebuke senior officials whose rule is lax and weak, who fail to discipline subordinates or punish wrongdoing, who linger in chronic illness, leave offices idle, and let law and order go slack.
translations.idiomatic: I knew full well that recent edicts deplore lax administration, the absence of discipline among subordinates, chronic neglect of duty, offices left idle, and statutes gone slack.

sentences.zh: 邑雖違科，當必繩正法，旣舉文書，操彈失禮，至乃使邑遠詣闕廷。

translations.literal: Although Wang Yi broke the law, he should have been dealt with strictly according to statute; yet once memorials were filed, the handling of impeachment departed from proper ritual to the point that Wang Yi had to travel far to the capital on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi broke the law and should have been prosecuted in due form; instead my memorials mishandled protocol to the point of driving him to flee to the capital on his own.

sentences.zh: 隳忝使命，挫傷爪牙。

translations.literal: Thus he has disgraced the mission entrusted to him and blunted the talons and fangs of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I have disgraced the commission entrusted to me and blunted the instruments of imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 而固誑迫吏民，拒畿連月，今雖反悔，犯順失正，海內兇赫，罪一由繇威刑闇弱。

translations.literal: Yet Gu deceived and coerced clerks and commoners, resisted Ji for months; now although they have repented, they violated compliance and lost rectitude, and ill repute has spread through the realm—the fault lies entirely with Yao’s weak enforcement of awe and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei Gu intimidated officials and townsfolk and blocked Du Ji for months. Even though they have since submitted, they defied lawful authority and threw the empire into an uproar—and the blame rests squarely on my slack grip on justice.

sentences.zh: 又繇乆病，不任所職，非繇大臣當所宜爲。

translations.literal: Moreover Yao has long been ill and cannot sustain the duties of his post—this is not what a senior minister ought to do.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have been chronically ill and am no longer equal to my duties—conduct unbecoming a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 繇輕慢憲度，不畏詔令，不與國同心，爲臣不忠，無所畏忌，大爲不敬。

translations.literal: Yao treats statutes with contempt, does not fear edicts and orders, is not of one mind with the state; as a subject he is disloyal, fears and shuns nothing—greatly disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: I have treated the law with contempt, ignored imperial commands, failed to serve the public interest, shown the disloyalty of a faithless minister, and acted without restraint—gross disrespect to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又不承用詔書，奉詔不謹。

translations.literal: Also he does not receive and employ edict documents; receiving edicts he is not careful.
translations.idiomatic: I have neither implemented edicts nor carried out orders with the care they require.

sentences.zh: 又聦明蔽塞，爲下所欺，弱不勝任。

translations.literal: Also keen intelligence is blocked and stopped; he is deceived by subordinates; weak and unable to bear office.
translations.idiomatic: My judgment has been clouded, I have let subordinates deceive me, and I lack the strength to discharge my office.

sentences.zh: 數罪謹以劾，臣請法車徵詣廷尉治繇罪，大鴻臚削爵土。

translations.literal: Several crimes are respectfully impeached; your subject requests a legal cart summons to the Commandant of Justice to try Yao’s guilt, and the Grand Herald to strip rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: On these several counts I impeach myself: I ask that I be conveyed under guard to the Commandant of Justice for trial and that the Grand Herald strike my noble title and lands.

sentences.zh: 臣乆嬰篤疾，涉夏盛劇，命縣呼吸，不任部官。

translations.literal: Your subject long has been afflicted with grave illness; crossing summer it grew severe; life hangs on breath; he cannot bear departmental office.
translations.idiomatic: I have long suffered a grave malady that worsened through the summer; my life hangs by a thread, and I am unfit for any departmental post.

sentences.zh: 輙以文書付功曹從事馬適議，免冠徒跣，伏須罪誅。」

translations.literal: Therefore he hands documents to merit-clerk retainer Ma Shi for deliberation, removes cap and goes barefoot, prostrate awaiting guilt and execution."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore entrust these papers to my merit clerk, retainer Ma Shi, for consultation, lay aside cap and shoes, and await whatever sentence the court may impose."

sentences.zh: 詔不聽。〉

translations.literal: The edict did not grant it.〉
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the request.〉

sentences.zh: 自天子西遷，洛陽人民單盡，繇徙關中民，又招納亡叛以充之，數年間民戶稍實。

translations.literal: Since the Son of Heaven moved west, Luoyang’s people were utterly depleted; Yao moved people from within the passes and also recruited fugitives and rebels to fill it; within several years households gradually became substantial.
translations.idiomatic: After the court withdrew westward, Luoyang was left empty. Zhong Yao resettled families from Guanzhong, welcomed refugees and surrendered rebels, and within a few years the city’s population began to recover.

sentences.zh: 太祖征關中，得以爲資，表繇爲前軍師。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned within the passes, he was able to take this as resource; he memorialized Yao as Forward Army Strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched into Guanzhong he drew on that manpower and supplies, and he then recommended Zhong Yao as Forward Army Strategist.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，爲大理，遷相國。

translations.literal: When the Wei state was first established, Zhong Yao became Minister of Justice and was later transferred to Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei state was first established, Zhong Yao became Minister of Justice and was later transferred to Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 文帝在東宮，賜繇五熟釜，爲之銘曰：「於赫有魏，作漢藩輔。厥相惟鍾，寔幹心膂。靖恭夙夜，匪遑安處。百寮師師，楷茲度矩。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was in the Eastern Palace, he gave Yao a five-flavor cauldron and composed an inscription for it: “Glorious is Wei, serving as Han’s fence and support. Its chancellor is Zhong, truly the trunk, heart, and backbone. Reverent and respectful day and night, he has no leisure for ease. The hundred officials are orderly and disciplined, taking this as model and measure.”
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was in the Eastern Palace, he gave Yao a five-flavor cauldron and composed this inscription for it: “How glorious is Wei, serving as Han's fence and support. Its chancellor is Zhong, truly its trunk, heart, and backbone. Reverent and respectful by day and night, he has no leisure to rest. The hundred officials are orderly and disciplined, taking him as model and measure.”

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：繇爲相國，以五熟釜鼎範因太子鑄之，釜成，太子與繇書曰：「昔有黃三鼎，周之九寶，咸以一體使調一味，豈若斯釜五味時芳？

translations.literal: The Weilue says: When Yao was Chancellor, the heir apparent had the five-flavor cauldron cast from a cauldron mold. When the cauldron was completed, the heir apparent wrote to Yao, “Formerly there were the Yellow Emperor’s three tripods and Zhou’s nine treasures; all used one body to harmonize one flavor. How can they compare with this cauldron, whose five flavors are fragrant in season?
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue says: When Yao was Chancellor, the heir apparent used a tripod mold to cast a five-flavor cauldron for him. When the cauldron was completed, the heir apparent wrote to Yao, “Formerly there were the Yellow Emperor's three tripods and Zhou's nine treasures; each used a single body to harmonize a single flavor. How could they compare with this cauldron, whose five flavors are fragrant in due season?

sentences.zh: 蓋鼎之烹餁，以饗上帝，以養聖賢，昭德祈福，莫斯之美。

translations.literal: The cooking done in tripods serves to feast the Lord on High and to nourish sages and worthies; in displaying virtue and praying for blessing, nothing is more beautiful than this.
translations.idiomatic: The cooking done in tripods serves to feast the Lord on High and nourish sages and worthies; for displaying virtue and praying for blessing, nothing is more beautiful than this.

sentences.zh: 故非大人，莫之能造；故非斯器，莫宜盛德。

translations.literal: Therefore, except for a great man, none can make it; and except for this vessel, nothing is fit to contain great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, except for a great man, none can make it; and except for this vessel, nothing is fit to contain great virtue.

sentences.zh: 今之嘉釜，有逾茲美。

translations.literal: The fine cauldron of today surpasses this beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The fine cauldron of today surpasses this beauty.

sentences.zh: 夫周之尸臣，宋之考父，衞之孔悝，晉之魏顆，彼四臣者，並以功德勒名鍾鼎。

translations.literal: As for Shi Chen of Zhou, Kaofu of Song, Kong Kui of Wei, and Wei Ke of Jin, those four ministers all had their names engraved on bells and tripods because of their achievements and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As for Shi Chen of Zhou, Kaofu of Song, Kong Kui of Wei, and Wei Ke of Jin, those four ministers all had their names engraved on bells and tripods for their achievements and virtue.

sentences.zh: 今執事寅亮大魏，以隆聖化。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, respectfully assist Great Wei, thereby exalting sagely transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Now you, sir, respectfully assist Great Wei, thereby exalting sagely transformation.

sentences.zh: 堂堂之德，於斯爲盛。

translations.literal: Your grand virtue is abundant in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your grand virtue is abundant in this.

sentences.zh: 誠太常之所宜銘，彝器之所宜勒。

translations.literal: It is truly what the Grand Master of Ceremonies should inscribe and what a ritual vessel should engrave.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly what the Grand Master of Ceremonies ought to inscribe and what a ritual vessel ought to engrave.

sentences.zh: 故作斯銘，勒之釜口，庶可贊揚洪美，垂之不朽。」

translations.literal: Therefore I have made this inscription and engraved it on the mouth of the cauldron, hoping thereby to praise and proclaim vast beauty and transmit it to imperishability.”
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have made this inscription and engraved it on the mouth of the cauldron, hoping thereby to praise and proclaim its vast beauty and pass it down undying.”

sentences.zh: 臣松之按《漢書·郊祀志》，孝宣時，美陽得鼎，京兆尹張敞上議曰：「按鼎有刻書曰：『王命尸臣，宕此栒邑。尸，主事之臣也；栒音荀，幽地。賜尔鸞旂，黼黻琱戈。尸臣拜首，稽首曰，敢對揚天子，丕顯休命！』

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: According to the Treatise on Sacrifices in the Book of Han, in Emperor Xuan’s time a tripod was found at Meiyang, and Zhang Chang, governor of the capital region, submitted an opinion saying, “Examining the tripod, there is an engraved text saying: ‘The king commands Shi Chen to open this Xun settlement. Shi means a minister in charge of affairs; Xun is pronounced xun and is a secluded place. He bestows on you a simurgh banner, embroidered ornaments, and carved spears. Shi Chen bows his head, kowtows, and says, I dare to respond to and proclaim the Son of Heaven’s greatly manifest and beautiful command!’
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Songzhi notes: According to the Treatise on Sacrifices in the Book of Han, in Emperor Xuan's time a tripod was found at Meiyang, and Zhang Chang, Governor of the Capital Region, submitted an opinion saying, “Examining the tripod, there is an engraved text saying: ‘The king commands Shi Chen to open this Xun settlement. Shi means a minister in charge of affairs; Xun is pronounced xun and is a secluded place. He bestows on you a simurgh banner, embroidered ornaments, and carved spears. Shi Chen bows his head, kowtows, and says, I dare to respond to and proclaim the Son of Heaven's greatly manifest and beautiful command!’

sentences.zh: 此殆周之所以襃賜大臣子孫，大臣子孫刻銘其先功，藏之于宮廟也。」

translations.literal: This was probably how Zhou commended and rewarded the descendants of great ministers; the descendants of great ministers engraved inscriptions on the achievements of their ancestors and stored them in their ancestral temples.”
translations.idiomatic: This was probably how Zhou commended and rewarded the descendants of great ministers: those descendants engraved inscriptions recording their ancestors' achievements and stored them in their ancestral temples.”

sentences.zh: 考父銘見《左氏傳》，孔悝銘在《禮記》，事顯故不載。

translations.literal: The inscription of Kaofu appears in the Zuo Tradition, and the inscription of Kong Kui is in the Record of Rites; because the matters are well known, I do not record them.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription of Kaofu appears in the Zuo Tradition, and the inscription of Kong Kui is in the Record of Rites. Because these matters are well known, I do not record them here.

sentences.zh: 《國語》曰：「昔克潞之役，秦來圖敗晉功，魏顆以其身追秦師于輔氏，親止杜囬；其勒銘于景鍾，至于今不遺類，其子孫不可不興也。」

translations.literal: The Discourses of the States says, “Formerly, in the campaign that conquered Lu, Qin came intending to defeat Jin’s achievement. Wei Ke personally pursued the Qin army at Fushi and himself stopped Du Hui. His inscription was engraved on the Jing bell, and down to the present none of his kind has been lost; his descendants cannot fail to flourish.”
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of the States says, “Formerly, in the campaign that conquered Lu, Qin came intending to defeat Jin's achievement. Wei Ke personally pursued the Qin army at Fushi and himself stopped Du Hui. His inscription was engraved on the Jing bell, and down to the present none of his kind has disappeared; his descendants cannot fail to flourish.”

sentences.zh: 太子所稱四銘者也。

translations.literal: These are the four inscriptions cited by the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: These are the four inscriptions cited by the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：後太祖征漢中，太子在孟津，聞繇有玉玦，欲得之而難。

translations.literal: The Weilue says: Later, when Taizu campaigned against Hanzhong and the heir apparent was at Mengjin, he heard that Yao possessed a jade pendant and wanted to obtain it but found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue says: Later, when Taizu campaigned against Hanzhong and the heir apparent was at Mengjin, he heard that Yao possessed a jade pendant. He wanted to obtain it but found it difficult to ask.

sentences.zh: 公密使臨菑侯轉因人說之，繇即送之。

translations.literal: The duke secretly had the Marquis of Linzi pass through another person to speak to him, and Yao immediately sent it.
translations.idiomatic: The duke secretly had the Marquis of Linzi pass through another person to speak to him, and Yao immediately sent it.

sentences.zh: 太子與繇書曰：「夫玉以比德君子，見美詩人。

translations.literal: The heir apparent wrote to Yao, “Jade is used to compare the virtue of a gentleman and is praised by the poets.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent wrote to Yao, “Jade is used to compare the virtue of a gentleman and is praised by the poets.

sentences.zh: 晉之垂棘，魯之璵璠，宋之結綠，楚之和璞，價越萬金，貴重都城，有稱疇昔，流聲將來。

translations.literal: The pendant of Chuiji in Jin, the yufan jade of Lu, the Jielu of Song, and the uncut He jade of Chu exceeded ten thousand gold pieces in value and were prized as heavily as capitals; they were praised in the past and their fame flowed into the future.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuiji pendant of Jin, the yufan jade of Lu, the Jielu of Song, and the uncut He jade of Chu exceeded ten thousand gold pieces in value and were prized as highly as whole cities; they were praised in the past, and their fame flowed on into the future.

sentences.zh: 是以垂棘出晉，虞、虢雙禽；和璧入秦，相如抗節。

translations.literal: Thus when Chuiji left Jin, Yu and Guo were both taken; when the He jade entered Qin, Xiangru upheld his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Chuiji left Jin, Yu and Guo were both taken; when the He jade entered Qin, Xiangru upheld his integrity.

sentences.zh: 竊見玉書，稱美玉白若截肪，黑譬純漆，赤擬雞冠，黃侔蒸栗。

translations.literal: I have privately seen books on jade, which say that beautiful jade is white like cut fat, black comparable to pure lacquer, red resembling a rooster’s comb, and yellow matching steamed chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: I have privately seen books on jade, which say that beautiful jade is white like sliced fat, black like pure lacquer, red like a rooster's comb, and yellow like steamed chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 側聞斯語，未覩厥狀。

translations.literal: I had heard these words indirectly but had not seen such a form.
translations.idiomatic: I had heard these words indirectly but had not seen such a form.

sentences.zh: 雖德非君子，義無詩人，高山景行，私所慕仰。

translations.literal: Though my virtue is not that of a gentleman and my righteousness is not that of a poet, high mountains and broad roads are what I privately admire and look up to.
translations.idiomatic: Though my virtue is not that of a gentleman and my righteousness is not that of a poet, the high mountain and the broad road are what I privately admire and look up to.

sentences.zh: 然四寶邈焉以遠，秦、漢未聞有良匹。

translations.literal: Yet those four treasures are remote and distant; in Qin and Han I have not heard that there were worthy matches.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those four treasures are remote and distant; in Qin and Han I have not heard that there were worthy matches.

sentences.zh: 是以求之曠年，未遇厥真，私願不果，饑渴未副。

translations.literal: Therefore I sought one for years but did not encounter the real thing; my private wish was not fulfilled, and my hunger and thirst were not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I sought one for years but did not encounter the genuine thing; my private wish went unfulfilled, and my hunger and thirst were not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 近見南陽宗惠叔稱君侯昔有美玦，聞之驚喜，笑與抃俱。

translations.literal: Recently I saw Zong Huishu of Nanyang say that you formerly had a beautiful pendant. Hearing this, I was startled and delighted, laughing and clapping at once.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I saw Zong Huishu of Nanyang mention that you once possessed a beautiful pendant. Hearing this, I was startled and delighted, laughing and clapping at once.

sentences.zh: 當自白書，恐傳言未審，是以令舍弟子建因荀仲茂轉言鄙旨。

translations.literal: I should have written myself, but feared the transmitted report had not been verified, and therefore had my younger brother Zijian convey my humble wish through Xun Zhongmao.
translations.idiomatic: I should have written myself, but feared the transmitted report had not been verified, and therefore had my younger brother Zijian convey my humble wish by way of Xun Zhongmao.

sentences.zh: 乃不忽遺，厚見周稱，鄴騎旣到，寶玦初至，捧跪發匣，爛然滿目。

translations.literal: You did not neglect the request but showed generous and full consideration. Once the Ye courier arrived and the precious pendant first came, I knelt holding it, opened the box, and its brilliance filled my eyes.
translations.idiomatic: You did not neglect my request, but showed generous and full consideration. Once the Ye courier arrived and the precious pendant came, I knelt to receive it, opened the box, and its brilliance filled my eyes.

sentences.zh: 猥以矇鄙之姿，得觀希世之寶，不煩一介之使，不損連城之價，旣有秦昭章臺之觀，而無藺生詭奪之誑。

translations.literal: Unworthily, with my ignorant and humble bearing, I was able to view a treasure rare in the world. It did not trouble a single envoy or diminish a price worth connected cities; I had the sight that King Zhao of Qin had on the Zhang Terrace, but without Lin Xiangru’s deceptive seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthily, with my ignorant and humble bearing, I was able to view a treasure rare in the world. It did not trouble even a single envoy or diminish a price worth linked cities; I enjoyed the sight King Zhao of Qin had on the Zhang Terrace, but without Lin Xiangru's deceptive seizure.

sentences.zh: 嘉貺益腆，敢不欽承！」

translations.literal: Your fine gift is increasingly generous; how dare I not receive it with reverence!”
translations.idiomatic: Your fine gift is increasingly generous; how dare I not receive it with reverence!”

sentences.zh: 繇報書曰：「昔忝近任，并得賜玦。

translations.literal: Yao replied in a letter, “Formerly I unworthily held a close office and also received the pendant as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yao replied in a letter, “Formerly I unworthily held a close office and also received the pendant as a gift.

sentences.zh: 尚方耆老，頗識舊物。

translations.literal: The elders of the imperial workshops were rather familiar with old objects.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the imperial workshops were rather familiar with old objects.

sentences.zh: 名其符采。

translations.literal: They named its pattern and color.
translations.idiomatic: The elders identified its auspicious pattern and colors.

sentences.zh: 必得處所。

translations.literal: It surely found its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: The pendant has surely found the place where it belongs.

sentences.zh: 以爲執事有珍此者，是以鄙之，用未奉貢。

translations.literal: I thought you, sir, possessed things that treasured this, and for this reason I considered it humble and had not presented it.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you, sir, possessed things that treasured this, and for this reason I considered it humble and had not presented it.

sentences.zh: 幸而紆意，實以恱懌。

translations.literal: Fortunately you turned your attention to it, and I am truly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately you turned your attention to it, and I am truly pleased.

sentences.zh: 在昔和氏，殷勤忠篤，而繇待命，是懷愧恥。」

translations.literal: In the past, Master He was earnest, loyal, and sincere; yet Yao waited for instruction, and I harbor shame over this.”
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Master He was earnest, loyal, and sincere; yet Yao waited for instruction, and I harbor shame over this.”

sentences.zh: 數年，坐西曹掾魏諷謀反，策罷就第。

translations.literal: Several years later, because Wei Feng, an assistant in the Western Bureau, plotted rebellion, Yao was dismissed by written order and sent to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, because Wei Feng, an assistant in the Western Bureau, plotted rebellion, Yao was dismissed by written order and sent home to his residence.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：孫權稱臣，斬送關羽。

translations.literal: The Weilue says: Sun Quan declared himself a subject and beheaded Guan Yu, sending the head.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue says: Sun Quan declared himself a subject and beheaded Guan Yu, sending the head.

sentences.zh: 太子書報繇，繇荅書曰：「臣同郡故司空荀爽言：『人當道情，愛我者一何可愛！憎我者一何可憎！』顧念孫權，了更侮媚。」

translations.literal: The heir apparent wrote to inform Yao. Yao replied, “The late Minister of Works Xun Shuang from my commandery said, ‘When people follow their feelings, how lovable are those who love me! How detestable are those who hate me!’ When I think of Sun Quan, he has become all the more insulting and fawning.”
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent wrote to notify Yao. Yao replied, “The late Minister of Works Xun Shuang, who was from my commandery, said, ‘When people follow their feelings, how lovable are those who love me! How detestable are those who hate me!’ When I think of Sun Quan, he has only become more insulting and fawning.”

sentences.zh: 太子又書曰：「得報，知喜南方。

translations.literal: The heir apparent wrote again, “I received your reply and know that you rejoice over the south.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent wrote again, “I received your reply and know that you rejoice over the south.

sentences.zh: 至於荀公之清談，孫權之侮媚，執書嗢噱，不能離手。

translations.literal: As for Master Xun’s pure discourse and Sun Quan’s insulting fawning, I held the letter and laughed aloud, unable to put it down.
translations.idiomatic: As for Master Xun’s pure discourse and Sun Quan’s insulting fawning, I held the letter and laughed aloud, unable to put it down.

sentences.zh: 若權復黠，當折以汝南許邵月旦之評。

translations.literal: If Quan is again cunning, he should be checked with Xu Shao of Runan’s monthly evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: If Quan is again cunning, he should be checked with Xu Shao of Runan’s monthly evaluation.

sentences.zh: 權優游二國，俯仰荀、許，亦已足矣。」

translations.literal: For Quan to move leisurely between the two states and bow up and down to Xun and Xu is already enough.”
translations.idiomatic: For Quan to move leisurely between the two states and bow up and down to Xun and Xu is already enough.”

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，復爲大理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the royal position, Yao again became Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the royal position, Yao again became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，改爲廷尉，進封崇高鄉侯。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Yao was changed to Commandant of Justice and advanced to Marquis of Chonggao Township.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, Yao was changed to Commandant of Justice and advanced to Marquis of Chonggao Township.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉，轉封平陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Commandant and his fief was changed to Marquis of Pingyang Township.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Commandant and his fief was changed to Marquis of Pingyang Township.

sentences.zh: 時司徒華歆、司空王朗，並先世名臣。

translations.literal: At that time the Minister over the Masses Hua Xin and the Minister of Works Wang Lang were both famous ministers from earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Minister over the Masses Hua Xin and the Minister of Works Wang Lang were both famous ministers from earlier generations.

sentences.zh: 文帝罷朝，謂左右曰：「此三公者，乃一代之偉人也，後世殆難繼矣！」

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen ended court, he said to those around him, “These three dukes are great men of a generation; later ages will probably find them hard to equal!”
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen ended the court session, he said to those around him, “These three dukes are great men of a generation; later ages will probably find them hard to equal!”

sentences.zh: 陸氏《異林》曰：繇嘗數月不朝會，意性異常，或問其故，云：「常有好婦來，美麗非凡。」

translations.literal: Lu’s Grove of Marvels says: Yao once did not attend court gatherings for several months, and his temperament became abnormal. Someone asked the reason, and he said, “A beautiful woman often comes; her beauty is extraordinary.”
translations.idiomatic: Lu's Grove of Marvels says: Yao once failed to attend court gatherings for several months, and his temperament became abnormal. Someone asked the reason, and he said, “A beautiful woman often comes; her beauty is extraordinary.”

sentences.zh: 問者曰：「必是鬼物，可殺之。」

translations.literal: The questioner said, “It must be a ghostly thing; you can kill it.”
translations.idiomatic: The questioner said, “It must be a ghostly thing; you can kill it.”

sentences.zh: 婦人後往，不即前，止戶外。

translations.literal: When the woman later came, she did not immediately advance but stopped outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: When the woman later came, she did not immediately advance but stopped outside the door.

sentences.zh: 繇問何以，曰：「公有相殺意。」

translations.literal: Yao asked why, and she said, “You have the intention to kill me.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao asked why, and she said, “You have the intention to kill me.”

sentences.zh: 繇曰：「無此。」

translations.literal: Yao said, “There is no such thing.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao said, “There is no such thing.”

sentences.zh: 乃勤勤呼之，乃入。

translations.literal: He called her earnestly, and only then did she enter.
translations.idiomatic: He called her earnestly, and only then did she enter.

sentences.zh: 繇意恨，有不忍之心，然猶斫之傷髀。

translations.literal: Yao felt regret and had an unwilling heart, yet still struck her and wounded her thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Yao felt regret and had an unwilling heart, yet still struck her and wounded her thigh.

sentences.zh: 婦人即出，以新緜拭血竟路。

translations.literal: The woman immediately went out, wiping the blood with new floss all along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The woman immediately went out, wiping the blood with new floss all along the road.

sentences.zh: 明日使人尋跡之，至一大冢，木中有好婦人，形體如生人，著白練衫，丹繡裲襠，傷左髀，以裲襠中緜拭血。

translations.literal: The next day he sent someone to follow the traces. They reached a large tomb, and inside the wood was a beautiful woman whose form and body were like a living person. She wore a white silk shirt and a red embroidered liangdang; her left thigh was wounded, and she had wiped the blood with the floss inside the liangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent someone to follow the traces. They reached a large tomb, and inside the coffin was a beautiful woman whose form and body were like those of a living person. She wore a white silk shirt and a red embroidered liangdang; her left thigh was wounded, and she had wiped the blood with the floss inside the liangdang.

sentences.zh: 叔父清河太守說如此。

translations.literal: My uncle, the Administrator of Qinghe, told the story in this way.
translations.idiomatic: My uncle, the Administrator of Qinghe, told the story in this way.

sentences.zh: 清河，陸雲也。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Qinghe was Lu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Qinghe was Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封定陵侯，增邑五百，并前千八百戶，遷太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Yao was advanced to Marquis of Dingling, his fief was increased by five hundred households, for a total of eighteen hundred households, and he was transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Yao was advanced to Marquis of Dingling. His fief was increased by five hundred households, making eighteen hundred households in all, and he was transferred to the post of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 繇有膝疾，拜起不便。

translations.literal: Yao had an illness of the knees, making it inconvenient for him to bow and rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yao had an illness of the knees, making it inconvenient for him to bow and rise.

sentences.zh: 時華歆亦以高年疾病，朝見皆使載輿車，虎賁舁上殿就坐。

translations.literal: At that time Hua Xin also, because of advanced age and illness, was made to ride in a carriage whenever he attended court, and Tiger Guards carried him up into the hall to sit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hua Xin too, because of advanced age and illness, was allowed to ride in a carriage whenever he attended court, and Tiger Guards carried him up into the hall to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 是後三公有疾，遂以爲故事。

translations.literal: After this, when the Three Dukes were ill, this became the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After this, when the Three Dukes were ill, this became the precedent.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖下令，使平議死刑可宮割者。

translations.literal: At first the Grand Progenitor issued an order, causing fair discussion of those sentenced to death who could be castrated or cut.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his rise Cao Cao ordered a review of capital cases to consider whether castration or mutilation might replace execution.

sentences.zh: 繇以爲「古之肉刑，更歷聖人，宜復施行，以代死刑。」

translations.literal: Yao thought, “The mutilating punishments of antiquity, passed through sagely men, ought to be restored and applied, to replace death punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Yao thought, “The mutilating punishments of antiquity, passed through sagely men, ought to be restored and applied, to replace death punishment."

sentences.zh: 議者以爲非恱民之道，遂寢。

translations.literal: Discussers thought it was not the way to please the people; thereupon it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters held that this would not win the people’s hearts, and the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 及文帝臨饗群臣，詔謂「大理欲復肉刑，此誠聖王之法。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen faced the feasting host of ministers, an edict said, “The Court of Justice wishes to restore mutilating punishments—this is truly the law of sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen presided over a feast for the assembled ministers, an edict said, “The Court of Justice wishes to restore mutilating punishments; this is truly the law of sage kings.

sentences.zh: 公卿當善共議。」

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers ought well jointly to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers were to deliberate together in good faith."

sentences.zh: 議未定，會有軍事，復寢。

translations.literal: Discussion was not settled; there happened to be military affairs; again it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could reach a conclusion, military emergencies intervened and the matter lapsed once more.

sentences.zh: 太和中，繇上疏曰：「大魏受命，繼蹤虞、夏。

translations.literal: In the Taihe years, Yao submitted a memorial saying, “Great Wei has received the mandate, following the traces of Yu and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era Zhong Yao memorialized the throne: “Great Wei has received Heaven’s mandate in succession to the legendary rulers Yu and Xia.

sentences.zh: 孝文革法，不合古道。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao changed the laws; they did not accord with the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han’s legal reforms departed from the ancient norm.

sentences.zh: 先帝聖德，固天所縱，墳典之業，一以貫之。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor’s sagely virtue was indeed what Heaven released; the enterprise of tomb-text classics he threaded through with one.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor’s sagely virtue was Heaven’s own gift, and he pursued the classical legacy with a single, consistent purpose.

sentences.zh: 是以繼世，仍發明詔，思復古刑，爲一代法。

translations.literal: Therefore succeeding generations repeatedly issued clear edicts, thinking to restore ancient punishments, to make a generation’s law.
translations.idiomatic: His successors therefore issued repeated edicts aiming to restore the old punishments and set a lasting standard for the age.

sentences.zh: 連有軍事，遂未施行。

translations.literal: Continuously there were military affairs; therefore it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare followed warfare, however, and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 陛下遠追二祖遺意，惜斬趾可以禁惡，恨入死之無辜，使明習律令，與群臣共議。

translations.literal: Your Majesty far pursues the two ancestors’ leftover intent, pitying that cutting toes can forbid evil, hating that entering death is innocent, causing clarity in statutes and ordinances, jointly to discuss with the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now carries forward the intent of your two imperial forebears: you regret that amputation could deter crime while execution sweeps away the guiltless, and you have ordered those versed in the code to debate the matter with the full court.

sentences.zh: 出本當右趾而入大辟者，復行此刑。

translations.literal: Those who originally ought to have had the right toe but entered great execution, again apply this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who would once have faced amputation of the right foot but are now liable to execution should again receive the lesser corporal penalty.

sentences.zh: 書云：『皇帝清問下民，鰥寡有辭于苗。』

translations.literal: The Document says: ‘The emperor clearly asked the lower people; widowers and widows had words regarding the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Documents says: ‘The emperor sought the truth from the common people, and even widowers and widows brought their grievances against the Miao.

sentences.zh: 此言堯當除蚩尤、有苗之刑，先審問於下民之有辭者也。

translations.literal: This speaks of Yao’s time removing Chiyou and the You-Miao punishments, first examining and asking among the lower people who had words.
translations.idiomatic: That passage shows how Yao abolished the cruel punishments of Chiyou and the Miao only after he had heard out the people’s complaints.

sentences.zh: 若今蔽獄之時，訊問三槐、九棘、群吏、萬民，使如孝景之令，其當棄巿，欲斬右趾者許之。

translations.literal: If at the time of covered trials one examines and asks the three sophoras, nine jujubes, host of clerks, and myriad people, making it like Emperor Xiaojing’s order—those who ought to be cast aside in the market, wishing to cut the right toe, permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When cases are tried in camera, consult the judges of the three sophoras and nine jujubes, the officials, and the people at large, as Emperor Jing of Han once commanded: allow substitution of right-foot amputation for execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 其黥、劓、左趾、宮刑者，自如孝文，易以髠、笞。

translations.literal: As for those with branding, nose-cutting, left toe, and palace punishment, as of themselves like Emperor Xiaowen, exchange for shaving and beating.
translations.idiomatic: For branding, nose removal, left-foot amputation, and castration, follow Emperor Wen of Han’s precedent and commute the sentence to shaving and flogging.

sentences.zh: 能有姦者，率年二十至四五十，雖斬其足，猶任生育。

translations.literal: Those able to have wickedness, generally age twenty to forty or fifty—even if cutting their foot, still they can bear and produce.
translations.idiomatic: Most criminals fall between twenty and fifty; even after losing a foot they can still marry and raise children.

sentences.zh: 今天下人少於孝文之世，下計所全，歲三千人。

translations.literal: Now the realm’s people are fewer than in Emperor Xiaowen’s age; by lower reckoning what is preserved, yearly three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The empire today is less populous than in Emperor Wen’s day; by a conservative estimate this policy would spare three thousand lives every year.

sentences.zh: 張蒼除肉刑，所殺歲以萬計。

translations.literal: Zhang Cang removed mutilating punishments; those killed yearly were reckoned by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Cang abolished corporal punishment, executions ran to tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 臣欲復肉刑，歲生三千人。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to restore mutilating punishments; yearly three thousand persons will live.
translations.idiomatic: If corporal punishment were restored, three thousand lives would be spared annually.

sentences.zh: 子貢問能濟民可謂仁乎？

translations.literal: Zi Gong asked, able to succor the people—may it be called benevolence?
translations.idiomatic: Zi Gong asked whether the power to rescue the people could be called true benevolence.

sentences.zh: 子曰：『何事於仁，必也聖乎，堯、舜其猶病諸！』

translations.literal: The Master said, ‘What affair is this regarding benevolence—must it be sageliness? Yao and Shun perhaps still were troubled by it!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius replied, ‘That is more than benevolence—it is the work of a sage; even Yao and Shun found it hard to achieve!

sentences.zh: 又曰：『仁遠乎哉？

translations.literal: Also he said, ‘Is benevolence far?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, ‘Is benevolence really so distant?

sentences.zh: 我欲仁，斯仁至矣。』

translations.literal: I desire benevolence, and this benevolence arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Desire it, and benevolence is at hand.

sentences.zh: 若誠行之，斯民永濟。」

translations.literal: If truly practicing it, these people will forever be succored."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty earnestly puts this into practice, the people will enjoy lasting relief."

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔曰：「太傅學優才高，留心政事，又於刑理深遠。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict said, “The Grand Tutor’s learning is excellent and talent high; he attends to government affairs; moreover in punishments and principle he is profound and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict declared: “The Grand Tutor is learned and able, attentive to statecraft, and deeply versed in penal theory.

sentences.zh: 此大事，公卿羣寮善共平議。」

translations.literal: This is a great matter; dukes, ministers, and host of officials ought well jointly to discuss fairly."
translations.idiomatic: This is a weighty question; let the high ministers and all officials deliberate together in good faith."

sentences.zh: 司徒王朗議，以爲「繇欲輕減大辟之條，以增益刖刑之數，此即起偃爲豎，化屍爲人矣。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Lang debated, thinking, “Yao wishes lightly to reduce the articles of great execution, thereby increasing the number of foot-severing punishments—this is raising the fallen to stand, transforming corpses into persons.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Wang Lang objected: “Zhong Yao would ease the statutes on capital crimes only to multiply sentences of foot amputation—that is like raising the dead to walk again.

sentences.zh: 然臣之愚，猶有未合微異之意。

translations.literal: Yet your subject’s stupidity still has not-yet-concordant slightly different intent.
translations.idiomatic: For my own part, humble as I am, I still harbor a few reservations.

sentences.zh: 夫五刑之屬，著在科律，自有減死一等之法，不死即爲減。

translations.literal: As for the categories of the five punishments, they are set out in statutes and ordinances; of themselves there is the law of reducing death by one grade—not dying is then reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The five punishments are already codified, including commutation one degree short of death; any sentence that stops short of execution is such a reduction.

sentences.zh: 施行已乆，不待遠假斧鑿於彼肉刑，然後有罪次也。

translations.literal: Application has already been long; one need not wait to borrow far axe and chisel on those mutilating punishments, and only then have guilty gradation.
translations.idiomatic: These rules have been in force for ages; we need not reach back to corporal mutilation to establish a proper scale of penalties.

sentences.zh: 前世仁者，不忍肉刑之慘酷，是以廢而不用。

translations.literal: Benevolent men of former ages could not bear the cruel severity of mutilating punishments; therefore they abolished and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Humane rulers of earlier times abolished corporal punishment because they could not stomach its cruelty.

sentences.zh: 不用已來，歷年數百。

translations.literal: Since not using them, years passed number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: We have done without it for centuries.

sentences.zh: 今復行之，恐所減之文未彰於萬民之目，而肉刑之問已宣於寇讎之耳，非所以來遠人也。

translations.literal: Now if again applying them, I fear the text of what is reduced will not be manifest to the myriad people’s eyes, while the report of mutilating punishments will already be proclaimed in bandit-enemies’ ears—not the means by which to draw distant people.
translations.idiomatic: To revive it now would fail to advertise leniency to our own subjects while advertising barbarity to enemy states—hardly the way to win distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 今可按繇所欲輕之死罪，使減死之髠、刖。

translations.literal: Now one may press on the death crimes Yao wishes to lighten, causing shaving and foot-severing that reduce death.
translations.idiomatic: We might instead take the capital offenses Zhong Yao would lighten and commute them to shaving or amputation short of death.

sentences.zh: 嫌其輕者，可倍其居作之歲數。

translations.literal: If disliking their lightness, one may double the years of their dwelling labor.
translations.idiomatic: Where the penalty still seems too mild, double the term of hard labor.

sentences.zh: 內有以生易死不訾之恩，外無以刖易釱駭耳之聲。」

translations.literal: Within there is the grace of exchanging life for death without reckoning; without there is no sound of exchanging foot-severing for cangue to startle ears."
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm men would receive the incalculable boon of life forfeit for death; abroad there would be none of the shock that comes from trading the cangue for the axe."

sentences.zh: 議者百餘人，與朗同者多。

translations.literal: Discussers were more than a hundred; those who agreed with Lang were many.
translations.idiomatic: Of the more than a hundred debaters, most sided with Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 帝以吳、蜀未平，且寢。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Wu and Shu were not yet pacified, for the time being shelved it.
