translations.idiomatic: Because Wu and Shu were still unconquered, the emperor let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏曰：夫民心樂全而不能常全，蓋利用之物懸於外，而嗜慾之情動於內也。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong said: As for the people’s hearts delighting in wholeness yet unable constantly to be whole—this is because things of profit and use hang outside, while the feelings of craving desire move within.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yuan Hong observed: People long for integrity yet rarely keep it, because profit tempts them from without and appetite stirs them from within.

sentences.zh: 於是有進取貪競之行，希求放肆之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon there is conduct of advancing and seizing, greedy competition; hoping and seeking for unrestrained affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence arise grasping ambition, ruthless rivalry, and the pursuit of unrestrained excess.

sentences.zh: 進取不已，不能充其嗜慾，則苟且儌倖之所生也；

translations.literal: Advancing and seizing without cease, unable to fill their craving desires—then what is born is recklessness and lucky chance;
translations.idiomatic: When ambition knows no limit yet desire remains unsatisfied, men turn to corner-cutting and desperate gambles;

sentences.zh: 希求無饜，無以愜其慾，則姦僞忿怒之所興也。

translations.literal: Hoping and seeking without satiety, nothing with which to satisfy their desires—then what rises is treacherous deceit and angry rage.
translations.idiomatic: when hope is insatiable and nothing slakes the appetite, fraud and fury follow.

sentences.zh: 先王知其如此，而欲救其弊，或先德化以陶其心；

translations.literal: Former kings knew it was thus and wished to save its ills; some first used virtuous transformation to mold their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings, seeing this, sought remedies: some began by molding the people through moral instruction;

sentences.zh: 其心不化，然後加以刑辟。

translations.literal: if their hearts did not transform, afterward applied punishments and execution to them.
translations.idiomatic: when hearts proved incorrigible, they added penal sanctions.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「百姓不親，五品不遜。

translations.literal: The Document says: “The hundred surnames are not close; the five grades are not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The Document says: “The hundred surnames are not close; the five grades are not compliant.

sentences.zh: 汝作司徒而敬敷五教。

translations.literal: You act as Minister of Education and respectfully spread the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: You shall be Minister of Education and reverently spread the five moral duties.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷猾夏，寇賊姦宄。

translations.literal: Barbarians trouble the Xia; bandits and thieves are treacherous villains.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes harass the heartland; robbers and traitors work their malice.

sentences.zh: 汝作士，五刑有服。」

translations.literal: You act as Minister of Crime; the five punishments have submission."
translations.idiomatic: You shall be Minister of Justice so that the five punishments are properly applied."

sentences.zh: 然則德、刑之設，參而用之者也。

translations.literal: Thus then virtue and punishment’s establishment—intertwined and using them is the way.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue and punishment are therefore meant to be woven together and applied in concert.

sentences.zh: 三代相因，其義詳焉。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties inherited one from another; its meaning is detailed therein.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties handed down this doctrine in full detail.

sentences.zh: 周禮：「使墨者守門，劓者守關，宮者守內，刖者守囿。」

translations.literal: Zhou Rites: “Make the branded guard gates, the nose-cut guard passes, the castrated guard the inner precincts, the foot-severed guard the preserves."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou says: “Make the branded guard the gates, the nose-cut guard the passes, the castrated guard the inner precincts, and the foot-severed guard the preserves."

sentences.zh: 此肉刑之制可得而論者也。

translations.literal: This is what of the mutilating punishments’ system can be obtained and discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the classical scheme of corporal punishment that scholars may still discuss.

sentences.zh: 荀卿亦云，殺人者死，傷人者刑，百王之所同，未有知其所由來者也。

translations.literal: Xun Qing also said, killers die, wounders suffer punishment—the hundred kings agree on this; none knows whence it came.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi likewise taught that murderers die and assailants are punished—a principle every dynasty has shared, though none can say where it began.

sentences.zh: 夫殺人者死，而相殺者不已，是大辟可以懲未殺，不能使天下無殺也。

translations.literal: As for killers dying, yet mutual killing does not cease—this is that great execution can punish not-yet-killing, but cannot cause the realm to have no killing.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment deters men who have not yet killed, yet it cannot stop killing altogether.

sentences.zh: 傷人者刑，而害物者不息，是黥、劓可以懼未刑，不能使天下無刑也。

translations.literal: As for wounders suffering punishment, yet harmers of things do not rest—this is that branding and nose-cutting can frighten not-yet-punishment, but cannot cause the realm to have no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal penalties may frighten offenders who have not yet been punished, but they cannot remove crime from the world.

sentences.zh: 故將欲止之，莫若先以德化。

translations.literal: Therefore if wishing to stop it, nothing compares to first using virtuous transformation.
translations.idiomatic: To end wrongdoing, nothing matches moral transformation applied first.

sentences.zh: 夫罪過彰著，然後入于刑辟，是將殺人者不必死，欲傷人者不必刑。

translations.literal: As for guilt and fault shining clear, afterward entering into punishments and execution—this is that those about to kill need not die, those wishing to wound need not suffer punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only when guilt is plain should the law intervene—so that men on the verge of murder need not die and men tempted to wound need not be mutilated.

sentences.zh: 縱而弗化，則陷於刑辟。

translations.literal: If indulged and not transformed, then they sink into punishments and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resist reform must then fall under the law’s edge.

sentences.zh: 故刑之所制，在於不可移之地。

translations.literal: Therefore what punishments regulate lies in the place that cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law should therefore strike only when guilt is beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 禮教則不然，明其善惡，所以潛勸其情，消之於未殺也；

translations.literal: Rites instruction is not thus; clarifying their good and evil is the means secretly to urge their feelings, dispelling it before killing;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and instruction work differently: by clarifying right and wrong they quietly guide the passions and dissolve murderous intent before it forms;

sentences.zh: 示之恥辱，所以內愧其心，治之於未傷也。

translations.literal: showing them shame and humiliation is the means inwardly to shame their hearts, ordering it before wounding.
translations.idiomatic: by exposing men to shame they are moved to inward remorse and cured before they do harm.

sentences.zh: 故過微而不至於著，罪薄而不及於刑。

translations.literal: Therefore faults are slight and do not reach to being manifest; crimes are thin and do not reach to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Minor faults never ripen into notorious crimes, and light offenses never reach the executioner.

sentences.zh: 終入罪辟者，非教化之所得也，故雖殘一物之生，刑一人之體，是除天下之害，夫何傷哉！

translations.literal: Those who in the end enter guilt and execution are not what transformation and instruction can obtain; therefore although mutilating one thing’s life, punishing one person’s body—this is removing the realm’s harm—what wound is there!
translations.idiomatic: Those who still end on the scaffold lie beyond the reach of instruction; to take one life or mutilate one body in order to rid the empire of a scourge is no real injury to humanity.

sentences.zh: 率斯道也，風化可以漸淳，刑罰可以漸少，其理然也。

translations.literal: Following this way, customs and transformation can gradually become pure; punishments and fines can gradually become few—its pattern is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue this path and customs will slowly improve while penalties grow ever rarer—that is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 苟不能化其心，而專任刑罰，民失義方，動罹刑網，求世休和，焉可得哉？

translations.literal: If unable to transform their hearts, yet solely trusting punishments and fines, the people lose the square of righteousness, movingly fall into the punishment net—seeking age peace and harmony, how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If you ignore moral suasion and rely on punishments alone, the people lose their moral bearings, tumble into the law’s snares, and peace can never be won.

sentences.zh: 周之成、康，豈按三千之文而致刑錯之美乎？

translations.literal: Zhou’s Cheng and Kang—did they press the three thousand texts to bring about the beauty of punishments set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Did the golden age of Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou rest on enforcing three thousand statutes, or on the rarity of executions?

sentences.zh: 蓋德化漸漬，致斯有由也。

translations.literal: This is because virtuous transformation gradually soaked; achieving this had a cause.
translations.idiomatic: Their success came from gradual moral transformation, not from multiplying written laws.

sentences.zh: 漢初懲酷刑之弊，務寬厚之論，公卿大夫，相與恥言人過。

translations.literal: At Han’s beginning they took warning from harsh punishments’ ills, strove for lenient-thick discourse; dukes, ministers, and grandees together were ashamed to speak of others’ faults.
translations.idiomatic: The early Han, reacting against Qin cruelty, cultivated a climate of tolerance in which high officials hesitated even to mention one another’s faults.

sentences.zh: 文帝登朝，加以玄默。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ascended the court, adding to it dark silence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne he deepened that reticent, understated style of government.

sentences.zh: 張武受賂，賜金以愧其心；

translations.literal: Zhang Wu received bribes; he was given gold to shame his heart;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Wu accepted bribes, yet the emperor gave him gold to prick his conscience rather than haul him into court;

sentences.zh: 吳王不朝，崇禮以訓其失。

translations.literal: the King of Wu did not attend court; he was honored with rites to instruct his fault.
translations.idiomatic: when the king of Wu failed to appear at court, the throne answered with heightened courtesy to correct his lapse.

sentences.zh: 是以吏民樂業，風流篤厚，斷獄四百，幾致刑錯，豈非德刑兼用已然之効哉？

translations.literal: Therefore clerks and people rejoiced in their occupations; customs flowed and were deep and thick; cases judged were four hundred—almost bringing punishments set aside—is this not the already manifest effect of virtue and punishment jointly used?
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners prospered, manners grew generous, and the annual caseload fell to some four hundred suits—nearly the ideal of unused punishments. Was that not the fruit of blending moral example with the law?

sentences.zh: 世之欲言刑罰之用，不先德教之益，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: Those in the age who wish to speak of punishments’ and fines’ use, not putting first virtuous instruction’s benefit—miss far.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who discusses penalties without first praising moral instruction has missed the point entirely.

sentences.zh: 今大辟之罪，與古同制。

translations.literal: Now great execution’s crimes are with antiquity same system.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes today follow the same categories as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 免死已下，不過五歲，旣釋鉗鎖，復得齒于人倫。

translations.literal: Below spared death, not passing five years; having released fetters and cangues, again they are ranked in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser offenders serve no more than five years, then shed their shackles and re-enter society as full members.

sentences.zh: 是以民無恥惡，數爲姦盜，故刑徒多而亂不治也。

translations.literal: Therefore the people have no shame in evil; repeatedly they commit treachery and theft; therefore punishment convicts are many and disorder is not ordered.
translations.idiomatic: People therefore feel no shame in wrongdoing, theft flourishes, the prisons fill, and chaos spreads unchecked.

sentences.zh: 苟教之所去，罰當其罪，一離刀鋸，沒身不齒，鄰里且猶恥之，而況于鄉黨乎？

translations.literal: If where instruction goes, punishment matches their crime, once parted from knife and saw, to the end of life not ranked—even neighbors still shame them, how much more village and community?
translations.idiomatic: If instruction were upheld and penalties matched each crime, a single session with the executioner’s tools would brand a man for life: his neighbors would shun him, to say nothing of the wider community.

sentences.zh: 而況朝廷乎？

translations.literal: How much more the court and capital?
translations.idiomatic: What then of acceptance at court?

sentences.zh: 如此，則夙沙、趙高之儔，無施其惡矣。

translations.literal: If thus, then for the sort of Susa and Zhao Gao there is nowhere to apply their evil.
translations.idiomatic: In such a world men of the stripe of Susa and Zhao Gao would have no opening for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 古者察其言，觀其行，而善惡彰焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity they examined their words, observed their conduct, and good and evil were manifest therein.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients judged men by word and deed, so merit and guilt stood plain.

sentences.zh: 然則君子之去刑辟，固已遠矣。

translations.literal: Thus then the gentleman’s distance from punishments and execution was indeed already far.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gentleman kept the headsman’s block at a great remove.

sentences.zh: 過誤不幸，則八議之所宥也。

translations.literal: Fault through error and misfortune—then what the eight deliberations forgives.
translations.idiomatic: Unlucky mistakes fall under the eight grounds for clemency.

sentences.zh: 若夫卞和、史遷之冤，淫刑之所及也。

translations.literal: As for Bian He and Shi Qian’s wrongs—what licentious punishments reached.
translations.idiomatic: The wrongs done to Bian He and Sima Qian were the work of arbitrary cruelty.

sentences.zh: 苟失其道，或不免于大辟，而況肉刑哉！

translations.literal: If losing this way, perhaps not avoiding great execution—how much more mutilating punishments!
translations.idiomatic: When justice miscarries, innocents still face the headsman—how much worse under corporal punishment!

sentences.zh: 漢書：「斬右趾及殺人先自言告，吏坐受賕，守官物而即盜之，皆棄巿。」

translations.literal: Book of Han: ‘Those liable to right-toe amputation and killers who first confess on their own, clerks convicted of taking bribes, and custodians who steal the goods they guard—all are cast aside in the market.’
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu says: "Those sentenced to right-foot amputation, killers who first confess, officials convicted of accepting bribes, and those who guard official goods and then steal them are all exposed in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 此班固所謂當生而令死者也。

translations.literal: This is what Ban Gu called those who ought to live yet were ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: That is what Ban Gu meant by condemning men who deserved to live to die nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 今不忍刻截之慘，而安勦絕之悲，此最治體之所先，有國所宜改者也。〉

translations.literal: Now not bearing carving-cutting’s cruelty, yet settling on extirpation-cutting’s grief—this is what governing substance puts first; what a state possessing ought to change.〉
translations.idiomatic: To shrink from the horror of mutilation yet accept the tragedy of mass execution is precisely the contradiction sound government must resolve; it is a reform any true state should embrace.〉

sentences.zh: 太和四年，繇薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, Yao died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao died in the fourth year of the Taihe era (230).

sentences.zh: 帝素服臨弔，謚曰成侯。

translations.literal: The Emperor in plain garb went to mourn; posthumous title was Marquis Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended in mourning dress and posthumously ennobled him as Marquis Cheng.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：有司議謚，以爲繇昔爲廷尉，辨理刑獄，決嫌明疑，民無怨者，由于、張之在漢也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Book states: the offices deliberated posthumous title, holding that Yao in the past as Commandant of Justice distinguished and ordered punishments and prisons, decided suspicion and clarified doubt, and the people had none who resented—this was like Yu and Zhang’s being in Han.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu records that the ministry proposed a posthumous name on the ground that Zhong Yao, as Commandant of Justice, had settled doubtful cases so fairly that no one bore a grudge—comparable to Yu Dingguo and Zhang Tang under the Han.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太傅功高德茂，位爲師保，論行賜謚，常先依此，兼叙廷尉于、張之德耳。」

translations.literal: An edict said: “The Grand Tutor’s merit is high and virtue luxuriant; his rank is tutor and protector; discussing conduct and granting posthumous title, always first rely on this, also narrating the Commandant of Justice Yu and Zhang’s virtue."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: “The Grand Tutor’s achievements and character are outstanding, and he served as imperial preceptor. When assigning a posthumous name we should begin from that, and only secondarily note his excellence in the mold of Yu and Zhang of the Han Commandery of Justice."

sentences.zh: 乃策謚曰成侯。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon by document posthumous title was Marquis Cheng.〉
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore canonized him as Marquis Cheng.〉

sentences.zh: 子毓嗣。

translations.literal: Son Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong Yu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝分毓戶邑，封繇弟演及子劭、孫豫列侯。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wen divided Yu’s registered households and fiefs, enfeoffing Yao’s younger brother Yan and son Shao and grandson Yu as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Wen had carved out part of Zhong Yu’s registered households and tax lands to enfeoff Zhong Yao’s brother Yan, his son Shao, and his grandson Yu as marquises.

sentences.zh: 毓字稚叔。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zhishu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu’s courtesy name was Zhishu.

sentences.zh: 年十四爲散騎侍郎，機捷談笑，有父風。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was gentleman cavalier attendant; nimble in talk and laughter, he had his father’s air.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he became a gentleman cavalier attendant—quick-witted and easy in conversation, very much in his father’s mold.

sentences.zh: 太和初，蜀相諸葛亮圍祁山，明帝欲西征，毓上疏曰：「夫策貴廟勝，功尚帷幄，不下殿堂之上，而決勝千里之外。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Shu Chancellor Zhuge Liang besieged Qishan; Emperor Ming wished to campaign west; Yu submitted a memorial saying, “As for strategy, temple victory is prized; as for merit, the tent curtain is honored—not descending from above the hall dais, yet deciding victory beyond a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era, when Zhuge Liang of Shu besieged Qishan and Emperor Ming planned a western expedition, Zhong Yu memorialized: “The best strategy wins in the council chamber; the highest merit belongs to those who plan behind the screen—victory may be fixed a thousand li away without the ruler’s ever leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 車駕宜鎮守中土，以爲四方威勢之援。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage ought to guard and hold the central lands, to be aid to awe-inspiring force in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train should hold the central plain firm and serve as the anchor of authority for every quarter.

sentences.zh: 今大軍西征，雖有百倍之威，於關中之費，所損非一。

translations.literal: Now the great army campaigns west; although there is a hundredfold’s awe, as for expense within the passes, what is lost is not one thing.
translations.idiomatic: A western expedition would multiply the army’s apparent might, yet the drain on Guanzhong would be incalculable.

sentences.zh: 且盛暑行師，詩人所重，實非至尊動軔之時也。」

translations.literal: Moreover in sweltering summer moving troops is what the Odes’ people stress; in truth it is not the time for the Most Honored to set wheel-ruts in motion."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the classics warn against marching in the dog days of summer; this is no season for the Son of Heaven to take the field."

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 時大興洛陽宮室，車駕便幸許昌，天下當朝正許昌。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang palace buildings were greatly raised; the imperial carriage then favored Xuchang; the realm was to hold New Year court at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The court was rebuilding the Luoyang palaces, so the emperor moved to Xuchang and the New Year audience was held there instead.

sentences.zh: 許昌偪狹，於城南以氊爲殿，備設魚龍曼延，民罷勞役。

translations.literal: Xuchang was cramped and narrow; south of the city they made a hall of felt, fully setting out fish-dragon spreading displays; the people were exhausted by labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang was cramped, so south of the city they threw up a felt hall and staged lavish spectacles, wearing the people out with corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 毓諫，以爲「水旱不時，帑藏空虛，凡此之類，可須豐年。」

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated, holding that “flood and drought do not come at the proper times; the treasuries are empty; matters of this sort may wait for a bumper year."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu remonstrated: “Floods and droughts come out of season, the treasury is bare—such extravagances should wait for years of plenty."

sentences.zh: 又上「宜復關內開荒地，使民肆力於農。」

translations.literal: He also submitted that “one ought to reopen wasteland within the passes and let the people exert their strength on farming."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted that “one ought to reopen wasteland within the passes and let the people exert their strength on farming."

sentences.zh: 事遂施行。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 正始中，爲散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi years he was regular attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he became a regular attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽盛夏興軍伐蜀，蜀拒守，軍不得進。

translations.literal: Grand General Cao Shuang in the height of summer raised troops to attack Shu; Shu defended and held; the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Cao Shuang launched a midsummer offensive against Shu, but the enemy held firm and his army stalled.

sentences.zh: 爽方欲增兵，毓與書曰：「竊以爲廟勝之策，不臨矢石；

translations.literal: Shuang was about to wish to increase troops; Yu wrote him a letter saying, “Your humble servant thinks the temple-victory plan does not face arrows and stones;
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang planned to reinforce the campaign, Zhong Yu wrote: “True strategic victory is won without exposing men to arrow and stone;

sentences.zh: 王者之兵，有征無戰。

translations.literal: the king’s host has expeditions but no battles.
translations.idiomatic: a king’s army should overawe foes into submission without needing to fight.

sentences.zh: 誠以干戚可以服有苗，退舍足以納原寇，不必縱吳漢於江關，騁韓信於井陘也。

translations.literal: Truly with shield and axe-helve one can subdue the You-Miao; withdrawing the camp is enough to admit Yuan’s bandits—one need not unleash Wu Han at the river passes nor gallop Han Xin through Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients subdued the Miao with ritual dance, and King Tang won over outlaws by pulling back his lines—there is no need to imitate Wu Han forcing the Yangzi gorges or Han Xin charging through Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 見可而進，知難而退，蓋自古之政。

translations.literal: See what may be done and advance; know what is hard and withdraw—this is government from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Advance when the odds favor you, withdraw when they do not—that has been sound policy since high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 惟公侯詳之！」

translations.literal: Only, my lord, examine it carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, General, to weigh this with care."

sentences.zh: 爽無功而還。

translations.literal: Shuang had no merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang withdrew without having accomplished anything.

sentences.zh: 後以失爽意，徙侍中，出爲魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Later because he lost Shuang’s favor, he was shifted to attendant-in-ordinary and sent out as grand administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, having fallen from Cao Shuang’s favor, he was moved to attendant-in-ordinary and posted out as governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 爽旣誅，入爲御史中丞、侍中廷尉。

translations.literal: After Shuang was executed, he entered as palace assistant secretary and attendant-in-ordinary commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Shuang’s execution he returned to court as palace assistant secretary and as attendant-in-ordinary concurrent commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 聽君父已沒，臣子得爲理謗，及士爲侯，其妻不復配嫁，毓所創也。

translations.literal: It was Yu who originated the rule that when lord and father are already dead, a subject may pursue a lawsuit over slander, and that when a scholar becomes a full marquis his wife may not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced the statutes allowing heirs to sue for libel after a father’s death and forbidding a marquis’s widow to remarry.

sentences.zh: 正元中，毌丘儉、文欽反，毓持節至揚、豫州班行赦令，告諭士民，還爲尚書。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan years, when Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled, Yu bearing credentials went to Yang and Yu provinces to promulgate amnesty edicts and instruct officials and commoners; he returned as minister.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengyuan uprising of Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin he carried credentials through Yang and Yu to proclaim amnesties and reassure the populace, then resumed his post as minister.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕反，大將軍司馬文王議自詣壽春討誕。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan rebelled, Grand General Sima Wenwang deliberated going in person to Shouchun to punish Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan rose in revolt, Grand General Sima Zhao debated leading the host in person against Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 會吳大將孫壹率衆降，或以爲「吳新有釁，必不能復出軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu’s great general Sun Yi led a host to surrender; some thought, “Wu has newly had a rift; they surely cannot again send out an army.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Wu's great general Sun Yi led a host to surrender; some thought, “Wu has recently suffered a rupture, so they surely cannot send out an army again.

sentences.zh: 東兵已多，可須後問」。

translations.literal: Eastern troops are already many; one may await later inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: We already have ample forces in the east; we can afford to wait and see.”

sentences.zh: 毓以爲「夫論事料敵，當以己度人。

translations.literal: Yu thought that “when discussing affairs and sizing up the enemy, one ought to measure others by oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu replied that “in judging the enemy you must put yourself in his place.

sentences.zh: 今誕舉淮南之地以與吳國，孫壹所率，口不至千，兵不過三百。

translations.literal: Now Dan has raised the lands of Huainan to give to Wu; what Sun Yi led numbered not a thousand mouths and not three hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan has pledged Huainan to Wu, yet Sun Yi brought fewer than a thousand civilians and three hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 吳之所失，蓋爲無幾。

translations.literal: What Wu has lost is in sum not much.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s actual loss is trifling.

sentences.zh: 若壽春之圍未解，而吳國之內轉安，未可必其不出也。」

translations.literal: If the siege of Shouchun is not yet lifted while Wu’s interior turns secure, one cannot be certain that they will not send troops."
translations.idiomatic: If Shouchun remains invested while Wu settles her own house, we cannot assume she will stay idle."

sentences.zh: 大將軍曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Grand General said, “Good."
translations.idiomatic: The grand general said, “Well said."

sentences.zh: 遂將毓行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Yu along.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took Zhong Yu with him on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲諸葛誕舉淮南以與吳，孫壹率三百人以歸魏，謂吳有釁，本非有理之言。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi thinks that Zhuge Dan raised Huainan to give to Wu and Sun Yi led three hundred men to submit to Wei—yet to say Wu had a rift was from the start not reasonable speech.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks: Zhuge Dan offered Huainan to Wu while Sun Yi brought only three hundred men to Wei—calling that proof of Wu’s collapse was never sound logic, and Zhong Yu’s inference from it was nothing to admire.

sentences.zh: 毓之此議，蓋何足稱耳！〉

translations.literal: Yu’s discussion here—how is it worth praising!〉
translations.idiomatic: Hence his verdict on Zhong Yu’s argument.〉

sentences.zh: 淮南旣平，爲青州刺史，加後將軍，遷都督徐州諸軍事，假節，又轉都督荊州。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he became inspector of Qingzhou, was added rear general, was promoted supervisor of all military affairs in Xu province with credential staff, and was later shifted to supervise Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huainan rebellion he became inspector of Qingzhou, was named rear general, then area commander for Xu province with imperial credentials, and finally transferred to command Jing province.

sentences.zh: 景元四年薨，追贈車騎將軍，謚曰惠侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyuan he died; posthumously he was gifted general of chariots and cavalry; posthumous title was Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Jingyuan era (263) and was posthumously honored as general of chariots and cavalry with the title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 子駿嗣。

translations.literal: Son Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong Jun inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 毓弟會，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yu’s younger brother Hui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhong Hui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 華歆字子魚，平原高唐人也。

translations.literal: Hua Xin, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin, courtesy name Ziyu, came from Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 高唐爲齊名都，衣冠無不游行市里。

translations.literal: Gaotang was Qi’s famous metropolis; none among cap-and-gown did not stroll the market wards.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang was a celebrated city of Qi, and every gentleman-about-town paraded the market streets.

sentences.zh: 歆爲吏，休沐出府，則歸家闔門。

translations.literal: When Xin was a clerk, on rest days leaving the office he would return home and shut the gate.
translations.idiomatic: As a minor clerk he spent his days off at home behind closed doors rather than roaming the city.

sentences.zh: 議論持平，終不毀傷人。

translations.literal: In discussion he held the balance and to the end did not slander or wound people.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he was even-handed and never used gossip to harm others.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：歆與北海邴原、管寧俱游學，三人相善，時人號三人爲「一龍」，歆爲龍頭，原爲龍腹，寧爲龍尾。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: Xin together with Bing Yuan of Beihai and Guan Ning all traveled to study; the three were on good terms; people of the time called the three “one dragon”—Xin was the dragon’s head, Yuan the dragon’s belly, Ning the dragon’s tail.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilue states: Xin, Bing Yuan of Beihai, and Guan Ning all traveled in pursuit of study, and the three were close friends. People of the time called them “one dragon”: Xin was the dragon's head, Yuan the dragon's belly, and Ning the dragon's tail.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲邴根矩之徽猷懿望，不必有愧華公，管幼安含德高蹈，又恐弗當爲尾。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that Bing Genju’s fine plan and lofty repute need not feel shame before Lord Hua; Guan You’an embraced virtue and trod high—again I fear he ought not to have been made the tail.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that Bing Yuan’s stature need not bow to Hua Xin’s, while Guan Ning’s moral elevation makes the “tail” label a poor fit.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》此言，未可以定其先後也。〉

translations.literal: This statement in the Wei Summary cannot be used to fix their order.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Weilüe’s ranking cannot be taken as definitive.〉

sentences.zh: 同郡陶丘洪亦知名，自以明見過歆。

translations.literal: Taoqiu Hong of the same commandery was also famous and believed his insight surpassed Xin’s.
translations.idiomatic: Taoqiu Hong of the same commandery was equally renowned and fancied himself shrewder than Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 時王芬與豪傑謀廢靈帝。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Fen plotted with bold spirits to depose Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen was then conspiring with local stalwarts to depose Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 語在武紀。

translations.literal: The account is in the Martial Emperor’s annals.
translations.idiomatic: The story is told in the annals of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書稱芬有大名於天下。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Book states that Fen had a great name in the realm.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu notes that Wang Fen enjoyed empire-wide renown.〉

sentences.zh: 芬陰呼歆、洪共定計，洪欲行，歆止之曰：「夫廢立大事，伊、霍之所難。

translations.literal: Fen secretly summoned Xin and Hong to settle the plan together; Hong wished to go, but Xin stopped him, saying, “As for deposing and enthroning—great affairs—even Yi and Huo found them hard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen secretly called in Hua Xin and Taoqiu Hong. Hong was ready to join the plot, but Hua Xin warned him: “Deposing an emperor is the gravest of acts—even Yi Yin and Huo Guang found it perilous.

sentences.zh: 芬性踈而不武，此必無成，而禍將及族。

translations.literal: Fen’s nature is careless and not martial; this surely will not succeed, and disaster will reach the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen is rash and no soldier—this cannot succeed, and it will destroy our families.

sentences.zh: 子其無往！」

translations.literal: You—do not go!"
translations.idiomatic: Stay out of it!"

sentences.zh: 洪從歆言而止。

translations.literal: Hong followed Xin’s words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taoqiu Hong heeded Hua Xin and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 後芬果敗，洪乃服。

translations.literal: Later Fen indeed failed; Hong then was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fen’s plot collapsed, Hong acknowledged Hua Xin’s wisdom.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中，病，去官。

translations.literal: He was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was appointed gentleman of the interior, but because of illness left office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he received a gentleman’s appointment but resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，何進輔政，徵河南鄭泰、潁川荀攸及歆等。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died, He Jin assisted the government and summoned Zheng Tai of Henan, Xun You of Yingchuan, and Xin and others.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling’s death the regent He Jin summoned Zheng Tai from Henan, Xun You from Yingchuan, Hua Xin, and others.

sentences.zh: 歆到，爲尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Xin arrived, he became gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital Hua Xin was made a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 董卓遷天子長安，歆求出爲下邽令，病不行，遂從藍田至南陽。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo moved the Son of Heaven to Chang’an; Xin asked to go out as magistrate of Xiagui, was ill and did not go, and thereupon went from Lantian to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo removed the court to Chang’an, Hua Xin sought appointment as magistrate of Xiagui but stayed behind, ill, and made his way from Lantian to Nanyang instead.

sentences.zh: 〈華嶠譜叙曰：歆少以高行顯名。

translations.literal: 〈Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Narrative states: Xin in youth by lofty conduct displayed fame.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Hua Qiao’s family history says that Hua Xin was known from youth for his high principles.

sentences.zh: 避西京之亂，與同志鄭泰等六七人，間步出武關。

translations.literal: Avoiding the western capital’s chaos, together with like-minded Zheng Tai and six or seven others, they walked stealthily out through Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the turmoil at Chang’an, he and six or seven companions including Zheng Tai slipped out through Wu Pass on foot.

sentences.zh: 道遇一丈夫獨行，願得俱，皆哀欲許之。

translations.literal: On the road they met one man walking alone who wished to join them; all pitied him and wished to consent.
translations.idiomatic: They met a lone traveler who begged to join them; the others, moved by pity, were ready to agree.

sentences.zh: 歆獨曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Xin alone said, “It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin alone objected: “We must not.

sentences.zh: 今已在危險之中，禍福患害，義猶一也。

translations.literal: Now we are already in danger; fortune and disaster, trouble and harm—in righteousness it is still one.
translations.idiomatic: We are already in peril; fortune and disaster will touch us alike.

sentences.zh: 無故受人，不知其義。

translations.literal: Without reason accepting a person—we do not know his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To take in a stranger for no good reason is to gamble on his character.

sentences.zh: 旣以受之，若有進退，可中棄乎！」

translations.literal: Once we have accepted him, if there is advance or retreat, can we abandon him midway!"
translations.idiomatic: And if we admit him and later regret it, we cannot simply cast him off midway down the road!"

sentences.zh: 衆不忍，卒與俱行。

translations.literal: The host could not bear it and in the end went with him together.
translations.idiomatic: The others overruled him and brought the stranger along.

sentences.zh: 此丈夫中道墮井，皆欲棄之。

translations.literal: This man midway fell into a well; all wished to abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: The man fell into a well along the way, and the others wanted to leave him.

sentences.zh: 歆曰：「已與俱矣，棄之不義。」

translations.literal: Xin said, “We are already together with him; to abandon him is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin said, “We accepted him; to abandon him now would be dishonorable."

sentences.zh: 相率共還出之，而後別去。

translations.literal: Leading one another they together returned and pulled him out, afterward parting and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him out together, then went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 衆乃大義之。〉

translations.literal: The host then greatly deemed him righteous.〉
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they all respected his integrity.〉

sentences.zh: 時袁術在穰，留歆。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shu was at Rang and detained Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was then at Rang and kept Hua Xin with him.

sentences.zh: 歆說術使進軍討卓，術不能用。

translations.literal: Xin persuaded Shu to advance the army and punish Zhuo; Shu could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin urged Yuan Shu to march against Dong Zhuo, but Yuan would not act.

sentences.zh: 歆欲棄去，會天子使太傅馬日磾安集關東，日磾辟歆爲掾。

translations.literal: Xin wished to abandon and leave; it happened that the Son of Heaven’s envoy Grand Tutor Ma Midi was pacifying east of the passes, and Midi summoned Xin as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin prepared to slip away when the imperial envoy Grand Tutor Ma Midi arrived to pacify the east; Ma Midi engaged him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 東至徐州，詔即拜歆豫章太守，以爲政清靜不煩，吏民感而愛之。

translations.literal: East to Xu province, an edict at once appointed Xin grand administrator of Yuzhang; because his government was clear, quiet, and not troublesome, clerks and people were moved and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He continued east to Xu province, where an edict named him governor of Yuzhang. His rule was calm and light-handed, and the officials and people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：揚州刺史劉繇死，其衆願奉歆爲主。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: When Yangzhou Inspector Liu Yao died, his host wished to uphold Xin as chief.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe adds that when Inspector Liu Yao of Yangzhou died, his followers wanted to make Hua Xin their leader.

sentences.zh: 歆以爲因時擅命，非人臣之宜。

translations.literal: Xin thought that seizing command by the opportunity of the times was not what a subject ought to do.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin held that grasping power on the spur of the moment was unworthy of a minister.

sentences.zh: 衆守之連月，卒謝遣之，不從。〉

translations.literal: The crowds guarded him for months; in the end he declined and sent them away; they did not obey.〉
translations.idiomatic: They besieged him for months until he firmly declined and dismissed them.〉

sentences.zh: 孫策略地江東，歆知策善用兵，乃幅巾奉迎。

translations.literal: Sun Ce was seizing territory in Jiang east; Xin knew Ce was good at using troops, and therefore in headcloth went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce carved out the lower Yangzi, Hua Xin—knowing Sun’s skill in war—went out in plain headcloth to submit.

sentences.zh: 策以其長者，待以上賔之禮。

translations.literal: Ce because he was an elder treated him with the rites of a high guest.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce treated him as an elder and received him with the honors due a senior guest.

sentences.zh: 〈胡冲吳歷曰：孫策擊豫章，先遣虞翻說歆。

translations.literal: 〈Hu Chong’s Wu Records states: When Sun Ce attacked Yuzhang, he first sent Yu Fan to persuade Xin.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Hu Chong’s Wu li relates that Sun Ce sent Yu Fan ahead to negotiate before striking Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歆荅曰：「乆在江表，常欲北歸；

translations.literal: Xin replied, saying, “Long on the south of the river, I have constantly wished to return north;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin answered, “I have long lingered south of the Yangzi but always wished to return north;

sentences.zh: 孫會稽來，吾便去也。」

translations.literal: when the Sun of Kuaiji comes, I then will go."
translations.idiomatic: and when your lord of Kuaiji arrives, I shall yield the command."

sentences.zh: 翻還報策，策乃進軍。

translations.literal: Fan returned and reported to Ce; Ce thereupon advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan carried this reply to Sun Ce, who then marched on the city.

sentences.zh: 歆葛巾迎策，策謂歆曰：「府君年德名望，遠近所歸；

translations.literal: Xin in ge cloth welcomed Ce; Ce said to Xin, “The governor’s years, virtue, and fame are what far and near return to;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin met him in homespun. Sun Ce said, “Your honor’s age and reputation command respect everywhere;

sentences.zh: 策年幼稚，宜脩子弟之禮。」

translations.literal: Ce’s years are young and weak; one ought to cultivate the rites of a younger kinsman."
translations.idiomatic: I am still young and should observe the courtesies due a junior."

sentences.zh: 便向歆拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed toward Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon bowed deeply to Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 華嶠譜叙曰：孫策略有揚州，盛兵徇豫章，一郡大恐。

translations.literal: Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Narrative states: When Sun Ce planned to take Yangzhou, he raised a great army and marched on Yuzhang; the whole commandery was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao records that when Sun Ce moved to seize Yangzhou and massed troops against Yuzhang, panic swept the commandery.

sentences.zh: 官屬請出郊迎，教曰：「無然。」

translations.literal: Subordinates asked to go out beyond the suburbs to welcome him; he instructed, saying, “Do not be so."
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates asked to go out beyond the suburbs to welcome him; he instructed, saying, “Do not be so."

sentences.zh: 策稍進，復白發兵，又不聽。

translations.literal: Ce gradually advanced; again they reported wishing to raise troops, and again he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: As Sun Ce drew nearer they again asked to mobilize the garrison, and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 及策至，一府皆造閤，請出避之。

translations.literal: When Ce arrived, the whole office went to the inner gate and asked to go out and avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce reached the yamen the entire staff crowded the inner gate, pleading to evacuate.

sentences.zh: 乃笑曰：「今將自來，何遽避之？」

translations.literal: He then laughed and said, “Now the general himself is coming—why urgently avoid him?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin only laughed and said, “The general is coming to see me in person—why flee?"

sentences.zh: 有頃，門下白曰：「孫將軍至。」

translations.literal: After a moment the gate reported, saying, “General Sun has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Presently a runner announced, “General Sun is here."

sentences.zh: 請見，乃前與歆共坐，談議良乆，夜乃別去。

translations.literal: He asked to be received; then he advanced and sat with Xin together, discussing a long time; at night they parted and left.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce asked for an audience, came forward, and sat with Hua Xin for a long talk before taking his leave that night.

sentences.zh: 義士聞之，皆長歎息而心自服也。

translations.literal: Righteous men who heard it all sighed long and in their hearts submitted of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle who heard the tale drew a long breath and conceded his moral authority.

sentences.zh: 策遂親執子孫之禮，禮爲上賔。

translations.literal: Ce thereupon personally performed the rites of a grandson, honoring him as a high guest.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce then treated him with the deference due a grandfather’s generation and received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 是時四方賢士大夫避地江南者甚衆，皆出其下，人人望風。

translations.literal: At that time worthy grandees from the four quarters who avoided trouble south of the Yangzi were very many; all ranked beneath him; every man watched the wind.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, many worthy gentlemen from the four quarters had taken refuge south of the Yangzi, yet all ranked below Hua Xin; every man watched and followed his direction.

sentences.zh: 每策大會，坐上莫敢先發言，歆時起更衣，則論議讙譁。

translations.literal: Whenever Ce held a great assembly, on the seats none dared speak first; when Xin from time to time rose to change clothes, then debate became noisy clamor.
translations.idiomatic: At Sun Ce’s banquets no one would speak until Hua Xin left the room to change his robes—only then would conversation break out freely.

sentences.zh: 歆能劇飲，至石餘不亂，衆人微察，常以其整衣冠爲異，江南號之曰「華獨坐」。

translations.literal: Xin could drink heavily, to more than a picul without disorder; the company subtly observed, always taking his keeping cap and gown neat as strange—south of the river styled him “Hua who sits alone."
translations.idiomatic: He could put away over a picul of wine without losing his composure; guests marveled that his cap and robes stayed perfectly straight, and south of the Yangzi they nicknamed him “Hua who sits alone."

sentences.zh: 虞溥江表傳曰：孫策在椒丘，遣虞翻說歆。

translations.literal: Yu Pu’s Account of the South of the Yangzi states: Sun Ce at Jiaoqiu sent Yu Fan to persuade Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu’s Jiangbiao zhuan records that Sun Ce, camped at Jiaoqiu, sent Yu Fan to negotiate with Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 翻旣去，歆請功曹劉壹入議。

translations.literal: After Fan had gone, Xin asked merit clerk Liu Yi to enter for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Fan withdrew, Hua Xin called in his merit clerk Liu Yi for counsel.

sentences.zh: 壹勸歆住城，遣檄迎軍。

translations.literal: Yi urged Xin to hold the city and dispatch a proclamation to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi urged him to hold the walls and issue a summons welcoming Sun Ce’s host.

sentences.zh: 歆曰：「吾雖劉刺史所置，上用，猶是剖符吏也。

translations.literal: Xin said, “Although I was installed by Inspector Liu, what the court employs is still a split-tally official.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin replied, “Inspector Liu may have appointed me, but I still serve the Han with a bronze tally—an officer of the throne.

sentences.zh: 今從卿計，恐死有餘責矣。」

translations.literal: Now if I follow your plan, I fear even in death there would be more than enough blame."
translations.idiomatic: If I followed your advice, I would still bear a crushing guilt after death."

sentences.zh: 壹曰：「王景興旣漢朝所用，且爾時會稽人衆盛彊，猶見原恕，明府何慮？」

translations.literal: Yi said, “Wang Jingxing was already employed by the Han court; moreover at that time the people of Kuaiji were numerous and strong—still he was forgiven and excused—what does my lord worry?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi answered, “Wang Lang served the Han and, though Kuaiji was populous and strong, was pardoned—why should you fear?"

sentences.zh: 於是夜逆作檄，明旦出城，遣吏齎迎。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the night they hastily drafted the proclamation; at dawn they left the city, dispatching clerks to carry it in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore drafted the proclamation overnight, opened the gates at dawn, and sent clerks to deliver it as a gesture of welcome.

sentences.zh: 策便進軍，與歆相見，待以上賔，接以朋友之禮。

translations.literal: Ce thereupon advanced the army, met Xin, treated him with rites of a high guest, and received him with the courtesies due a friend.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce marched in, met Hua Xin, honored him as a chief guest, and greeted him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：夫大雅之處世也，必先審隱顯之期，以定出處之分，否則括囊以保其身，泰則行義以達其道。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: As for the great-minded gentleman’s dwelling in the world, he must first examine the timing of concealment and exposure, to fix the division of going out and staying in; otherwise he bundles the sack to preserve his person; when open he practices righteousness to extend his way.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observed that a true gentleman first weighs when to hide and when to serve, then chooses office or retirement accordingly—either binding ambition like a sealed purse or stepping forth to advance the Way.

sentences.zh: 歆旣無夷、皓韜邈之風，又失王臣匪躬之操，故撓心於邪儒之說，交臂於陵肆之徒，位奪於一豎，節墯於當時。

translations.literal: Xin had neither the wind of Boyi and Donggao’s far-reaching concealment, nor again the conduct of a royal minister who is not for himself; therefore his heart was twisted by a heterodox scholar’s persuasion, he locked arms with a tomb-raiding sort; rank was wrested by one stripling, integrity fell in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin lacked the reclusive integrity of Boyi or the Han hermits, and he failed the steadfast loyalty of a true king’s minister; he let a clever aide sway him, dealt with a warlord, surrendered his post to a young conqueror, and forfeited his reputation forever.

sentences.zh: 昔許、蔡失位，不得列於諸侯；

translations.literal: Formerly when Xu and Cai lost their stations, they could not be ranked among the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: When the lords of Xu and Cai lost their thrones, the Spring and Autumn annals refused them a place among the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 州公寔來，魯人以爲賤恥。

translations.literal: when the Duke of Zhou came in truth, the people of Lu took it as base shame.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Duke of Zhou marched east, the people of Lu counted it a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 方之於歆，咎孰大焉！〉

translations.literal: Compared to Xin—which fault is greater!〉
translations.idiomatic: Set that beside Hua Xin—whose offense is the greater?〉

sentences.zh: 後策死。

translations.literal: Later Ce died.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ce died,

sentences.zh: 太祖在官渡，表天子徵歆。

translations.literal: the Grand Progenitor at Guandu memorialized the Son of Heaven to summon Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao at Guandu petitioned the emperor to summon Hua Xin north.

sentences.zh: 孫權欲不遣，歆謂權曰：「將軍奉王命，始交好曹公，分義未固，使僕得爲將軍效心，豈不有益乎？

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished not to send him; Xin said to Quan, “The general upholds the king’s commands and has only begun friendly relations with Lord Cao; the bond of duty is not yet firm—if your servant can devote his heart to the general’s service, would it not be beneficial?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was reluctant to let him go. Hua Xin said, “You hold the Han mandate and have only begun to treat with Cao Cao—if I go north and speak for you, will that not strengthen your position?

sentences.zh: 今空留僕，是爲養無用之物，非將軍之良計也。」

translations.literal: Now to keep your servant here empty is to raise a useless thing—not the general’s good plan."
translations.idiomatic: To detain me here for nothing is to hoard a useless hostage—not wise policy for a general."

sentences.zh: 權恱，乃遣歆。

translations.literal: Quan was pleased and thereupon sent Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was persuaded and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 賔客舊人送之者千餘人，贈遺數百金。

translations.literal: Guests and old associates who saw him off were more than a thousand persons; gifts exceeded several hundred pounds of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand friends and former colleagues attended his departure, pressing gifts of several hundred pounds of gold upon him.

sentences.zh: 歆皆無所拒，密各題識，至臨去，悉聚諸物，謂諸賔客曰：「本無拒諸君之心，而所受遂多。

translations.literal: Xin refused none, but secretly marked each; when about to depart, he gathered all the objects together and said to the host of guests, “Originally I had no mind to refuse you gentlemen, yet what I received has become much.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted every offering but secretly labeled each bundle. As he was leaving he piled the gifts together and told the crowd, “I never meant to refuse your kindness, yet I have accepted far too much.

sentences.zh: 念單車遠行，將以懷璧爲罪，願賔客爲之計。」

translations.literal: Thinking that alone in a cart traveling far, I will take carrying the jade as a crime—I beg you gentlemen to devise for me."
translations.idiomatic: A lone rider crossing the empire with a fortune in gold courts the fate of the man who clutched the jade—please decide what I should do."

sentences.zh: 衆乃各留所贈，而服其德。

translations.literal: The host thereupon each kept what they had gifted, and admired his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They each reclaimed their presents and admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 歆至，拜議郎，參司空軍事，入爲尚書，轉侍中，代荀彧爲尚書令。

translations.literal: When Xin arrived, he was appointed consultant, joined the Minister of Works’ military staff, entered as master of writing, was shifted to attendant-in-ordinary, and replaced Xun Yu as director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the north he was named consultant, served on Cao Cao’s staff, entered the Masters of Writing, became attendant-in-ordinary, and succeeded Xun Yu as director.

sentences.zh: 太祖征孫權，表歆爲軍師。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Sun Quan, he memorialized Xin as army strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Sun Quan he appointed Hua Xin chief army strategist.

sentences.zh: 魏國旣建，爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was established, he became imperial counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When the kingdom of Wei was founded he became imperial counselor.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，拜相國，封安樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the king’s throne, he was appointed minister of state and enfeoffed as village marquis of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the title of king he named Hua Xin minister of state and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Anle.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，改爲司徒。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, it was changed to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession Hua Xin was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：文帝受禪，歆登壇相儀，奉皇帝璽綬，以成受命之禮。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Book states: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, Xin ascended the altar to assist the ceremony, presented the imperial seal and ribbon, and thereby completed the rite of receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu records that at Cao Pi’s accession Hua Xin mounted the terrace to direct the ritual and handed over the imperial seal to complete the abdication.

sentences.zh: 華嶠譜叙曰：文帝受禪，朝臣三公已下並受爵位；

translations.literal: Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Narrative states: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, court ministers from the three dukes down all received noble ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao's family history says that when Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, all court ministers from the Three Excellencies downward received noble titles;

sentences.zh: 歆以形色忤時，徙爲司徒，而不進爵。

translations.literal: Xin by facial expression offended the times and was shifted to Minister of Education without advance in noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: but Hua Xin’s grim expression offended the court, so he was sidelined as Minister of Education without promotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝乆不懌，以問尚書令陳羣曰：「我應天受禪，百辟群后，莫不人人恱喜，形于聲色，而相國及公獨有不怡者，何也？」

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wen long was not pleased and asked Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Qun, saying, “I responded to Heaven and received the abdication; the hundred nobles and host of lords—there was none who was not personally joyful, showing it in voice and countenance—yet the minister of state and you alone had unpleased looks—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei remained uneasy for a long time and asked Chen Qun, Director of the Masters of Writing: “I responded to Heaven and received the abdication; among the hundred officials and many lords, everyone without exception rejoiced, showing it in voice and countenance. Why did only the Minister of State and you have unhappy expressions?"

sentences.zh: 羣起離席長跪曰：「臣與相國曾臣漢朝，心雖恱喜，義形其色，亦懼陛下實應且憎。」

translations.literal: Qun rose from his mat, knelt long, and said, “Your subject and the minister of state were once Han ministers; though in our hearts we were joyful, righteousness showed in our expression—we also feared Your Majesty would in truth both respond and resent."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun left his seat and knelt: “We were Han officials; joy could not erase duty—we feared Your Majesty might read our faces as resentment."

sentences.zh: 帝大恱，遂重異之。〉

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and thereupon thought them doubly extraordinary.〉
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and held them in still higher regard.〉

sentences.zh: 歆素清貧，祿賜以振施親戚故人，家無擔石之儲。

translations.literal: Xin was always clear and poor; salary and gifts he used to relieve and give to kinsmen and old friends; his household had not a picul’s store.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin lived plainly, spent his stipends on kin and old friends, and kept no surplus grain at home.

sentences.zh: 公卿嘗並賜沒入生口，唯歆出而嫁之。

translations.literal: When dukes and ministers were together granted confiscated bond servants, only Xin took them out and married them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the high ministers were allotted confiscated slaves, Hua Xin alone freed his share and saw the women married out.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息，

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed with approval,

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：盛聞慶賞威刑，必宗於主，權宜宥怒，出自人君。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: Sheng has heard that rewards and awesome punishments must take the ruler as their model; expedient forgiveness of anger issues from the lord alone.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng comments: rewards and punishments belong to the sovereign alone;

sentences.zh: 子路私饋，仲尼毀其食器；

translations.literal: When Zilu privately gave food, Zhongni smashed his vessels;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius broke Zilu’s bowl for giving alms on his own authority;

sentences.zh: 田氏盜施，春秋著以爲譏。

translations.literal: the Tian clan stole charity, and the Spring and Autumn recorded it as blame.
translations.idiomatic: the Tian clan’s unauthorized largesse earned the Spring and Autumn’s censure.

sentences.zh: 斯襃貶之成言，已然之顯義也。

translations.literal: These are fixed words of praise and blame, already manifest righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Such precedents define what praise and blame mean.

sentences.zh: 孥戮之家，國刑所肅，受賜之室，乾施所加，若在哀矜，理無偏宥。

translations.literal: Families subject to child execution—the state’s punishments awe them; chambers that receive gifts—Heaven’s lord applies grace; if there is pity and compassion, in principle there is no partial pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned families await the law’s severity; favored households receive the Son of Heaven’s grace—mercy cannot be applied unevenly.

sentences.zh: 歆居股肱之任。

translations.literal: Xin occupied the duty of thigh and arm.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin held one of the empire’s highest posts,

sentences.zh: 同元首之重，則當公言皇朝，以彰天澤，而默受嘉賜，獨爲君子，旣犯作福之嫌，又違必去之義，可謂匹夫之仁，蹈道則未也。

translations.literal: Sharing the head’s weight, he ought to have spoken openly for the royal court to display Heaven’s grace—yet silently he accepted fine gifts and alone played the gentleman; he both incurred the suspicion of arrogating blessing and violated the duty of surely declining—this may be called the benevolence of a common man; treading the Way he had not yet done so.
translations.idiomatic: yet he pocketed imperial largesse in silence to play the private saint—inviting the charge of usurping the ruler’s prerogative and breaking the rule that such gifts must be refused. That is kindness of a petty sort, not the conduct of a man who walks the true Way.

sentences.zh: 魏書曰：歆性周密，舉動詳慎。

translations.literal: The Wei Book states: Xin’s nature was thorough and close; movements were detailed and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu describes him as meticulous and deliberate in every action.

sentences.zh: 常以爲人臣陳事，務以諷諫合道爲貴，就有所言，不敢顯露，故其事多不見載。

translations.literal: He always held that when a subject presents affairs, the task is to use indirect remonstrance to accord with the Way as precious; even when he had something to say, he dared not display it openly—therefore his affairs for the most part are not seen recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He believed ministers should remonstrate through subtle counsel; because he rarely spoke bluntly, few of his policy debates were written down.

sentences.zh: 華嶠譜叙曰：歆淡於財欲，前後寵賜，諸公莫及，然終不殖產業。

translations.literal: Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Narrative states: Xin was indifferent to wealth and desire; former and later favor and gifts—none of the dukes matched him—yet to the end he did not amass property.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao adds that Hua Xin cared nothing for riches: no minister received more imperial largesse, yet he never built an estate.

sentences.zh: 陳羣常歎曰：「若華公，可謂通而不泰，清而不介者矣。」

translations.literal: Chen Qun often sighed, saying, “As for Lord Hua, one may say he is penetrating yet not arrogant, clear yet not stiff."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun often said of him, “Master Hua is discerning without arrogance, incorruptible without priggishness."

sentences.zh: 傅子曰：敢問今之君子？

translations.literal: The Master Fu’s text says: I dare ask of today’s gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan’s Fu zi asks: Who counts as a gentleman today?

sentences.zh: 曰：「袁郎中積德行儉，華太尉積德居順，其智可及也，其清不可及也。

translations.literal: It is said, “Gentleman Yuan of the Masters of Writing piles virtue and practices frugality; Grand Commandant Hua piles virtue and dwells in compliance—their wisdom can be matched; their clarity cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: “Yuan Huan hoards virtue and lives frugally; Grand Commandant Hua hoards virtue and moves with the times—their wisdom others may equal, but not their purity.

sentences.zh: 事上以忠，濟下以仁，晏嬰、行父何以加諸？」〉

translations.literal: Serving superiors with loyalty, succoring inferiors with benevolence—how could Yan Ying or Xingfu add to that?”〉"
translations.idiomatic: Loyal to those above, kind to those below—what could Yan Ying or Ji Wenzi add to that?”〉"

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「司徒，國之儁老，所與和陰陽理庶事也。

translations.literal: An edict said, “The Minister of Education is the state’s eminent elder; with him one harmonizes yin and yang and orders the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “The Minister of Education is the kingdom’s senior steward, the man who balances yin and yang and oversees every branch of government.

sentences.zh: 今大官重膳，而司徒蔬食，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: Now the grand provisioner serves heavy delicacies, yet the Minister of Education eats vegetables—this is very meaningless."
translations.idiomatic: The palace serves rich fare while you dine on vegetables—that is absurd."

sentences.zh: 特賜御衣，及爲其妻子男女皆作衣服。

translations.literal: He was specially gifted imperial robes, and for his wife, sons, and daughters, male and female, all were made clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore sent him imperial robes and had garments made for his entire household.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：又賜奴婢五十人。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Book states: In addition fifty male and female slaves were granted.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu adds that he was also given fifty male and female servants.〉

sentences.zh: 三府議：「舉孝廉，本以德行，不復限以試經。」

translations.literal: The Three Offices debated: “In recommending Filial and Incorrupt, originally it was by virtue and conduct; no longer limit them by examination on the classics."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices debated: “Recommendations as Filial and Incorrupt were originally based on virtue and conduct; they should no longer be limited by examinations on the classics.”

sentences.zh: 歆以爲「喪亂以來，六籍墮廢，當務存立，以崇王道。

translations.literal: Xin thought that “since the turmoil of arms, the six storehouses have fallen in ruin; one ought urgently to preserve and establish them, to exalt the king’s way.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin objected: “Since the wars began the Six Classics have been neglected; we must restore them to uphold the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 夫制法者，所以經盛衰。

translations.literal: As for those who make laws, they are the means to thread through flourishing and decline.
translations.idiomatic: Law is the thread that runs through order and chaos;

sentences.zh: 今聽孝廉不以經試，恐學業遂從此而廢。

translations.literal: Now if we hear Filial and Incorrupt without classics examination, I fear learning will from this be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: to waive the classics test for nominees is to let scholarship die altogether.

sentences.zh: 若有秀異，可特徵用。

translations.literal: If there are outstanding talents, one may specially summon and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Truly exceptional men can always be summoned by special edict.

sentences.zh: 患於無其人，何患不得哉？」

translations.literal: Worry that there are no such persons—why worry that you cannot obtain them?"
translations.idiomatic: The problem is finding worthy men, not devising easier ways to find none."

sentences.zh: 帝從其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，詔公卿舉獨行君子，歆舉管寧，帝以安車徵之。

translations.literal: During the Huangchu era, an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to recommend gentlemen of solitary conduct. Hua Xin recommended Guan Ning, and the emperor summoned him in a comfortable carriage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangchu era, an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to recommend gentlemen of solitary conduct. Hua Xin recommended Guan Ning, and the emperor summoned him with a quiet carriage.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封博平侯，增邑五百戶，并前千三百戶，轉拜太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Hua Xin was advanced to Marquis of Boping, his fief was increased by five hundred households, for a total of thirteen hundred households, and he was transferred and appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Hua Xin was advanced to Marquis of Boping. His fief was increased by five hundred households, making thirteen hundred households in all, and he was transferred and appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 《列異傳》曰：歆爲諸生時，嘗宿人門外。

translations.literal: The Accounts of Strange Events says: When Hua Xin was a student, he once spent the night outside someone’s gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Accounts of Strange Events says: When Hua Xin was a student, he once spent the night outside someone’s gate.

sentences.zh: 主人婦夜產。

translations.literal: The master’s wife gave birth during the night.
translations.idiomatic: The master’s wife gave birth during the night.

sentences.zh: 有頃，兩吏詣門，便辟易却，相謂曰：「公在此。」

translations.literal: After a short while, two officials came to the gate, immediately drew back, and said to each other, “The duke is here.”
translations.idiomatic: After a short while, two officials came to the gate, immediately drew back, and said to each other, “The duke is here.”

sentences.zh: 躊躇良乆，一吏曰：「籍當定，柰何得住？」

translations.literal: They hesitated for a long time. One official said, “The register must be fixed; how can we remain here?”
translations.idiomatic: They hesitated for a long time. One official said, “The register must be fixed; how can we remain here?”

sentences.zh: 乃前向歆拜，相將入。

translations.literal: They then went forward, bowed toward Hua Xin, and went in together.
translations.idiomatic: They then went forward, bowed toward Hua Xin, and went in together.

sentences.zh: 出並行，共語曰：「當與幾歲？」

translations.literal: When they came out, they walked side by side and spoke together, saying, “How many years should we give?”
translations.idiomatic: When they came out, they walked side by side and spoke together, saying, “How many years should we give?”

sentences.zh: 一人曰：「當三歲。」

translations.literal: One said, “Three years.”
translations.idiomatic: One said, “Three years.”

sentences.zh: 天明，歆去。

translations.literal: At daybreak, Hua Xin left.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, Hua Xin left.

sentences.zh: 後欲驗其事，至三歲，故往問兒消息，果已死。

translations.literal: Later he wanted to verify the matter; when the child reached the age of three, he deliberately went to ask for news of the child, and the child had indeed already died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he wanted to verify the matter. When the child would have reached the age of three, he deliberately went to ask for news of him, and the child had indeed already died.

sentences.zh: 歆乃自知當爲公。

translations.literal: Hua Xin then knew himself that he would become a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin then knew himself that he would become a duke.

sentences.zh: 臣松之按《晉陽秋》說魏舒少時寄宿事，亦如之。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes that the Jin Yangqiu tells the same story about Wei Shu when he was young and lodging away from home.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Songzhi notes that the Jin Yangqiu tells the same story about Wei Shu when he was young and lodging away from home.

sentences.zh: 以爲理無二人俱有此事，將由傳者不同。

translations.literal: I think it is unreasonable that two people both had this same event; it must be due to differing transmitters.
translations.idiomatic: I think it is unreasonable that two people both had this same event; it must be due to differing transmitters.

sentences.zh: 今寧信列異。

translations.literal: Here I would rather trust the Accounts of Strange Events.
translations.idiomatic: Here I would rather trust the Accounts of Strange Events.

sentences.zh: 歆稱病乞退，讓位於寧。

translations.literal: Hua Xin pleaded illness and requested retirement, yielding his position to Guan Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin pleaded illness and requested retirement, yielding his position to Guan Ning.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 臨當大會，乃遣散騎常侍繆襲奉詔喻指曰：「朕新莅庶事，一日萬機，懼聽斷之不明。

translations.literal: When a great court gathering was about to be held, he sent the Regular Mounted Attendant Miao Xi with an edict explaining his intent: “I have newly taken charge of the many affairs; in a single day there are ten thousand matters, and I fear that my hearings and judgments are not clear.
translations.idiomatic: When a great court gathering was about to be held, he sent the Regular Mounted Attendant Miao Xi to convey an edict explaining his intent: “I have newly taken charge of the many affairs; each day brings ten thousand matters, and I fear that my hearings and judgments are unclear.

sentences.zh: 賴有德之臣，左右朕躬，而君屢以疾辭位。

translations.literal: I rely on ministers of virtue to assist me personally, yet you have repeatedly used illness to decline your position.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on ministers of virtue to assist me personally, yet you have repeatedly used illness to decline your position.

sentences.zh: 夫量主擇君，不居其朝，委榮棄祿，不究其位，古人固有之矣，顧以爲周公、伊尹則不然。

translations.literal: Measuring the ruler and choosing one’s lord, not dwelling at his court, casting aside honor and abandoning salary, and not completing one’s tenure are indeed things that men of old sometimes did; but I think the Duke of Zhou and Yi Yin were not like this.
translations.idiomatic: To measure the ruler and choose one's lord, refuse to dwell at his court, cast aside honor and abandon salary, and not complete one's tenure are indeed things men of old sometimes did; but I think the Duke of Zhou and Yi Yin were not like this.

sentences.zh: 絜身徇節，常人爲之，不望之於君。

translations.literal: Keeping one’s person pure and following one’s private integrity are things ordinary men do; I do not expect this from you.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping one’s person pure and following one’s private integrity are things ordinary men do; I do not expect this from you.

sentences.zh: 君其力疾就會，以惠予一人。

translations.literal: You should exert yourself despite illness and attend the gathering, thereby favoring me, the one man.
translations.idiomatic: You should exert yourself despite illness and attend the gathering, thereby favoring me, the one man.

sentences.zh: 將立席机莚，命百官緫己，以須君到，朕然後御坐。」

translations.literal: I shall have mats, armrests, and cushions set up, and order the hundred officials to compose themselves and await your arrival; only then will I take my seat.”
translations.idiomatic: I shall have mats, armrests, and cushions set up, and order the hundred officials to compose themselves and await your arrival; only afterward will I take my seat.”

sentences.zh: 又詔襲：「須歆必起，乃還。」

translations.literal: He also ordered Xi, “Wait until Hua Xin definitely rises, and only then return.”
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Xi, “Wait until Hua Xin definitely rises, and only then return.”

sentences.zh: 歆不得已，乃起。

translations.literal: Hua Xin had no choice and therefore rose.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin had no choice and therefore rose.

sentences.zh: 太和中，遣曹真從子午道伐蜀，車駕東幸許昌。

translations.literal: In the Taihe years he sent Cao Zhen by the Ziwu Road to attack Shu; the imperial carriage favored Xuchang to the east.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era the court sent Cao Zhen against Shu through the Ziwu defile while the emperor moved east to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 歆上疏曰：「兵亂以來，過踰二紀。

translations.literal: Xin submitted a memorial saying, “Since the turmoil of arms, more than two dozen years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin memorialized: “More than twenty-four years have passed since the wars began.

sentences.zh: 大魏承天受命，陛下以聖德當成康之隆，宜弘一代之治，紹三王之迹。

translations.literal: Great Wei has received Heaven’s mandate; Your Majesty by sagely virtue ought to match Cheng and Kang’s height; you ought to expand a generation’s good order and continue the traces of the three kings.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei holds the mandate, and Your Majesty’s virtue should rival the golden ages of Cheng and Kang—extend good government and walk in the footsteps of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 雖有二賊負險延命，苟聖化日躋，遠人懷德，將襁負而至。

translations.literal: Although the two bandits rely on defiles and prolong their lives, if sagely transformation daily ascends, distant men will cherish virtue and will come carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shu and Wu cling to their mountains, steady moral government will draw the border peoples until the enemy heartlands crumble of themselves.

sentences.zh: 夫兵不得已而用之，故戢而時動。

translations.literal: As for arms, one uses them when there is no choice; therefore they are sheathed and moved at the proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are a last resort; they should stay sheathed until the moment is ripe.

sentences.zh: 臣誠願陛下先留心於治道，以征伐爲後事。

translations.literal: Your subject sincerely wishes Your Majesty first to set your heart on the way of good order, and take punitive expeditions as a later matter.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to put governance first and treat campaigns as a secondary concern.

sentences.zh: 且千里運糧，非用兵之利；

translations.literal: Moreover to transport grain a thousand li is not advantageous to using troops;
translations.idiomatic: Supplying an army across a thousand li is no way to win a war;

sentences.zh: 越險深入，無獨克之功。

translations.literal: to cross perils and go deep brings no merit of sole conquest.
translations.idiomatic: forcing perilous terrain deep into enemy country rarely yields a clean victory.

sentences.zh: 如聞今年徵役，頗失農桑之業。

translations.literal: As I have heard, this year’s levies for service have somewhat lost farming and mulberry’s occupation.
translations.idiomatic: This year’s conscriptions, I hear, have already disrupted sowing and silkworm work.

sentences.zh: 爲國者以民爲基，民以衣食爲本。

translations.literal: Those who order the state take the people as foundation; the people take clothing and food as root.
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on the people, and the people rest on food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 使中國無饑寒之患，百姓無離土之心，則天下幸甚，二賊之釁，可坐而待也。

translations.literal: If the central lands have no trouble of hunger and cold, and the hundred surnames have no mind to leave the soil, then all under Heaven will be greatly fortunate—the two bandits’ rifts may be awaited sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Free the heartland from want and the farmers from flight, and the empire will prosper—then the rebels’ doom can be awaited without stirring an army.

sentences.zh: 臣備位宰相，老病日篤，犬馬之命將盡，恐不復奉望鑾蓋，不敢不竭臣子之懷，唯陛下裁察！」

translations.literal: Your subject occupies the place of chief minister; old age and illness daily grow grave; the dog-and-horse life is about to end—I fear I will not again attend the imperial palanquin—I dare not not exhaust a subject’s devotion—only may Your Majesty judge and examine!"
translations.idiomatic: I hold the chancellorship though age and sickness waste me; I may never again attend your carriage—yet I dare not withhold a minister’s utmost counsel. I beg you to weigh it carefully!"

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「君深慮國計，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, saying, “You deeply ponder the state’s plan; We greatly approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: “Your care for the realm does you credit.

sentences.zh: 賊憑恃山川，二祖勞於前世，猶不克平，朕豈敢自多，謂必滅之哉！

translations.literal: The bandits rely on mountains and rivers; the two ancestors toiled in former ages and still could not pacify them—how dare We alone presume, saying we are sure to destroy them!
translations.idiomatic: Those rebels hold the mountains and rivers; my father and grandfather campaigned for years without finishing them—how could I boast that I alone will wipe them out?

sentences.zh: 諸將以爲不一探取，無由自弊，是以觀兵以闚其釁。

translations.literal: The generals thought that without once probing and taking, there would be no way for them to ruin themselves—therefore We display troops to spy their rift.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged a probe, arguing that the enemy must be flushed into some mistake—hence this show of force to test their weakness.

sentences.zh: 若天時未至，周武還師，乃前事之鑒，朕敬不忘所戒。」

translations.literal: If Heaven’s season has not yet arrived, King Wu of Zhou’s returning the host is a mirror of former affairs—We respectfully do not forget what is warned."
translations.idiomatic: If the time is not ripe, King Wu’s withdrawal is our precedent—I heed that lesson."

sentences.zh: 時秋大雨，詔真引軍還。

translations.literal: At that time in autumn came great rain; an edict ordered Zhen to lead the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rains set in, and an edict recalled Cao Zhen’s army.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，歆薨，謚曰敬侯。《魏書》云：歆時年七十五。子表嗣。初，文帝分歆戶邑，封歆弟緝列侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, Xin died and was posthumously titled Marquis Jing. The Book of Wei says: Xin was then seventy-five years old. His son Biao succeeded him. Earlier, Emperor Wen divided Xin’s household fief and enfeoffed Xin’s younger brother Ji as a ranked marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin died in Taihe 5 (231) and received the posthumous title Marquis Jing. According to the Book of Wei, he was seventy-five. His son Hua Biao succeeded him. Earlier, Emperor Wen had divided off part of Hua Xin’s fief and made Xin’s younger brother Hua Ji a marquis.

sentences.zh: 華嶠《譜叙》曰：歆有三子。時同寮諸郎共平尚書事，年少，並兼厲鋒氣，要召名譽。
