translations.literal: Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Preface says: Xin had three sons. At the time, the various gentlemen who were his colleagues jointly handled Secretariat affairs; they were young and all had, besides sharp and vigorous temperaments, a desire to summon reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao’s Genealogical Preface says: Hua Xin had three sons. When Hua Biao and the other young gentlemen of his office jointly handled Secretariat business, most of them were sharp-tempered and eager for renown.

sentences.zh: 尚書事至，或有不便，故遺漏不視，及傳書者去，即入深文論駮。

translations.literal: When Secretariat matters arrived, if something was unsuitable, they therefore let it be omitted and did not look at it; when the one transmitting the document had gone, they then entered into deep-text disputation and rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: If a Secretariat document seemed improper, they would deliberately ignore it until the messenger left, then compose elaborate legalistic refutations.

sentences.zh: 惟表不然，事來有不便，輒與尚書共論盡其意，主者固執，不得已，然後共奏議。司空陳羣等以此稱之。

translations.literal: Only Biao was not so. When a matter came and something was unsuitable, he would at once discuss it fully with the Director; if the responsible official firmly persisted and there was no choice, only then would they jointly submit a deliberation. Minister of Works Chen Qun and others praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Biao behaved differently. When a document was problematic, he would discuss it fully with the Masters of Writing, and only if the responsible official stubbornly held firm and there was no choice did they submit a joint deliberation. Chen Qun, Minister of Works, and others praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 仕晉，歷太子少傅、太常。稱疾致仕，拜光祿大夫。性清淡，常慮天下退理。

translations.literal: Serving Jin, he passed through the offices of Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and Minister of Ceremonies. Pleading illness, he retired from office and was appointed Grandee of Splendid Happiness. His nature was pure and detached, and he constantly worried that order under Heaven was declining.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he served as Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and then Minister of Ceremonies. He retired on grounds of illness and was made Grandee of Splendid Happiness. Plain and detached by nature, he often worried that public order was slipping away.

sentences.zh: 司徒李胤、司隷王弘等常稱曰：「若此人者，不可得而貴，不可得而賤，不可得而親，不可得而踈。」

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Li Yin, Colonel Director of Retainers Wang Hong, and others often praised him, saying, “As for a man like this, he cannot be made noble, cannot be made base, cannot be made intimate, and cannot be made distant."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin and Wang Hong often said of him, “A man like this cannot be raised by honor, lowered by disgrace, drawn in by intimacy, or pushed away by distance."

sentences.zh: 中子博，歷三縣內史，治有名跡。少子周，黃門侍郎、常山太守，博學有文思。中年遇疾，終于家。

translations.literal: The middle son, Bo, successively served as Interior Minister of three counties, and his governance had noted achievements. The youngest son, Zhou, was Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Administrator of Changshan; he was broadly learned and had literary thought. In middle age he encountered illness and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: The middle son, Hua Bo, governed three counties as Interior Minister and left a good record. The youngest, Hua Zhou, served as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Administrator of Changshan; he was learned and gifted in writing, but fell ill in middle age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 長子廙，字長駿。《晉諸公贊》曰：廙有文翰，歷位尚書令、太子少傅，追贈光祿大夫開府。

translations.literal: The eldest son, Yi, had the courtesy name Changjun. The Eulogies of the Various Lords of Jin says: Yi had literary writing; he successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, and was posthumously presented as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with office opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi, the eldest son, courtesy name Changjun, was accomplished in letters. The Eulogies of the Various Lords of Jin says that he rose to Director of the Secretariat and Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, and was posthumously granted the honors of Grandee of Splendid Happiness and office-opening rank.

sentences.zh: 嶠字叔駿，有才學，撰《後漢書》，世稱爲良史。爲祕書監、尚書。澹字玄駿，最知名，爲河南尹。

translations.literal: Qiao, courtesy name Shujun, had talent and learning; he compiled the Book of Later Han, and the age called him a good historian. He became Director of the Palace Library and Director of the Secretariat. Tan, courtesy name Xuanjun, was the most famous and became Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao, courtesy name Shujun, was talented and learned; he wrote a Book of Later Han and was regarded as a fine historian. He served as Director of the Palace Library and Director of the Secretariat. Hua Tan, courtesy name Xuanjun, was the best known of them and became Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 廙三子。昆字敬倫，清粹有檢，爲尚書。薈字敬叔。世語稱薈貴正。恒字敬則，以通理稱。昆，尚書；薈，河南尹；恒，左光祿大夫開府。

translations.literal: Yi had three sons. Kun, courtesy name Jinglun, was pure and had restraint, and became Director of the Secretariat. Hui, courtesy name Jingshu; the Sayings of the Age says Hui valued correctness. Heng, courtesy name Jingze, was praised for penetrating principle. Kun was Director of the Secretariat; Hui was Intendant of Henan; Heng was Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness with office opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi had three sons: Hua Kun, courtesy name Jinglun, who was pure and disciplined and became Director of the Secretariat; Hua Hui, courtesy name Jingshu, whom the Sayings of the Age praises for uprightness; and Hua Heng, courtesy name Jingze, known for sound judgment. Kun became Director of the Secretariat, Hui Intendant of Henan, and Heng Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness with office-opening rank.

sentences.zh: 澹子軼，字彥夏。有當世才志，爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: Tan’s son Yi, courtesy name Yanxia, had talent and ambition suited to the age and became Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan’s son Hua Yi, courtesy name Yanxia, had contemporary talent and ambition and served as Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王朗字景興，東海郡人也。以通經，拜郎中，除菑丘長。師太尉楊賜，賜薨，棄官行服。舉孝廉，辟公府，不應。徐州刺史陶謙察朗茂才。

translations.literal: Wang Lang, courtesy name Jingxing, was a man of Donghai Commandery. Because he understood the Classics, he was appointed Gentleman of the Interior and made Chief of Ziqiu. He studied under Grand Commandant Yang Ci; when Ci died, he abandoned office and performed mourning dress. He was recommended as filial and incorrupt and summoned by the offices of the Excellencies, but did not respond. Tao Qian, Inspector of Xuzhou, examined Lang as flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang, courtesy name Jingxing, was from Donghai Commandery. Learned in the Classics, he was appointed Gentleman of the Interior and then Chief of Ziqiu. He had studied with Grand Commandant Yang Ci, and when Yang Ci died he left office to mourn him. Though recommended as filial and incorrupt and summoned by the Excellencies, he refused to serve, until Tao Qian, Inspector of Xuzhou, nominated him as an abundant talent.

sentences.zh: 時漢帝在長安，關東兵起，朗爲謙治中，與別駕趙昱等說謙曰：「春秋之義，求諸侯莫如勤王。今天子越在西京，宜遣使奉承王命。」

translations.literal: At the time the Han emperor was in Chang’an and troops had risen east of the passes. Lang was Qian’s Administrator, and with Administrative Aide Zhao Yu and others he persuaded Qian, saying, “In the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, in seeking the feudal lords nothing is like diligently serving the king. Now the Son of Heaven is away in the western capital; it is proper to send an envoy to receive and uphold the royal commands."
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor was in Chang’an and armies rose east of the passes, Wang Lang was Tao Qian’s Administrator. He and Zhao Yu urged Tao Qian, saying, “According to the Spring and Autumn tradition, nothing better summons the regional lords than loyal service to the king. Now the Son of Heaven is in the western capital; you should send envoys to receive and honor his commands."

sentences.zh: 謙乃遣昱奉章至長安。天子嘉其意，拜謙安東將軍。以昱爲廣陵太守，朗會稽太守。

translations.literal: Qian then sent Yu to present a memorial at Chang’an. The Son of Heaven commended his intention and appointed Qian General Who Pacifies the East. He made Yu Administrator of Guangling and Lang Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian accordingly sent Zhao Yu with a memorial to Chang’an. The Son of Heaven praised the gesture, appointed Tao Qian General Who Pacifies the East, made Zhao Yu Administrator of Guangling, and made Wang Lang Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 《朗家傳》曰：會稽舊祀秦始皇，刻木爲像，與夏禹同廟。朗到官，以爲無德之君不應見祀，於是除之。居郡四年，惠愛在民。

translations.literal: The Family Tradition of Lang says: Kuaiji had formerly sacrificed to the First Emperor of Qin, carving wood to make his image and placing him in the same temple as Yu of Xia. When Lang arrived in office, he thought that a ruler without virtue should not be seen in sacrifice, and thereupon removed it. He dwelt in the commandery for four years, and kindness and affection were among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Family Tradition of Wang Lang says that Kuaiji had long sacrificed to the First Emperor of Qin, with a wooden image set in the same temple as Yu of Xia. On taking office, Wang Lang judged that a ruler without virtue should not receive sacrifices and removed the image. During his four years in the commandery, the people felt his kindness.

sentences.zh: 孫策渡江略地。朗功曹虞翻以爲力不能拒，不如避之。朗自以身爲漢吏，宜保城邑，遂舉兵與策戰，敗績，浮海至東冶。

translations.literal: Sun Ce crossed the Yangzi and seized territory. Lang’s Merit Officer Yu Fan thought their strength could not resist him and that it would be better to avoid him. Lang himself considered that, since he was a Han official, he ought to defend the city and town; he then raised troops and fought Ce, was defeated, and floated by sea to Dongye.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce crossed the Yangzi and began taking territory, Wang Lang’s Merit Officer Yu Fan advised that they lacked the strength to resist and should withdraw. Wang Lang held that, as an officer of Han, he had to defend his city. He raised troops against Sun Ce, was defeated, and escaped by sea to Dongye.

sentences.zh: 策又追擊，大破之。朗乃詣策。策以朗儒雅，詰讓而不害。

translations.literal: Ce again pursued and attacked, greatly defeating him. Lang then went to Ce. Ce, because Lang was refined and scholarly, questioned and reproached him but did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce pursued and routed him again. Wang Lang then presented himself to Sun Ce, who respected his scholarly bearing, rebuked him, and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：孫策率軍如閩、越討朗。朗泛舟浮海，欲走交州，爲兵所逼，遂詣軍降。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Emperor Xian says: Sun Ce led his army to Min and Yue to campaign against Lang. Lang set boats afloat on the sea, wishing to flee to Jiaozhou, but was pressed by troops and thereupon went to the army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Emperor Xian says that Sun Ce led his army into Min and Yue to attack Wang Lang. Wang Lang took to the sea, intending to flee to Jiaozhou, but troops closed in and he surrendered at Sun Ce’s camp.

sentences.zh: 策令使者詰朗曰：「問逆賊故會稽太守王朗：朗受國恩當官，云何不惟報德，而阻兵安忍？大軍征討，幸免梟夷，不自埽屏，復聚黨衆，屯住郡境。遠勞王誅，卒不悟順。捕得云降，庶以欺詐，用全首領，得爾與不，具以狀對。」

translations.literal: Ce ordered an envoy to question Lang, saying, “We question the rebel bandit, former Administrator of Kuaiji Wang Lang: Lang received the state’s grace and occupied office; how could he not think only of repaying virtue, but instead blocked troops and settled in cruelty? When the great army campaigned, you were fortunate to escape exposure and execution, yet you did not sweep yourself away and hide; again you gathered followers and camped within the commandery’s borders. You made the royal punishment toil from afar and to the end did not awaken to submission. Now that you have been captured you say you surrender, hoping by deceit to preserve your head and neck. Whether this can be granted or not, answer fully according to the circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent an envoy to interrogate him: “We question Wang Lang, rebel and former Administrator of Kuaiji. You received the state’s favor and held office; why did you fail to repay that grace and instead stubbornly took up arms? When the great army marched, you escaped execution by luck, yet instead of disappearing you again gathered followers and occupied the commandery. You made royal punishment come from afar and still never understood submission. Now captured, you claim surrender, hoping deceit will save your head. State the facts fully, and we shall see whether this can be allowed."

sentences.zh: 朗稱禽虜，對使者曰：「朗以瑣才，誤竊朝私，受爵不讓，以遘罪網。

translations.literal: Lang called himself a captured prisoner and answered the envoy, saying, “Lang, with trifling talent, mistakenly stole the court’s private favor, received rank and did not decline, and thereby encountered the net of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Calling himself a captive, Wang Lang answered the envoy: “With my petty ability, I wrongly took the court’s favor and accepted rank without declining it, thereby falling into guilt.

sentences.zh: 前見征討，畏死苟免。因治人物，寄命須臾。又迫大兵，惶怖北引。從者疾患，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: Previously, seeing the campaign against me, I feared death and barely escaped. Relying on managing people and goods, I lodged my life for a brief while. Again pressed by a great army, in terror I drew north. My followers suffered illness, and the dead and lost were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign first came, I feared death and escaped by chance. I clung for a moment to men and supplies, then, pressed again by the army, fled north in panic. Illness struck my followers, and almost all died or scattered.

sentences.zh: 獨與老母共乘一欐，流矢始交，便棄欐就俘，稽顙自首於征役之中。朗惶惑不達，自稱降虜。緣前迷謬，被詰慙懼。

translations.literal: Alone with my old mother I shared one boat; when stray arrows first crossed, I then abandoned the boat and went to be captured, knocking my forehead and giving myself up amid the campaign. Lang was confused and did not understand, and called himself a surrendered captive. Because of my former delusion and error, when questioned I am ashamed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: I was alone with my aged mother in a single boat. As soon as arrows began to fly, I left the boat, submitted to capture, knocked my forehead to the ground, and gave myself up in the army. Confused and ignorant, I called myself a surrendered prisoner. Because of my earlier folly, I am ashamed and afraid under questioning.

sentences.zh: 朗愚淺駑怯，畏威自驚。又無良介，不早自歸。於破亡之中，然後委命下隷。

translations.literal: Lang is foolish, shallow, worn-out, and cowardly; fearing majesty, I frightened myself. Also, I had no good intermediary and did not early return myself. Only amid defeat and ruin did I then entrust my life to lower servitude.
translations.idiomatic: I am foolish, shallow, weak, and fearful; overawed by authority, I terrified myself. Having no proper intermediary, I failed to submit earlier, and only in defeat placed my life among the lowest servants.

sentences.zh: 身輕罪重，死有餘辜。申脰就鞅，蹴足入絆，叱咤聽聲，東西惟命。」

translations.literal: My body is light and my guilt heavy; in death I would have surplus blame. I stretch my neck to the yoke, kick my feet into the fetters, and at rebuke listen for the voice; east or west, I only obey commands."
translations.idiomatic: My person is slight and my guilt heavy; death would not exhaust my offense. I stretch my neck for the yoke and put my feet into the bonds; at a shout I await command, east or west as ordered."

sentences.zh: 雖流移窮困，朝不謀夕，而收卹親舊，分多割少，行義甚著。

translations.literal: Though he was displaced, destitute, and hard-pressed, unable in the morning to plan for the evening, yet he gathered and aided kin and old acquaintances, sharing out the much and cutting off the little; his conduct of righteousness was very manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Even in flight and poverty, with no certainty from morning to night, Wang Lang cared for relatives and old friends, sharing what he had and keeping little for himself. His righteous conduct was widely known.

sentences.zh: 太祖表徵之，朗自曲阿展轉江海，積年乃至。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized summoning him; Lang from Qu’e wound through rivers and seas, years accumulating before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao petitioned the throne to summon Wang Lang, who left Qu’e and spent years threading rivers and coasts before he reached the north.

sentences.zh: 〈朗被徵未至。

translations.literal: 〈Lang had been summoned but had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wang Lang was still en route when

sentences.zh: 孔融與朗書曰：「世路隔塞，情問斷絕，感懷增思。

translations.literal: Kong Rong wrote Lang a letter saying, “The world’s roads are blocked and cut; feeling and inquiry are severed—my thoughts increase with longing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong wrote: “The roads are blocked and news scarce, yet my thoughts go out to you.

sentences.zh: 前見章表，知尋湯武罪己之迹，自投東裔同鯀之罰，覽省未周，涕隕潸然。

translations.literal: Formerly seeing your memorial, I knew you would soon tread Tang and Wu’s blaming-themselves traces, casting yourself to the eastern fringe with Gun’s punishment—I had not finished reading when tears fell streaming.
translations.idiomatic: I read your memorial and saw you ready to imitate Tang and Wu’s self-reproach and accept exile like Gun—before I finished the page my tears were falling.

sentences.zh: 主上寬仁，貴德宥過。

translations.literal: The lord above is lenient and benevolent, honoring virtue and forgiving faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is merciful and values virtue over old faults.

sentences.zh: 曹公輔政，思賢並立。

translations.literal: Lord Cao assists the government, thinking of worthies and standing them together.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao governs with every wish to gather talent.

sentences.zh: 策書屢下，殷勤款至。

translations.literal: Commissioned documents have repeatedly descended, earnest and sincere to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: His summonses have gone out again and again, each more earnest than the last.

sentences.zh: 知櫂舟浮海，息駕廣陵，不意黃能突出羽淵也。

translations.literal: I know you rowed a boat across the sea, rested your carriage at Guangling—I did not expect the yellow bear to burst from Yu’s abyss.
translations.idiomatic: I heard you put to sea and halted at Guangling—I little thought you would drop from sight like the yellow bear from the abyss.

sentences.zh: 談笑有期，勉行自愛！」

translations.literal: Laughing talk will have its time—strive to go and love yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: We shall meet and laugh about this—take care of yourself until then!"

sentences.zh: 漢晉春秋曰：孫策之始得朗也，譴讓之。

translations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals states: When Sun Ce first got Lang, he rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Jin chunqiu records that when Sun Ce first seized Wang Lang he berated him,

sentences.zh: 使張昭私問朗，朗誓不屈，策忿而不敢害也，留置曲阿。

translations.literal: He sent Zhang Zhao privately to question Lang; Lang swore he would not yield; Ce was angry yet did not dare harm him, and detained him at Qu’e.
translations.idiomatic: sent Zhang Zhao to interrogate him in private. Wang Lang refused to submit; Sun Ce raged but dared not kill him and held him at Qu’e.

sentences.zh: 建安三年，太祖表徵朗，策遣之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jian’an, the Grand Progenitor memorialized summoning Lang; Ce sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: In 198 Cao Cao petitioned for Wang Lang’s recall, and Sun Ce let him go.

sentences.zh: 太祖問曰：「孫策何以得至此邪？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked, saying, “How did Sun Ce come to reach this point?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked him, “How did Sun Ce rise so high?"

sentences.zh: 朗曰：「策勇冠一世，有儁才大志。

translations.literal: Lang said, “Ce’s courage crowned a generation; he had outstanding talent and great intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang replied, “His courage was unmatched, his ambition immense,

sentences.zh: 張子布，民之望也，北面而相之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zibu is the people’s hope; he faced north and served as his minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao commanded the people’s respect and served him as chief minister,

sentences.zh: 周公瑾，江淮之傑，攘臂而爲其將。

translations.literal: Zhou Gongjin was a hero of the Jiang and Huai; he rolled up sleeves and became his general.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhou Yu was the pick of the Jiang-Huai region—he rolled up his sleeves and became Sun Ce’s general.

sentences.zh: 謀而有成，所規不細，終爲天下大賊，非徒狗盜而已。」〉

translations.literal: He plotted and had success; what he aimed at was not fine—in the end he became the realm’s great bandit, not merely a dog-thief.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: His schemes succeeded and his ambitions were large—he became a scourge to the empire, no common robber.”〉"

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫，參司空軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed consultant, joined the Minister of Works’ military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang was named consultant and joined Cao Cao’s staff as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 〈朗家傳曰：朗少與沛國名士劉陽交友。

translations.literal: 〈The Lang Family Tradition states: Lang in youth was friends with the noted man of Pei, Liu Yang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wang Lang family tradition records that in youth he befriended Liu Yang, a celebrated scholar from Pei.

sentences.zh: 陽爲莒令，年三十而卒，故後世鮮聞。

translations.literal: Yang was magistrate of Ju, age thirty when he died; therefore later ages seldom heard of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yang served as magistrate of Ju but died at thirty, so later generations barely knew his name.

sentences.zh: 初，陽以漢室漸衰，知太祖有雄才，恐爲漢累，意欲除之而事不會。

translations.literal: At first Yang because the Han house gradually declined, knew the Grand Progenitor had heroic talent, feared he would be a burden to Han, wished in intent to remove him but the affair did not coincide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han throne faltered, Liu Yang saw Cao Cao’s genius and feared he would doom the dynasty; he plotted assassination but never found the moment.

sentences.zh: 及太祖貴，求其嗣子甚急。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became noble, he sought Yang’s heir son very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao rose to power he hunted relentlessly for Liu Yang’s son.

sentences.zh: 其子惶窘，走伏無所。

translations.literal: His son was frightened and cornered, ran and hid with nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: The boy was terrified and fled from hiding place to hiding place.

sentences.zh: 陽親舊雖多，莫敢藏者。

translations.literal: Yang’s kin and old friends though many, none dared shelter him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Yang had many kinsmen and friends, none dared hide the youth.

sentences.zh: 朗乃納受積年，及從會稽還，又數開解。

translations.literal: Lang then took him in for accumulated years, and when returning from Kuaiji again several times opened and explained.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang sheltered him for years and, after returning from Kuaiji, repeatedly interceded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 太祖乆乃赦之，陽門戶由是得全。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor after a long time then pardoned him; Yang’s household gate thereby was preserved whole.〉
translations.idiomatic: At length Cao Cao pardoned the boy, and Liu Yang’s line survived.〉

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，以軍祭酒領魏郡太守，遷少府、奉常、大理。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was first established, he as army libationer concurrently held grand administrator of Wei commandery, was promoted grand coach of the household, chamberlain for ceremonials, and commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the kingdom of Wei he served as army libationer and concurrent governor of Wei commandery, then rose to superintendent of the household, chamberlain for worship, and commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 務在寬恕，罪疑從輕。

translations.literal: His task lay in leniency and forgiveness; when guilt was doubtful, he leaned toward the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: He emphasized mercy and, when guilt was uncertain, always chose the milder sentence.

sentences.zh: 鍾繇明察當法，俱以治獄見稱。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao was clear-sighted and hit the mark in law; both by ordering prisons were praised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was noted for legal precision; both men won praise as judges.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖請同會，啁朗曰：「不能效君昔在會稽折秔米飯也。」

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: the Grand Progenitor invited him to the same feast and teased Lang, saying, “You cannot imitate you, sir, in former days at Kuaiji breaking glutinous rice for food."
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe says Cao Cao once joked at a banquet: “You cannot match your old self in Kuaiji, pinching every grain of rice."

sentences.zh: 朗仰而歎曰：「宜適難值！」

translations.literal: Lang looked up and sighed, saying, “The right fit is hard to meet!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang looked up and sighed, “Times that suit a man are hard to find!"

sentences.zh: 太祖問：「云何？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked, “How so?"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor asked, “How so?"

sentences.zh: 朗曰：「如朗昔者，未可折而折；

translations.literal: Lang said, “As for Lang in former days, it was not yet possible to break yet I broke;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang replied, “In those days I could ill afford to stint yet I stinted;

sentences.zh: 如明公今日，可折而不折也。」

translations.literal: as for my enlightened lord today, it is possible to break yet you do not break."
translations.idiomatic: today you, my lord, could afford waste yet you do not waste."

sentences.zh: 太祖以孫權稱臣遣貢諮朗，朗荅曰：「孫權前牋，自詭躬討虜以補前愆，後疏稱臣，以明無二。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because Sun Quan had declared himself subject and sent tribute consulted Lang; Lang replied, saying, “In Sun Quan’s former note he himself falsely claimed personally punishing captives to make up for former faults; in a later memorial he declared himself subject to show he had no second mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan submitted tribute, Cao Cao asked Wang Lang’s opinion. Wang said, “Sun Quan’s first letter boasted of chastising rebels to atone for past errors; his later memorial declared vassalage to prove he had no second loyalty.

sentences.zh: 牙獸屈膝，言鳥告歡，明珠、南金，遠珍必至。

translations.literal: Fang-tooth beasts bend the knee; speaking birds announce joy; bright pearls and southern gold—distant treasures are sure to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Wild beasts kneel, auspicious birds sing, pearls and southern gold will flow in as tribute from afar.

sentences.zh: 情見乎辭，效著乎功。

translations.literal: Feeling appears in his phrases; effect shines in his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity shows in his words and deeds alike.

sentences.zh: 三江五湖，爲沼于魏，西吳東越，化爲國民。

translations.literal: The three rivers and five lakes become marshes for Wei; western Wu and eastern Yue transform into the state’s people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi heartland will become Wei’s marsh, and Wu and Yue will become your subjects.

sentences.zh: 鄢、郢旣拔，荊門自開。

translations.literal: When Yan and Ying are already taken, the Jingmen opens of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan and Ying fall, the gates of Chu will swing open.

sentences.zh: 席卷巴、蜀，形勢已成。

translations.literal: Rolling up Ba and Shu, the situation is already formed.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Shu will be swept in, and the strategic picture will be complete.

sentences.zh: 重休累慶，雜沓相隨。

translations.literal: Repeated blessings pile in celebration, mixed and crowding follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings will crowd in one upon another.

sentences.zh: 承旨之日，撫掌擊節。

translations.literal: On the day of receiving the decree, I clap palms and beat the measure.
translations.idiomatic: The day your edict arrives I shall clap my hands for joy.

sentences.zh: 情之畜者，辭不能宣。」〉

translations.literal: What feeling has stored up, phrases cannot declare.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: Words cannot express the fullness of my delight.”〉"

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，遷御史大夫，封安陵亭侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the king’s throne, he was promoted imperial counselor and enfeoffed as village marquis of Anling.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi became king he promoted Wang Lang to imperial counselor and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Anling.

sentences.zh: 上疏勸育民省刑曰：「兵起已來三十餘年，四海盪覆，萬國殄瘁。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial urging nurturing the people and sparing punishments, saying, “Since arms rose it has been more than thirty years; the four seas have been overturned and shaken; the myriad states are exhausted and withered.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on nurturing the people and lightening penalties: “Thirty years of war have shaken the empire and left every state exhausted.

sentences.zh: 賴先王芟除寇賊，扶育孤弱，遂令華夏復有綱紀。

translations.literal: Relying on the former kings’ cutting away bandits and thieves, supporting and nurturing the orphaned and weak, thereupon they ordered Huaxia again to have guiding threads.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to your father’s campaigns against rebels and his care for the helpless, the heartland again has law and order.

sentences.zh: 鳩集兆民，于茲魏土，使封鄙之內，雞鳴狗吠達於四境，蒸庶欣欣，喜遇升平。

translations.literal: They gathered the hundred myriad people on this Wei soil, so that within the borders of fief and borderland, cock-crow and dog-bark reached the four boundaries; the multitude steamed and was joyful, glad to meet rising peace.
translations.idiomatic: The people have gathered on Wei soil; cockcrow and dog bark reach every border; commoners rejoice in the return of peace.

sentences.zh: 今遠方之寇未賔，兵戎之役未息，誠令復除足以懷遠人，良宰足以宣德澤，阡陌咸脩，四民殷熾，必復過於曩時而富於平日矣。

translations.literal: Now the distant quarter’s bandits have not yet submitted; military service’s levies have not ceased; truly if orders of remission and exemption suffice to cherish distant men, good magistrates suffice to display virtue’s moisture, field paths are all repaired, the four peoples are abundant and thriving—one must again surpass former times and be richer than ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: The far rebels are not yet pacified and conscription continues; yet if tax relief wins the border peoples, honest magistrates spread your grace, fields are cleared, and the four orders of society thrive, we shall surpass even the old prosperity.

sentences.zh: 易稱勑法，書著祥刑，一人有慶，兆民賴之，慎法獄之謂也。

translations.literal: The Changes speaks of ordering law; the Document records auspicious punishments; one man has blessing, the hundred myriad rely on him—this is what is called being careful in law and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Yijing urges orderly laws, the Documents praise merciful justice—when the ruler is just, the people depend on him. That is true care in judgment.

sentences.zh: 昔曹相國以獄市爲寄，路溫舒疾治獄之吏。

translations.literal: Formerly Chancellor Cao took prisons and markets as his charge; Lu Wenshu hated clerks who ran prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shen left the markets to regulate themselves; Lu Wenshu inveighed against harsh jailers.

sentences.zh: 夫治獄者得其情，則無冤死之囚；

translations.literal: As for those who order prisons, if they obtain the truth of the case, then there are no prisoners who die wronged;
translations.idiomatic: When judges seek the truth, no innocent dies in prison;

sentences.zh: 丁壯者得盡地力，則無饑饉之民；

translations.literal: if able-bodied men can exhaust the land’s power, then there are no people who starve;
translations.idiomatic: when farmers till every acre, no one starves;

sentences.zh: 窮老者得仰食倉廩，則無餧餓之殍；

translations.literal: if the utterly old can look up and eat from granaries, then there are no corpses of starvation;
translations.idiomatic: when the aged are fed from public granaries, no one dies in the ditch;

sentences.zh: 嫁娶以時，則男女無怨曠之恨；

translations.literal: if marrying and taking wives are timely, then men and women have no resentment of being left unwed;
translations.idiomatic: when men and women marry in due season, none are left bitter and alone;

sentences.zh: 胎養必全，則孕者無自傷之哀；

translations.literal: if fetal nurture is sure to be complete, then the pregnant have no grief of harming themselves;
translations.idiomatic: when mothers are cared through pregnancy, none need fear miscarriage;

sentences.zh: 新生必復，則孩者無不育之累；

translations.literal: if the newborn is sure to be restored, then infants have no burden of not being reared;
translations.idiomatic: when infants survive, parents are spared the grief of losing them;

sentences.zh: 壯而後役，則幼者無離家之思；

translations.literal: if after being strong they then serve corvée, then the young have no thought of leaving home;
translations.idiomatic: when corvée waits until manhood, boys are not torn from their families;

sentences.zh: 二毛不戎，則老者無頓伏之患。

translations.literal: if two-hair does not do military service, then the old have no trouble of stumbling and prostrating.
translations.idiomatic: when gray-haired men are exempted from the ranks, the elderly are spared collapse on the road.

sentences.zh: 醫藥以療其疾，寬繇以樂其業，威罰以抑其彊，恩仁以濟其弱，振貸以贍其乏。

translations.literal: Use medicine to heal their illness, lighten corvée to give joy in their occupations, awesome punishments to check their strength, favor and benevolence to succor their weakness, relief loans to supply their want.
translations.idiomatic: Heal sickness with medicine, ease corvée to give livelihood, check the strong with stern law, lift the weak with kindness, lend grain to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 十年之後，旣笄者必盈巷。

translations.literal: After ten years, those who have already capped must fill the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years marriageable girls will crowd every lane.

sentences.zh: 二十年之後，勝兵者必滿野矣。」

translations.literal: After twenty years, those fit for arms must fill the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: In twenty years fit soldiers will fill every field."

sentences.zh: 及文帝踐阼，改爲司空，進封樂平鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, it was changed to Minister of Works; advance enfeoffment was village marquis of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: At Cao Pi’s accession Wang Lang became Minister of Works and was promoted to village marquis of Leping.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏名臣奏》載朗節省奏曰：「詔問所宜損益，必謂東京之事也。

translations.literal: 〈The Memorials of Wei’s Famous Ministers carries Lang’s austerity memorial, saying, “The edict asking what ought to be cut or added surely refers to Eastern Capital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei mingchen zou preserves Wang Lang’s memorial on retrenchment: “Your question on what to cut surely concerns Later Han practice.

sentences.zh: 若夫西京雲陽、汾陰之大祭，千有五百之羣，祀通天之臺，入阿房之宮，齋必百日，養犧五載，牛則三千，其重玉則七千；

translations.literal: As for Western Capital’s great sacrifices at Yunyang and Fenyin, the throng of fifteen hundred, sacrifice at the terrace that communicates with Heaven, entering Epang’s palace, fasts that must be a hundred days, raising sacrificial victims five years, oxen then three thousand, their heavy jade then seven thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Western Han’s mass sacrifices at Yunyang and Fenyin, fifteen hundred participants, the Tower of Heaven, Epang Palace, hundred-day fasts, five-year-old victims, three thousand oxen, seven thousand pieces of ritual jade—

sentences.zh: 其器，文綺以飾重席，童女以蹈舞綴；

translations.literal: as for vessels, patterned silk to ornament heavy mats, young girls to tread dance and hang tassels;
translations.idiomatic: brocaded silks for mats, child dancers for the rites,

sentences.zh: 釀酎必貫三時而後成，樂人必三千四百而後備；

translations.literal: brewed strong wine must pass through three seasons before it is complete; musicians must be three thousand four hundred before they are ready;
translations.idiomatic: wine aged three seasons, three thousand four hundred musicians,

sentences.zh: 內宮美人數至近千，學官博士七千餘人；

translations.literal: inner-palace beauties number nearly a thousand; erudite scholars of the academy more than seven thousand;
translations.idiomatic: nearly a thousand palace women, over seven thousand academy scholars,

sentences.zh: 中廄則騑騄駙馬六萬餘匹，外牧則扈養三萬而馬十之；

translations.literal: middle stables then bay and dappled team horses more than sixty thousand, outer pasture then attendant-raised thirty thousand and horses ten times that;
translations.idiomatic: sixty thousand team horses in the imperial stables, thirty thousand grooms in the outer pastures and ten times as many horses,

sentences.zh: 執金吾從騎六百，走卒倍焉；

translations.literal: Bearer of the gilded mace’s mounted escort six hundred, runners double that;
translations.idiomatic: six hundred mounted guards for the Bearer of the Gilded Mace and twice as many runners,

sentences.zh: 太常行陵赤車千乘，太官賜官奴婢六千，長安城內治民爲政者三千，中二千石蔽罪斷刑者二十有五獄。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies’ tomb procession red carts a thousand, Grand Provisioner’s gift of palace bond servants six thousand, within Chang’an city those who governed the people as officials three thousand, among two-thousand-bushel rank those who covered crimes and decided punishments had twenty-five prisons.
translations.idiomatic: a thousand red hearses for imperial tomb rites, six thousand palace slaves from the provisioner, three thousand petty officials in Chang’an, and twenty-five prisons for two-thousand-bushel officials.

sentences.zh: 政充事猥，威儀繁富，隆於三代，近過禮中。

translations.literal: Government was full and affairs numerous; awe-inspiring display was elaborate and rich—more lofty than the Three Dynasties, near exceeding what ritual allows.
translations.idiomatic: Government swelled beyond the Three Dynasties and far exceeded what ritual allows.

sentences.zh: 夫所以極奢吝，大抵多受之於秦餘。

translations.literal: As for the reason they reached utmost extravagance and stinginess, for the most part they largely received it from Qin’s leavings.
translations.idiomatic: That extravagance was mostly inherited from the Qin.

sentences.zh: 旣違繭栗愨誠之本，埽地簡易之指，又失替質而損文、避泰而從約之趣。

translations.literal: Already it violated cocoon-and-millet sincere simplicity’s root, swept the ground for simple ease’s aim, and again lost replacing substance and diminishing pattern, avoiding excess and following frugality’s drift.
translations.idiomatic: This already departs from the root of plain and sincere sacrifice, from the intention of simply sweeping the ground, and also loses the meaning of substituting substance for display, reducing ornament, avoiding excess, and following restraint.

sentences.zh: 豈夫當今隆興盛明之時，祖述堯舜之際，割奢務儉之政，除繁崇省之令，詳刑慎罰之教，所宜希慕哉？

translations.literal: Is it not what at this time of lofty rise and splendid clarity, when tracing Yao and Shun, cutting extravagance and pursuing thrift’s government, removing the many and honoring reduction’s orders, detailed punishments and careful penalties’ instruction, one ought to admire?
translations.idiomatic: In this present age of flourishing renewal and brilliant rule, when we take Yao and Shun as our models, cut away extravagance and pursue frugality, remove complexity and honor simplicity, and teach careful examination of crimes and cautious punishments, are these things what we ought to admire and long for?

sentences.zh: 及夫寢廟日一太牢之祀，郡國並立宗廟之法，丞相御史大夫官屬吏從之數，若此之輩，旣已屢改於哀、平之前，不行光武之後矣。

translations.literal: As for the daily one grand-ox sacrifice at the resting temple, the law of commanderies and kingdoms jointly erecting ancestral temples, the chief minister and imperial counselor’s offices’ clerks and followers’ numbers—matters of this sort—already they were repeatedly changed before Ai and Ping, and after Guangwu were not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: As for the daily grand-animal sacrifices in the sleeping temples, the law by which commanderies and kingdoms all established ancestral temples, and the numbers of officials, clerks, and attendants attached to the Chancellor and Imperial Counselor: matters of this kind had already been repeatedly changed before Emperors Ai and Ping and were no longer practiced after Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 謹按圖牒，所改秦在天地及五帝、六宗、宗廟、社稷，旣已因前代之兆域矣。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to maps and registers, what was changed from Qin in Heaven and Earth and the Five Thearchs, Six Honored Ones, ancestral temples, and altars of soil and grain—already they followed former ages’ spirit precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the maps and registers, the Qin institutions that were changed concerned Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, the Six Honored Ones, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; these had already followed the precincts of former ages.

sentences.zh: 夫天地則埽地而祭，其餘則皆壇而埒之矣。

translations.literal: As for Heaven and Earth, then sweep the ground and sacrifice; as for the rest, then all are earthen altars with low walls.
translations.idiomatic: For Heaven and Earth, one simply sweeps the ground and sacrifices; for the rest, all have altars and enclosing banks.

sentences.zh: 明堂所以祀上帝，靈臺所以觀天文，辟雍所以脩禮樂，太學所以集儒林，高禖所以祈休祥，又所以察時務，揚教化。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is the means to sacrifice to the High Lord; the Spirit Terrace is the means to observe Heaven’s patterns; the Ring Moat Hall is the means to cultivate ritual and music; the Imperial Academy is the means to gather the forest of scholars; the High Matchmaker is the means to pray for auspicious blessing; again it is the means to examine the season’s tasks and raise transformation’s instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is for sacrificing to the Lord on High; the Spirit Terrace is for observing the patterns of Heaven; the Biyong is for cultivating rites and music; the Imperial Academy is for gathering the forest of classicists; and the High Matchmaker is for praying for auspicious blessings. These are also means to examine the needs of the time and spread teaching and transformation.

sentences.zh: 稽古先民，開誕慶祚，舊時皆在國之陽，並高棟夏屋，足以肆饗射，望雲物。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity’s former people, opening and extending blessing’s fate—in old times all were on the state’s south side, together high ridge and summer roof, enough to spread feasting and archery, gaze at cloud omens.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the ancient people, when they opened and extended blessed fortune, these buildings in old times all stood south of the capital, with high beams and broad roofs, sufficient for feasting and archery and for observing clouds and phenomena.

sentences.zh: 七郊雖尊祀尚質，猶皆有門宇便坐，足以避風雨。

translations.literal: The seven suburban sacrifices though honored sacrifice still valued substance; still all had gate-houses and convenient seats, enough to avoid wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Although the seven suburban rites are honored sacrifices and value simplicity, they still all have gate buildings and convenient seats, enough to shelter from wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 可須軍罷年豐，以漸脩治。

translations.literal: One may wait until armies cease and years are bumper, then by degrees repair and order.
translations.idiomatic: We may wait until the armies are withdrawn and the harvests are abundant, and then gradually repair and arrange them.

sentences.zh: 舊時虎賁羽林五營兵，及衞士并合，雖且萬人，或商賈墯游子弟，或農野謹鈍之人；

translations.literal: Former times’ tiger-guard, feather-forest, five-camp troops, and guardsmen combined, though nearly ten thousand men, were either merchants’ fallen idle sons or careful dull men of the farms;
translations.idiomatic: The old Huben, Yulin, Five Camps troops, and guardsmen together numbered nearly ten thousand, yet some were the idle sons of merchants and traders, and others were cautious and dull men from the farms and fields;

sentences.zh: 雖有乘制之處，不講戎陣，旣不簡練，又希更寇，雖名實不副，難以備急。

translations.literal: although there were places that rode regulation, they did not drill battle formations; since they were neither picked nor trained, and seldom replaced in facing bandits—although name and reality did not match, it was hard to prepare for emergency.
translations.idiomatic: though there were places where they rode in imperial processions, they did not practice military formations. Since they were neither selected nor trained, and rarely replaced by men experienced against raiders, name and reality did not match, and they were difficult to rely on in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 有警而後募兵，軍行而後運粮，或乃兵旣乆屯，而不務營佃，不脩器械，無有貯聚，一隅馳羽檄，則三靣並荒擾，此亦漢氏近世之失而不可式者也。

translations.literal: When there was alarm then recruiting soldiers, when the army marched then transporting grain—or even troops long encamped yet not attending to camp farming, not repairing weapons, having no stores piled up—when from one corner a feathered dispatch flew, then three sides together were wasteland disturbed: this too is Han’s recent-age loss and cannot be taken as model.
translations.idiomatic: Only after alarms came were troops recruited, and only after armies marched was grain transported. Sometimes armies had been stationed for a long time, yet did not attend to camp farming, did not repair equipment and weapons, and had no stored reserves. If a feather dispatch rushed from one corner, three sides would all be thrown into desolation and disorder. This too was a recent failing of the Han house and cannot serve as a model.

sentences.zh: 當今諸夏已安，而巴蜀在畫外。

translations.literal: Now the various Xia are already secure, while Ba and Shu are outside the map.
translations.idiomatic: At present, the Chinese lands are already at peace, while Ba and Shu remain beyond our plans.

sentences.zh: 雖未得偃武而弢甲，放馬而戢兵，宜因年之大豐，遂寄軍政於農事。

translations.literal: Although we have not yet been able to lay aside arms and bundle armor, release horses and store weapons, one ought by the year’s great bumper to thereupon lodge military government in farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Although we cannot yet lay down arms, put armor away, release the horses, and store the weapons, we should take advantage of this year's great abundance and entrust military administration to agricultural work.

sentences.zh: 吏士小大，並勤稼穡，止則成井里於廣野，動則成校隊於六軍，省其暴繇，贍其衣食。

translations.literal: Clerks and soldiers great and small, together diligent in grain and reaping; at rest then they form well-and-field in the broad wilds; in motion then they form camp companies in the six armies; reduce their violent corvée, supply their clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and soldiers, great and small, should all diligently farm and harvest. At rest, they will form well-field hamlets across the broad plains; in motion, they will form companies and squads among the six armies. Reduce their harsh corvee and provide for their clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 易稱『恱以使民，民忘其勞；

translations.literal: The Changes says, “With joy to employ the people, the people forget their toil;
translations.idiomatic: The Yijing says, “Lead the people gladly and they forget fatigue;

sentences.zh: 恱以犯難，民忘其死』，今之謂矣。

translations.literal: with joy to brave difficulty, the people forget their death”—today’s is spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: lead them gladly into danger and they forget death”—that is what we need now.

sentences.zh: 粮畜於食，勇畜於勢，雖坐曜烈威而衆未動，畫外之蠻，必復稽顙以求改往而效用矣。

translations.literal: Grain stored in eating, courage stored in situation—although sitting you display fierce awe yet the host has not moved, the barbarians outside the map are sure again to knock forehead seeking to change the past and offer effect.
translations.idiomatic: When grain is stored in food and courage is stored in circumstances, then even if we merely sit displaying blazing authority and the masses have not yet moved, the barbarians beyond the frontier will surely again bow their foreheads and seek to change their past conduct and offer service.

sentences.zh: 若畏威效用，不戰而定，則賢於交兵而後威立，接刃而後功成遠矣。

translations.literal: If in fearing awe they offer effect, without battle then settled, then it is worthier than crossing weapons afterward to establish awe, meeting blades afterward to complete merit—far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: If they fear our majesty and offer service, and are settled without battle, this is far worthier than establishing authority only after exchanging blows and completing achievement only after blades meet.

sentences.zh: 若姦凶不革，遂迷不反，猶欲以其所虐用之民，待大魏投命報養之士，然後徐以前歌後舞樂征之衆，臨彼倒戟折矢樂服之羣，伐腐摧枯，未足以爲喻也。」〉

translations.literal: If the wicked and fierce do not reform, thereupon are lost and do not return, still wishing with the people they cruelly used to await Great Wei’s giving-life-and-repaying-nurture knights, afterward slowly with front-singing rear-dancing joyful-campaign host, facing that inverted halberds and broken arrows joyful-submission throng, cutting rotten and crushing withered—not enough to serve as comparison.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: If the wicked do not change, persist in delusion, and fail to return, and still wish to use the people they have abused against Great Wei's soldiers who offer their lives in repayment for its support, then afterward, with troops who sing before and dance behind in joyful campaign, we will face those who reverse their halberds, break their arrows, and gladly submit. Even cutting rot and crushing withered wood is not enough as a comparison.”〉"

sentences.zh: 時帝頗出游獵，或昏夜還宮。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor rather went out hunting, sometimes returning to the palace in dark night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often hunted and sometimes returned after dark.

sentences.zh: 朗上疏曰：「夫帝王之居，外則飾周衞，內則重禁門，將行則設兵而後出幄，稱警而後踐墀，張弧而後登輿，清道而後奉引，遮列而後轉轂，靜室而後息駕，皆所以顯至尊，務戒慎，垂法教也。

translations.literal: Lang submitted a memorial saying, “As for the Son of Heaven’s dwelling, without then ornament complete encirclement, within then double barred gates; about to march then set troops and afterward leave the screen, call the guard and afterward tread the steps, bend the bow and afterward ascend the carriage, clear the road and afterward draw the train, screen ranks and afterward turn the wheel hubs, quiet the chamber and afterward rest the horses—all these are the means to display the most honored, strive for caution and fear, hang down law’s instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang memorialized: “As for the dwelling of emperors and kings, outside it is adorned with surrounding guards, and inside the forbidden gates are made weighty. When the ruler is about to go out, troops are set in place before he leaves the curtain; the alarm is proclaimed before he treads the steps; bows are strung before he mounts the carriage; the road is cleared before the escort proceeds; ranks are arrayed as screens before the wheels turn; and the chamber is quieted before the carriage rests. All these are means to make supreme honor manifest, to devote care to caution, and to hand down law and instruction.

sentences.zh: 近日車駕出臨捕虎，日昃而行，及昏而反，違警蹕之常法，非萬乘之至慎也。」

translations.literal: Recently the imperial carriage went out to catch tigers, the sun slanting then proceeding, reaching dusk then returning—violating the constant law of cleared roads and cordons, not the utmost caution of the ten-thousand-chariot."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the imperial carriage went out to oversee the capture of tigers, setting out when the sun was slanting and returning at dusk. This violates the regular laws of warning and clearing the roads, and is not the utmost caution of a ruler of ten thousand chariots."

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「覽表，雖魏絳稱虞箴以諷晉悼，相如陳猛獸以戒漢武，未足以喻。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, saying, “Reading your memorial—even Wei Jiang’s citing the Yu ode to remonstrate Jin Dao, Xiangru’s stating fierce beasts to warn Han Wu are not enough to compare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: “Having read your memorial, I see that even Wei Jiang citing the Admonition of Yu to remonstrate with Duke Dao of Jin, or Sima Xiangru describing fierce beasts to warn Emperor Wu of Han, are not enough as comparisons.

sentences.zh: 方今二寇未殄，將帥遠征，故時入原野以習戎備。

translations.literal: Just now the two bandits are not yet extinguished; generals campaign far—therefore from time to time I enter the wilds to drill martial readiness.
translations.idiomatic: At present the two rebels have not yet been destroyed, and the generals and commanders are campaigning far away; therefore from time to time I enter the fields and wilds in order to practice military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 至於夜還之戒，已詔有司施行。」

translations.literal: As for the warning about returning at night, already I have ordered the offices to carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: As for the warning about returning at night, I have already ordered the offices concerned to carry it out."

sentences.zh: 〈王朗集載朗爲大理時上主簿趙郡張登：「昔爲本縣主簿，值黑山賊圍郡，登與縣長王儁帥吏兵七十二人直往赴救，與賊交戰，吏兵散走。

translations.literal: 〈The Wang Lang Collection carries when Lang was commandant of justice his memorial for chief clerk Zhang Deng of Zhao commandery: “Formerly as chief clerk of his home commandery, when Black Mountain bandits besieged the commandery, Deng with the magistrate Wang Jun led clerks and soldiers seventy-two men straight to go to the rescue, crossed weapons with bandits, clerks and soldiers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wang Lang Collection includes Lang's memorial, submitted when he was Commandant of Justice, on behalf of Zhang Deng, chief clerk from Zhao commandery: “Formerly, when he was chief clerk of his home county and the Black Mountain bandits besieged the commandery, Deng and the county magistrate Wang Jun led seventy-two clerks and soldiers straight to the rescue and fought the bandits. The clerks and soldiers scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 儁殆見害，登手格二賊，以全儁命。

translations.literal: Jun was nearly seen harmed; Deng with his hands fought two bandits, thereby preserving Jun’s life.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was nearly harmed, but Deng fought two bandits with his own hands and thereby preserved Jun's life.

sentences.zh: 又守長夏逸，爲督郵所枉，登身受考掠，理逸之罪。

translations.literal: Again he defended Magistrate Xia Yi, who was wronged by the regional inspector’s clerk; Deng personally received beating and torture, straightening Yi’s crime.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when he defended Magistrate Xia Yi, who had been wronged by the postal inspector, Deng himself underwent interrogation and beating in order to resolve Yi's crime.

sentences.zh: 義濟二君。

translations.literal: In righteousness he succored two lords.
translations.idiomatic: By righteousness he rescued two lords.

sentences.zh: 宜加顯異。」

translations.literal: One ought to add clear distinction."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Deng should be given manifest and exceptional distinction."

sentences.zh: 太祖以所急者多，未遑擢叙。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because what was urgent was many, had no leisure to promote and narrate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was too busy to promote him at once.

sentences.zh: 至黃初初，朗又與太尉鍾繇連名表聞，兼稱登在職勤勞。

translations.literal: Reaching the beginning of Huangchu, Lang again with Grand Commandant Zhong Yao jointly memorialized to inform the throne, also praising Deng’s diligent toil in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangchu Wang Lang and Grand Commandant Zhong Yao jointly recommended Zhang Deng’s faithful service.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「登忠義彰著，在職功勤。

translations.literal: An edict said, “Deng’s loyalty and righteousness shine clear; in office his merit is diligent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “Deng's loyalty and righteousness are manifest and clear, and in office he has been meritorious and diligent.

sentences.zh: 名位雖卑，直亮宜顯。

translations.literal: Though name and rank are low, his straight brightness ought to be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Although his name and rank are low, his upright brightness should be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 饔膳近任，當得此吏。

translations.literal: For provisioner’s near service, one ought to get this clerk.
translations.idiomatic: For the nearby office of providing meals, one ought to obtain this official.

sentences.zh: 今以登爲太官令。」〉

translations.literal: Now appoint Deng as grand provisioner.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: Now appoint Deng as Grand Provisioner.”〉"

sentences.zh: 初，建安末，孫權始遣使稱藩，而與劉備交兵。

translations.literal: At first, at the end of Jian’an, Sun Quan first sent envoys declaring himself a vassal, while crossing weapons with Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jian’an era Sun Quan first sent envoys acknowledging Wei while still fighting Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 詔議「當興師與吳并取蜀不」？

translations.literal: An edict ordered debate: “Should we raise troops together with Wu to take Shu or not?”
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for debate: “Should we raise troops together with Wu to take Shu, or not?”

sentences.zh: 朗議曰：「天子之軍，重於華、岱，誠宜坐曜天威，不動若山。

translations.literal: Lang debated, saying, “The Son of Heaven’s army weighs more than Mount Hua and Mount Dai; truly one ought to sit displaying Heaven’s awe, unmoved as a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang argued: “Imperial armies should rest like Mount Hua—awesome and still.

sentences.zh: 假使權親與蜀賊相持，搏戰曠日，智均力敵，兵不速決，當須軍興以成其勢者，然後宜選持重之將，承寇賊之要，相時而後動，擇地而後行，一舉可無餘事。

translations.literal: Suppose Quan personally with the Shu bandit locked in mutual hold, fought hand to hand many days, wisdom matched strength matched, troops not quickly decided—when one must raise the army to complete that situation, then it is fitting to choose a steady general, take the bandits’ choke point, watch the season afterward then move, choose ground afterward then go—one stroke can leave no leftover affair.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Quan and Shu stalemate until one side must be reinforced, then send a cautious general to strike the enemy’s vitals at the right moment—one blow will finish it.

sentences.zh: 今權之師未動，則助吳之軍無爲先征。

translations.literal: Now Quan’s troops have not yet moved; then the army that aids Wu has no reason to march first.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan has not yet moved; Wei has no cause to march first in his aid.

sentences.zh: 且雨水方盛，非行軍動衆之時。」

translations.literal: Moreover rain and water are just abundant; it is not the season for marching troops and moving hosts."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the rains are heavy—no season for a great campaign."

sentences.zh: 帝納其計。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，鵜鶘集靈芝池，詔公卿舉獨行君子。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu years, pelicans gathered at Lingzhi Pool; an edict ordered dukes and ministers to recommend men of solitary integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu, pelicans alighted on the Lingzhi Pool, and the court ordered the high ministers to nominate men of proven moral independence.

sentences.zh: 朗薦光祿大夫楊彪，且稱疾，讓位於彪。

translations.literal: Lang recommended Minister of the Household Yang Biao, and moreover claimed illness, yielding his seat to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang nominated Yang Biao, minister of the household, then pleaded illness and offered him his own post.

sentences.zh: 帝乃爲彪置吏卒，位次三公。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore for Biao set clerks and guards, rank placement next after the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assigned Yang Biao a full staff and protocol ranking just below the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕求賢於君而未得，君乃翻然稱疾，非徒不得賢，更開失賢之路，增玉鉉之傾。

translations.literal: An edict said, “We seek worthies from you yet have not obtained them; you then suddenly claim illness—not only do we not obtain worthies, you further open a road of losing worthies, increasing the jade handle’s tilt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: “We asked you for worthy men and you answer by resigning—not only do we lose your service, we risk losing the very path to talent and unsettling the state.

sentences.zh: 無乃居其室出其言不善，見違於君子乎！

translations.literal: Is it not dwelling in its chamber yet issuing words that are not good, being rejected by gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not read the classic warning: ill-considered speech brings the gentleman’s censure?

sentences.zh: 君其勿有後辭。」

translations.literal: You—do not have afterward declining words."
translations.idiomatic: Do not refuse us again."

sentences.zh: 朗乃起。

translations.literal: Lang thereupon rose.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang thereupon resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 孫權欲遣子登入侍，不至。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wished to send his son Deng to attend at court; he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had promised to send his heir Sun Deng to the Wei court as hostage, but the boy never came.

sentences.zh: 是時車駕徙許昌，大興屯田，欲舉軍東征。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage moved to Xuchang, greatly raised garrison farming, wished to raise the army and campaign east.
translations.idiomatic: The court had moved to Xuchang, expanded military colonies, and planned an eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 朗上疏曰：「昔南越守善，嬰齊入侍，遂爲冢嗣，還君其國。

translations.literal: Lang submitted a memorial saying, “Formerly Southern Yue kept good faith; Yingqi entered attendance; thereupon he became heir of the tomb, returned and lorded his state.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang memorialized: “When Nanyue kept faith, its prince Yingqi came to court as hostage, succeeded his father, and returned to rule.

sentences.zh: 康居驕黠，情不副辭，都護奏議以爲宜遣侍子，以黜無禮。

translations.literal: Kangju was arrogant and cunning; feeling did not match words; the protector-general’s memorial debated that it was fitting to send a hostage son, thereby demoting their lack of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju was arrogant and insincere—the protector-general rightly demanded a royal hostage to humble their discourtesy.

sentences.zh: 且吳濞之禍，萌於子入，隗嚻之叛，亦不顧子。

translations.literal: Moreover the disaster of Wu Pi sprouted from the son’s entering; Wei Xiao’s rebellion also did not care for the son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi’s revolt began with a hostage son, and Wei Ao rebelled without regard for his son’s safety.

sentences.zh: 往者聞權有遣子之言而未至，今六軍戒嚴，臣恐輿人未暢聖旨，當謂國家慍於登之逋留，是以爲之興師。

translations.literal: Formerly I heard Quan had words of sending a son yet he did not arrive; now the six armies are on alert; your servant fears the cart-men have not fully understood the sage edict, and will suppose the state is angry at Deng’s delay, and therefore for this raises troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan spoke of sending an heir but has not done so. With the host mobilized, common folk may think we march only because Sun Deng tarried—that misreads Your Majesty’s intent.

sentences.zh: 設師行而登乃至，則爲所動者至大，所致者至細，猶未足以爲慶。

translations.literal: Suppose the army marches and Deng then arrives—then what is stirred is very great, what is achieved is very fine—still it is not enough to be counted celebration.
translations.idiomatic: If we march and Sun Deng then appears, the stir will be immense for a trifling gain—hardly cause for rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 設其傲很，殊無入志，懼彼輿論之未暢者，並懷伊邑。

translations.literal: Suppose he is arrogant and stubborn, utterly without mind to enter—fearing those whose public opinion is not yet smooth, together harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If he defies us and never sends the boy, rumor will sour and resentment spread on every side.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲宜勑別征諸將，各明奉禁令，以慎守所部。

translations.literal: Your stupid servant thinks it fitting to order the various generals on separate expeditions each clearly to uphold prohibition orders, carefully to guard what they hold.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to instruct each commander to hold his lines, enforce discipline, and guard his sector.

sentences.zh: 外曜烈威，內廣耕稼，使泊然若山，澹然若淵，勢不可動，計不可測。」

translations.literal: Without display fierce awe; within broadly plow and reap; make it still as a mountain, placid as a deep pool—situation cannot be moved, plan cannot be fathomed."
translations.idiomatic: Show strength at the border, encourage farming within, stand immovable as a mountain and deep as a pool—let the enemy find no opening."

sentences.zh: 是時，帝以成軍遂行，權子不至，車駕臨江而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor because the completed army thereupon marched, Quan’s son did not arrive, the imperial carriage faced the Yangzi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched anyway; Sun Deng never arrived; the imperial train reached the Yangzi and turned back.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：車駕旣還，詔三公曰：「三世爲將，道家所忌。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Book states: After the imperial carriage had returned, an edict to the Three Dukes said, “Three generations as generals—what the Daoists taboo.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu records that after the withdrawal an edict told the Three Excellencies: “Three generations of generals is what Daoist lore forbids.

sentences.zh: 窮兵黷武，古有成戒。

translations.literal: Exhausting troops and abusing arms—the ancients had established warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Endless war was already condemned by the ancients.

sentences.zh: 況連年水旱，士民損耗，而功作倍於前，勞役兼於昔，進不滅賊，退不和民。

translations.literal: Moreover successive years of flood and drought, gentry and people diminished and worn, while works double those before, labor service combines with former times, advancing does not destroy bandits, retreating does not harmonize the people.
translations.idiomatic: Years of flood and drought have wasted the people while corvée doubles; we neither crush the foe nor comfort the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫屋漏在上，知之在下，然迷而知反，失道不遠，過而能改，謂之不過。

translations.literal: As for a roof leaking above, those who know are below—yet lost and knowing to return, missing the way is not far; having fault and able to change is called not faulting.
translations.idiomatic: The people see a leaking roof before the ruler does; to turn back from error is not far from the Way.

sentences.zh: 今將休息，棲備高山，沈權九淵，割除擯棄，投之畫外。

translations.literal: Now We will rest and cease, roost and prepare on high mountains, sink Quan in the nine abysses, cut away and cast aside, throw him outside the map.
translations.idiomatic: We shall rest the host, let Sun Quan stew in his marshes, and cast him beyond the pale.

sentences.zh: 車駕當以今月中旬到譙，淮、漢衆軍，亦各還反，不臘西歸矣。」〉

translations.literal: The imperial carriage ought this month’s middle to reach Qiao; Huai and Han’s mass armies also each return and go back, not waiting for la before returning west.”〉"
translations.idiomatic: This court will reach Qiao by mid-month; the Huai and Han armies will withdraw without waiting for the winter sacrifice.”〉"

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進封蘭陵侯，增邑五百，并前千二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, advance enfeoffment was Marquis of Lanling, adding registered households five hundred, together with former twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming promoted him to marquis of Lanling with five hundred new households, twelve hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 使至鄴省文昭皇后陵，見百姓或有不足。

translations.literal: He was sent to Ye to inspect Empress Wenzhao’s tomb; he saw commoners some of whom had insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched to Ye to visit Lady Bian’s tomb, he found the people still in want.

sentences.zh: 是時方營脩宮室，朗上疏曰：「陛下即位已來，恩詔屢布，百姓萬民莫不欣欣。

translations.literal: At that time they were just building and repairing palace chambers; Lang submitted a memorial saying, “Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, favor edicts have repeatedly been issued; the hundred surnames and myriad people none are not steaming with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Palace construction was under way. Wang Lang wrote: “Since your accession your benevolent edicts have gladdened every household.

sentences.zh: 臣頃奉使北行，往反道路，聞衆傜役，其可得蠲除省減者甚多。

translations.literal: Your subject recently received orders to go north; going and returning on the road, hearing the mass corvée labor, of what can be remitted, removed, and reduced there is very much.
translations.idiomatic: On my recent mission north I heard endless corvée calls—much of it could be cut or deferred.

sentences.zh: 願陛下重留日昃之聽，以計制寇。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty heavily to retain the sun-slanting’s hearing, to use planning to regulate bandits.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to heed the warning of the setting sun and plan against the enemy instead of taxing the people.

sentences.zh: 昔大禹將欲拯天下之大患，故乃先卑其宮室，儉其衣食，用能盡有九州，弼成五服。

translations.literal: Formerly the Great Yu about to wish to save the realm’s great calamity, therefore first humbled his palace chambers, was frugal in clothing and food, thereby able fully to possess the nine provinces and assist in completing the five domains.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yu saved the realm by living in a hut and eating coarse food until he mastered the nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 句踐欲廣其禦兒之疆，

translations.literal: Goujian wished to broaden his Yuer’s frontier,
translations.idiomatic: King Goujian meant to push his border at Yuer

sentences.zh: 〈禦兒，吳界邊戍之地名。〉

translations.literal: 〈Yuer is a Wu border garrison place name.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yuer was a Wu frontier post.〉

sentences.zh: 馘夫差於姑蘇，故亦約其身以及家，儉其家以施國，用能囊括五湖，席卷三江，取威中國，定霸華夏。

translations.literal: beheaded Fucha at Gusu; therefore also restrained his person extending to family, was frugal in his family to apply to the state, thereby able to wrap and hold the five lakes, roll up the three rivers, take awe in the central states, fix hegemony in Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: and slew King Fuchai of Wu at Gusu; he tightened his own household budget to feed the army, swallowed the five lakes and three rivers, and made the central states acknowledge his supremacy.

sentences.zh: 漢之文、景亦欲恢弘祖業，增崇洪緒，故能割意於百金之臺，昭儉於弋綈之服，內減太官而不受貢獻，外省傜賦而務農桑，用能號稱升平，幾致刑錯。

translations.literal: Han’s Wen and Jing also wished to expand the ancestors’ enterprise, increase and exalt the great thread; therefore they could cut intent at the hundred-gold terrace, display frugality in shooting-silk robes, within reduce the grand provisioner and not accept tribute, without reduce corvée taxes and strive at farming and mulberry, thereby able to be called rising peace, almost bringing punishments set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing of Han built on their forebears by scrapping costly towers, wearing plain robes, cutting palace budgets and tribute, easing taxes, and promoting tillage—hence their age neared the ideal of unused punishments.

sentences.zh: 孝武之所以能奮其軍勢，拓其外境，誠因祖考畜積素足，故能遂成大功。

translations.literal: The reason Emperor Wu was able to rouse his military power and broaden the outer marches was truly because grandfather and father stored and accumulated plain sufficiency, therefore able thereupon to complete great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu could conquer abroad only because Wen and Jing had filled the treasury first.

sentences.zh: 霍去病，中才之將，猶以匈奴未滅，不治第宅。

translations.literal: Huo Qubing, a middling-talent general, still because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, did not build a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Even Huo Qubing, a middling commander, refused a mansion while the Xiongnu lived.

sentences.zh: 明卹遠者略近，事外者簡內。

translations.literal: The enlightened take pity on what is far and sketch what is near; those who work on the outside simplify the inside.
translations.idiomatic: The wise spare the distant frontier by easing the interior.

sentences.zh: 自漢之初及其中興，皆於金革略寢之後，然後鳳闕猥閌，德陽並起。

translations.literal: From Han’s beginning to its middle revival, all were after metal and leather wars slightly rested, then phoenix towers piled high, Deyang rose together.
translations.idiomatic: Early and middle Han built their lofty towers only after the wars cooled.

sentences.zh: 今當建始之前足用列朝會，崇華之後足用序內官，華林、天淵足用展游宴，若且先成閶闔之象魏，使足用列遠人之朝貢者，脩城池，使足用絕踰越，成國險，其餘一切，且須豐年。

translations.literal: Now Jianshi’s front suffices to array court audiences; Chonghua’s rear suffices to order inner officials; Hualin and Tianyuan suffice to spread roaming feasts—if for now you first complete Changhe’s elephant Wei so it suffices to array distant men’s court tribute, repair city walls so they suffice to cut off climbing and crossing, complete the state’s defences, as for the rest one may wait for bumper years.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianshi halls already host court; Chonghua serves the harem; Hualin and Tianyuan suffice for pleasure—finish only the Changhe gate tower for barbarian envoys, strengthen the walls against raiders, and defer every other project to fat years.

sentences.zh: 一以勤耕農爲務，習戎備爲事，則國無怨曠，戶口滋息，民充兵彊，而寇戎不賔，緝熙不足，未之有也。」

translations.literal: One take diligent plowing and farming as the task, drill martial readiness as the affair—then the state has no resentful unwed, households increase and breed, people fill and troops are strong, yet if bandits and barbarians do not submit, splendid brightness not sufficing—there has never been such."
translations.idiomatic: Make farming and readiness your priorities and the people will multiply, the army strengthen, and rebels submit without extra glory—nothing less has ever failed."

sentences.zh: 轉爲司徒。

translations.literal: He was shifted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 時屢失皇子，而後宮就館者少，朗上疏曰：「昔周文十五而有武王，遂享十子之祚，以廣諸姬之胤。

translations.literal: At that time imperial sons had repeatedly been lost, and few women of the rear palace were going to the maternity chambers. Wang Lang submitted a memorial, saying, “In the past King Wen of Zhou had King Wu when he was fifteen, and so enjoyed the blessing of ten sons, broadening the descendants of the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time imperial sons had repeatedly been lost, and few women of the rear palace were going to the maternity chambers. Wang Lang submitted a memorial, saying, “In the past King Wen of Zhou had King Wu when he was fifteen, and thereafter enjoyed the blessing of ten sons, broadening the descendants of the Ji clan.

sentences.zh: 武王旣老而生成王，成王是以鮮於兄弟。

translations.literal: King Wu was already old when he begot King Cheng, and therefore King Cheng had few brothers.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu was already old when he begot King Cheng, and therefore King Cheng had few brothers.

sentences.zh: 此二王者，各樹聖德，無以相過，比其子孫之祚，則不相如。

translations.literal: These two kings each established sagely virtue, and neither surpassed the other, but if one compares the fortune of their descendants, they were not alike.
translations.idiomatic: These two kings each established sagely virtue, and neither surpassed the other; but if one compares the fortune of their descendants, they were not alike.

sentences.zh: 蓋生育有早晚，所產有衆寡也。

translations.literal: This is because in begetting and bearing there is early and late, and in offspring there are many and few.
translations.idiomatic: This is because in begetting and bearing there is early and late, and in offspring there are many and few.

sentences.zh: 陛下旣德祚兼彼二聖，春秋高於姬文育武之時矣，而子發未舉於椒蘭之奧房，藩王未繁於掖庭之衆室。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s virtue and fortune combine those of those two sages, but your age is already greater than Ji Wen’s when he raised Wu, while sons are not yet being lifted up from the inner chambers of pepper and thoroughwort, and feudatory kings are not yet numerous among the many rooms of the palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue and fortune combine those of those two sages, but your age is already greater than Ji Wen's when he raised Wu, while sons have not yet emerged from the inner chambers scented with pepper and thoroughwort, and feudatory kings are not yet numerous among the many rooms of the palace women.

sentences.zh: 以成王爲喻，雖未爲晚，取譬伯邑，則不爲夙。

translations.literal: If King Cheng is used as the comparison, it is not yet late; if Bo Yi is taken as the analogy, then it is not early.
translations.idiomatic: If King Cheng is used as the comparison, it is not yet late; if Bo Yi is taken as the analogy, then it is not early either.

sentences.zh: 周禮六宮內官百二十人，而諸經常說，咸以十二爲限，至於秦漢之末，或以千百爲數矣。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou has one hundred twenty inner officials in the six palaces, while the regular explanations of the various classics all take twelve as the limit; by the end of Qin and Han, some numbered them by the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou gives one hundred twenty inner officials for the six palaces, while the standard explanations of the various classics all take twelve as the limit; by the end of Qin and Han, some numbered them in the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 然雖彌猥，而就時於吉館者或甚鮮，明「百斯男」之本，誠在於一意，不但在於務廣也。

translations.literal: Yet even when they became more numerous and crowded, those who went at the proper time to the auspicious chambers were sometimes very few. This shows that the basis of “a hundred sons” truly lies in focused intent, not merely in striving for breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even when they became more numerous and crowded, those who went at the proper time to the auspicious chambers were sometimes very few. This shows that the basis of “a hundred sons” truly lies in singleness of purpose, not merely in seeking greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 老臣慺慺，願國家同祚於軒轅之五五，而未及周文之二五，用爲伊邑。

translations.literal: This old minister is anxiously sincere. I hope the state will share the blessing of Xuanyuan’s five times five sons and not fall short of King Wen of Zhou’s two times five; this is why I am troubled.
translations.idiomatic: This old minister speaks with anxious sincerity. I hope the state will share the blessing of Xuanyuan's five times five sons and not fall short of King Wen of Zhou's two times five; this is why I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 且少小常苦被褥泰溫，泰溫則不能便柔膚弱體，是以難可防護，而易用感慨。

translations.literal: Moreover, the very young often suffer from bedding and coverlets being too warm; when they are too warm, this does not suit tender skin and weak bodies, so they are difficult to protect and easily affected.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the very young often suffer when bedding and coverlets are too warm. Excessive warmth does not suit tender skin and weak bodies, so they become hard to protect and easily affected.

sentences.zh: 若常令少小之縕袍，不至於甚厚，則必咸保金石之性，而比壽於南山矣。」

translations.literal: If the padded robes of the very young are always kept from becoming too thick, then they will surely all preserve constitutions like metal and stone, and their longevity will compare with the Southern Mountain.”
translations.idiomatic: If the padded robes of the very young are always kept from becoming too thick, then they will surely all preserve constitutions like metal and stone, and their longevity will equal the Southern Mountain.”

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「夫忠至者辭篤，愛重者言深。

translations.literal: The emperor replied, “When loyalty is utmost, the words are earnest; when concern is weighty, the language is deep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, “When loyalty is utmost, the words are earnest; when concern is weighty, the language is deep.

sentences.zh: 君旣勞思慮，又手筆將順，三復德音，欣然無量。

translations.literal: You have taken the trouble to think carefully and have also written by your own hand to guide me rightly. Having read your virtuous words three times, I am immeasurably pleased.
translations.idiomatic: You have taken the trouble to think carefully and have written by your own hand to guide me rightly. After reading your virtuous words three times, I am pleased beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 朕繼嗣未立，以爲君憂，欽納至言，思聞良規。」

translations.literal: My heir has not yet been established, and you take this as your concern. I respectfully accept your perfect words and wish to hear good counsel.”
translations.idiomatic: My heir has not yet been established, and you take this as your concern. I respectfully accept your utmost words and wish to hear good counsel.”

sentences.zh: 朗著易、春秋、孝經、周官傳，奏議論記，咸傳於世。

translations.literal: Wang Lang wrote commentaries on the Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Zhou Offices, as well as memorials, discussions, treatises, and records; all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang wrote commentaries on the Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Zhou Offices, along with memorials, discussions, treatises, and records; all circulated in the world.
