sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：朗本名嚴，後改爲朗。

translations.literal: The Weilue says: Wang Lang’s original name was Yan; he later changed it to Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue says: Wang Lang’s original name was Yan; he later changed it to Lang.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：朗高才博雅，而性嚴整慷慨，多威儀，恭儉節約，自婚姻中表禮贄無所受。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Wang Lang had high talent and broad refinement, and his nature was stern, orderly, impassioned, and full of dignity. He was respectful, frugal, and restrained, and accepted no ritual gifts from affinal kin or maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says: Wang Lang had high talent and broad refinement, and by nature he was stern, orderly, impassioned, and dignified. He was respectful, frugal, and restrained, and accepted no ritual gifts from affinal kin or maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 常譏世俗有好施之名，而不卹窮賤，故用財以周急爲先。

translations.literal: He often criticized worldly customs for having the reputation of liking generosity while not caring for the poor and lowly, and therefore in using wealth he put first the relief of urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: He often criticized worldly custom for valuing a reputation for generosity while failing to care for the poor and lowly; therefore, when using wealth, he gave priority to relieving urgent need.

sentences.zh: 太和二年228年薨，謚曰成侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, 228, he died, and his posthumous name was Marquis Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe (228), he died, and his posthumous name was Marquis Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子肅嗣。

translations.literal: His son Su succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝分朗戶邑，封一子列侯，朗乞封兄子詳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen divided Wang Lang’s households and territory to enfeoff one son as a ranked marquis, but Wang Lang requested that his elder brother’s son Xiang be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wen divided Wang Lang's households and territory to enfeoff one son as a ranked marquis, but Wang Lang requested that his elder brother's son Xiang be enfeoffed instead.

sentences.zh: 肅字子雍。

translations.literal: Su, courtesy name Ziyong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, courtesy name Ziyong,

sentences.zh: 年十八，從宋忠讀太玄，而更爲之解。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he followed Song Zhong in reading the Supreme Mystery and moreover for it made a commentary.
translations.idiomatic: at eighteen studied the Taixuan jing under Song Zhong and wrote his own commentary.

sentences.zh: 〈肅父朗與許靖書云：肅生於會稽。〉

translations.literal: 〈Su’s father Lang in a letter to Xu Jing said: Su was born in Kuaiji.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wang Lang wrote Xu Jing that Wang Su was born in Kuaiji.〉

sentences.zh: 黃初中，爲散騎黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu years he was gentleman cavalier attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu he became gentleman cavalier attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was appointed regular attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 he was named regular attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 四年，大司馬曹真征蜀，肅上疏曰：「前志有之，『千里饋糧，士有饑色，樵蘇後爨，師不宿飽』，此謂平塗之行軍者也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Grand Marshal Cao Zhen campaigned against Shu; Su submitted a memorial saying, “Former records have it, ‘To haul grain a thousand li, soldiers have a hungry color; to gather firewood before cooking, the army does not lodge full’—this speaks of marching on level roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Grand Marshal Cao Zhen campaigned against Shu. Su submitted a memorial saying, “Former records have it, ‘When grain is transported a thousand li, soldiers show hunger in their faces; when firewood must be gathered before cooking, the army does not sleep with full bellies.’ This speaks of marching on level roads.

sentences.zh: 又況於深入阻險，鑿路而前，則其爲勞必相百也。

translations.literal: Moreover as for deeply entering blocked peril, chiseling a road and advancing, then its toil must mutually be a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: how much worse to cut roads through mountains where the labor multiplies a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 今又加之以霖雨，山坂峻滑，衆逼而不展，糧縣而難繼，實行軍者之大忌也。

translations.literal: Now moreover adding to it unending rain, mountain slopes steep and slippery, the host pressed and unable to spread, grain hung and hard to continue—this is truly the great taboo of marching armies.
translations.idiomatic: Add endless rain and treacherous slopes, cramped columns and broken supply—that is every general’s nightmare.

sentences.zh: 聞曹真發已踰月而行裁半谷，治道功夫，戰士悉作。

translations.literal: I hear Cao Zhen’s setting out already exceeds a month yet the march cuts only half a valley; road repair work, fighting soldiers all do it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen has marched over a month yet cleared only half a defile—his warriors spend their strength building roads.

sentences.zh: 是賊偏得以逸而待勞，乃兵家之所憚也。

translations.literal: This is the bandits on the contrary obtaining to be at ease while awaiting toil—what military families fear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the enemy rests while we exhaust ourselves—the worst position in war.

sentences.zh: 言之前代，則武王伐紂，出關而復還；

translations.literal: Speaking of former ages, then King Wu punished Zhou, left the passes and again returned;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu once turned back from his march against Shang;

sentences.zh: 論之近事，則武、文征權，臨江而不濟。

translations.literal: speaking of recent matters, then Wu and Wen campaigned against Quan, faced the Yangzi and did not ford.
translations.idiomatic: your father and grandfather halted at the Yangzi against Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 豈非所謂順天知時，通於權變者哉！

translations.literal: Is this not what is called obeying Heaven and knowing the season, penetrating in power to change!
translations.idiomatic: Were they not obeying Heaven and knowing when to yield?

sentences.zh: 兆民知聖上以水雨艱劇之故，休而息之，後日有釁，乘而用之，則所謂恱以犯難，民忘其死者矣。」

translations.literal: The hundred omens will know the sage above because of rain’s hard toil’s reason, rest and cease them; a later day will have a rift, ride and use them—then what is called with joy to brave difficulty, the people forget their death."
translations.idiomatic: Let the people see you halt for rain and they will trust you; when a real opening comes they will follow you gladly into death."

sentences.zh: 於是遂罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 又上疏：「宜遵舊禮，爲大臣發哀，薦果宗廟。」

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial: “One ought to follow old ritual, for great ministers sound mourning, present fruit at the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: Again he submitted a memorial: “One ought to follow old ritual, for great ministers sound mourning, present fruit at the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: The matters all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne adopted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 又上疏陳政本曰：「除無事之位，損不急之祿，止因食之費，并從容之官；

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial stating the government’s root, saying, “Remove offices without business, cut salaries not urgent, stop redundant eaters’ expense, merge easygoing officials;
translations.idiomatic: Again he submitted a memorial setting out the root of government, saying, “Remove offices that have no business, cut salaries that are not urgent, stop the expense of dependent eaters, and merge idle offices;

sentences.zh: 使官必有職，職任其事，事必受祿，祿代其耕，乃往古之常式，當今之所宜也。

translations.literal: make offices sure to have duties, duties charge their affairs, affairs sure to receive salary, salary replaces their plowing—this is former antiquity’s constant pattern, what the present ought to follow.
translations.idiomatic: let every office have a duty, every duty a salary, every salary earned like a farmer’s crop—that was the ancient norm and should be ours.

sentences.zh: 官寡而祿厚，則公家之費鮮，進仕之志勸。

translations.literal: If offices are few and salaries thick, then the ducal house’s expense is little, advancing to office’s intent is encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer posts and richer pay lighten the treasury and encourage talent.

sentences.zh: 進仕之志勸，各展才力，莫相倚仗。

translations.literal: If advancing to office’s intent is encouraged, each displays talent and strength, none leans on another.
translations.idiomatic: When pay is ample, men exert themselves instead of leaning on patrons.

sentences.zh: 敷奏以言，明試以功，能之與否，簡在帝心。

translations.literal: Spread memorials with words, clearly test with merit; able or not, the choice lies in the Emperor’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: Let memorials speak and merit tests decide—success or failure rests with the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是以唐、虞之設官分職，申命公卿，各以其事，然後惟龍爲納言，猶今尚書也，以出內帝命而已。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang and Yu’s setting offices and dividing duties, repeatedly charging dukes and ministers, each with his affair, afterward only Long was receiver of words, like today’s Masters of Writing, to issue and receive the Emperor’s commands only.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun each minister had a task; only Long as “receiver of words” resembled today’s director of the Masters of Writing, passing the ruler’s orders.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷不可得而詳。

translations.literal: Xia and Yin cannot be obtained and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Shang records are too scant for detail.

sentences.zh: 甘誓曰『六事之人』，明六卿亦典事者也。

translations.literal: The Gan oath says “men of the six affairs”—showing the six ministers also superintend affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The oath of Gan names “the six ministers”—proof that the six high ministers each held real duties.

sentences.zh: 周官則備矣，五日視朝，公卿大夫並進，而司士辨其位焉。

translations.literal: Zhou’s offices then were complete; every five days they viewed court; dukes, ministers, and grandees together advanced, and the officer of scholars distinguished their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou held full court every five days; the master of appointments ranked every attendee.

sentences.zh: 其記曰：『坐而論道，謂之王公；

translations.literal: Its record says, “Sitting and discussing the Way—called kings and dukes;
translations.idiomatic: The classic says, “Those who sit and discuss policy are kings and dukes;

sentences.zh: 作而行之，謂之士大夫。』

translations.literal: acting and carrying it out—called grandees and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: those who carry it out are the ministers."

sentences.zh: 及漢之初，依擬前代，公卿皆親以事升朝。

translations.literal: Reaching Han’s beginning, modeling on former ages, dukes and ministers all in person by affairs ascended court.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han modeled antiquity: every high minister attended court in person.

sentences.zh: 故高祖躬追反走之周昌，武帝遙可奉奏之汲黯，宣帝使公卿五日一朝，成帝始置尚書五人。

translations.literal: Therefore Gaozu in person pursued the fleeing Zhou Chang; Emperor Wu from afar approved the memorial-presenting Ji An; Emperor Xuan ordered dukes and ministers once every five days to attend court; Emperor Cheng first set the Masters of Writing at five men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Gaozu personally pursued Zhou Chang when he fled back; Emperor Wu approved Ji An's presented memorial from afar; Emperor Xuan had the dukes and ministers attend court once every five days; and Emperor Cheng first established the five Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 自是陵遲，朝禮遂闕。

translations.literal: From this decline and delay, court ritual thereupon was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations let that discipline slip.

sentences.zh: 可復五日視朝之儀，使公卿尚書各以事進。

translations.literal: One may restore the five-day court-viewing ceremony, causing dukes, ministers, and Masters of Writing each to advance by affair.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the five-day audience and require each minister to report on his portfolio.

sentences.zh: 廢禮復興，光宣聖緒，誠所謂名美而實厚者也。」

translations.literal: Abolished ritual again rises, spreads and displays the sage thread—this is truly what is called a beautiful name with thick substance."
translations.idiomatic: Reviving that practice would honor the sage kings in both name and deed."

sentences.zh: 青龍中，山陽公薨，漢主也。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong years, the Duke of Shanyang died—he was the Han lord.
translations.idiomatic: During Qinglong the Duke of Shanyang—the abdicated Han emperor—died.

sentences.zh: 肅上疏曰：「昔唐禪虞，虞禪夏，皆終三年之喪，然後踐天子之尊。

translations.literal: Su submitted a memorial saying, “Formerly Tang yielded to Yu, Yu yielded to Xia, all ended three years’ mourning, afterward then trod the Son of Heaven’s honor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su wrote: “When Yao yielded to Shun and Shun to Yu, each observed three years’ mourning before taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 是以帝號無虧，君禮猶存。

translations.literal: Therefore the imperial title had no flaw, lord ritual still existed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the imperial dignity stayed intact and courtesy to the former ruler remained.

sentences.zh: 今山陽公承順天命，允荅民望，進禪大魏，退處賔位。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Shanyang obeyed and followed Heaven’s mandate, truly answered the people’s hope, advanced and yielded to Great Wei, withdrew and dwelt in guest seat.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Duke of Shanyang accepted and followed Heaven's mandate, truly answered the people's hopes, advanced and yielded the throne to Great Wei, then withdrew and occupied the position of guest.

sentences.zh: 公之奉魏，不敢不盡節。

translations.literal: The duke’s serving Wei did not dare not exhaust utmost duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Duke's service to Wei, he did not dare fail to exhaust his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魏之待公，優崇而不臣。

translations.literal: Wei’s treating the duke was generous and exalted yet not treating him as subject.
translations.idiomatic: In its treatment of the Duke, Wei honored and exalted him without making him a subject.

sentences.zh: 旣至其薨，櫬斂之制，輿徒之飾，皆同之於王者，是故遠近歸仁，以爲盛美。

translations.literal: Already reaching his death, coffining and dressing rites, carriage and follower ornament, all were the same as for kings—therefore far and near returned to benevolence, taking it as splendid beauty.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to die, the rules for coffin and shroud and the ornament of carriage and followers were all made the same as for a king. Therefore far and near returned to benevolence and regarded it as splendid beauty.

sentences.zh: 且漢緫帝皇之號，號曰皇帝。

translations.literal: Moreover Han gathered the emperor’s title, the title being called emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han combined the titles di and huang and called the title huangdi.

sentences.zh: 有別稱帝，無別稱皇，則皇是其差輕者也。

translations.literal: There was a separate title di; there was no separate title huang—then huang is the one that is the lighter gradation.
translations.idiomatic: There are separate cases of calling someone di, but no separate case of calling someone huang; therefore huang is the lighter distinction.

sentences.zh: 故當高祖之時，土無二王，其父見在而使稱皇，明非二王之嫌也。

translations.literal: Therefore at Gaozu’s time, within the land there were not two kings; his father was still alive yet made him called huang—showing it was not the suspicion of two kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu honored his living father as “Supreme Emperor,” no one thought two thrones existed.

sentences.zh: 況今以贈終，可使稱皇以配其謚。」

translations.literal: Moreover now using burial’s end, one may make him called huang to match his posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: At his death we may call him huang to match his posthumous name."

sentences.zh: 明帝不從使稱皇，乃追謚曰漢孝獻皇帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming did not follow making him called huang; thereupon pursued posthumous title as Han Filial and Presented Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming refused the huang title but posthumously named him Emperor Xian of Han.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：化合神者曰皇，德合天者曰帝。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: He who blends with the spirits is called huang; he whose virtue blends with Heaven is called di.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng said: “Huang” names union with the spirits; “di” names union with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是故三皇創號，五帝次之。

translations.literal: Therefore the Three Huang founded titles, the Five Di came next.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Three Sovereigns took huang first and the Five Thearchs took di afterward.

sentences.zh: 然則皇之爲稱，妙於帝矣。

translations.literal: Thus then as for huang as title, it is subtler than di.
translations.idiomatic: By that logic huang is the loftier title, not the lesser.

sentences.zh: 肅謂爲輕，不亦謬乎！

translations.literal: Su calling it light—is it not mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: For Wang Su to call huang the lighter term is absurd!

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲上古謂皇皇后帝，次言三、五，先皇後帝，誠如盛言。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that in high antiquity they called huang and later di; next speaking of three and five, first huang later di—indeed as Sheng said.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that antiquity paired huanghou with di and spoke of “three sovereigns, five thearchs” in that order—Sun Sheng was right about that.

sentences.zh: 然漢氏諸帝，雖尊父爲皇，其實則貴而無位，高而無民，比之於帝，得不謂之輕乎！

translations.literal: Yet Han’s various emperors, although honoring fathers as huang, in truth then noble yet without position, high yet without people—compared to di, can it not be called lighter!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han “supreme emperors” were fathers without thrones or subjects—surely that was a lesser huang than a ruling di!

sentences.zh: 魏因漢禮，名號無改。

translations.literal: Wei followed Han ritual; titles were not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei followed Han precedent without renaming.

sentences.zh: 孝獻之崩，豈得遠考古義？

translations.literal: When Filial and Presented collapsed, how could one far seek ancient meanings?
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xian’s death there was no need to revive archaic definitions.

sentences.zh: 肅之所云，蓋就漢制而爲言耳。

translations.literal: What Su spoke was roughly taking Han institutions as the words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su argued from Han usage alone.

sentences.zh: 謂之爲謬，乃是譏漢，非難肅也。〉

translations.literal: Calling it mistaken is then criticizing Han, not refuting Su.〉
translations.idiomatic: To call him wrong is to fault the Han system, not Wang Su.〉

sentences.zh: 後肅以常侍領祕書監，兼崇文觀祭酒。

translations.literal: Later Su as regular attendant concurrently held director of the secretariat, concurrently libationer of the Chongwen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Su served as regular attendant, director of the palace library, and libationer of the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 景初間，宮室盛興，民失農業，期信不敦，刑殺倉卒。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu interval, palace chambers flourished in building; the people lost farming occupation; appointed trust was not thick; punishments and killings were hasty.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu palace building ran wild, farmers were pulled from the fields, promises went unkept, and executions grew rash.

sentences.zh: 肅以疏曰：「大魏承百王之極，生民無幾，干戈未戢，誠宜息民而惠之以安靜遐邇之時也。

translations.literal: Su by memorial said, “Great Wei inherits the hundred kings’ utmost; the living people are not many; shields and spears are not yet stored away; truly it is fitting to rest the people and favor them with quiet—this is the time to quiet the far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su wrote: “Wei succeeds exhausted dynasties; the people are few and arms still bare—this is the hour to let them breathe.

sentences.zh: 夫務畜積而息疲民，在於省傜役而勤稼穡。

translations.literal: As for the task of storing accumulation and resting weary people, it lies in reducing corvée labor and being diligent in grain and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: To rebuild stores and revive the weary, cut corvée and put every hand to the plow.

sentences.zh: 今宮室未就，功業未訖，運漕調發，轉相供奉。

translations.literal: Now palace chambers are not yet finished, merit works are not yet ended, transport by water and levies issue, turning in relays to supply one another.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces are still rising, projects unfinished, and grain barges and levies shuttle endlessly to feed the work gangs.

sentences.zh: 是以丁夫疲於力作，農者離其南畒，種穀者寡，食穀者衆，舊穀旣沒，新穀莫繼。

translations.literal: Therefore corvée men are weary in laboring work; farmers leave their southern acres; those who sow grain are few, those who eat grain are many; old grain is already gone, new grain does not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers are exhausted, fields lie empty, sowers are few and eaters many—old granaries are bare and no new harvest follows.

sentences.zh: 斯則有國之大患，而非備豫之長策也。

translations.literal: This then is a great calamity for a state possessing, and not a long plan of preparation.
translations.idiomatic: That is a mortal danger to the realm, not prudent foresight.

sentences.zh: 今見作者三四萬人，九龍可以安聖體，其內足以列六宮，顯陽之殿，又向將畢，惟泰極已前，功夫尚大，方向盛寒，疾疢或作。

translations.literal: Now those seen working are thirty or forty thousand men; Jiulong can settle the sage body, within it suffices to array the six palaces; Xianyang’s hall moreover is about to be finished; only before the Grand Ultimate the work effort is still great, the direction is peak cold—sickness may arise.
translations.idiomatic: Some forty thousand builders swarm the site; the Jiulong complex can house the throne, the six palaces fit within it, Xianyang hall is nearly done—only the Taichi wing still needs heavy work in the depths of winter, when disease spreads.

sentences.zh: 誠願陛下發德音，下明詔，深愍役夫之疲勞，厚矜兆民之不贍，取常食廩之士，非急要者之用，選其丁壯，擇留萬人，使一朞而更之，咸知息代有日，則莫不恱以即事，勞而不怨矣。

translations.literal: Truly I wish Your Majesty to issue virtuous pronouncements, send down clear edicts, deeply pity the corvée men’s weariness, generously pity the hundred omens’ insufficiency, take from among the gentlemen who eat regular granary—those not urgently needed—select their able-bodied, choose and retain ten thousand men, make them rotate after one year, all knowing rest and replacement have a day—then none will not joyfully attend the work, toiling yet without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Issue edicts of mercy: spare the exhausted builders, pity the hungry populace, strip nonessential salaried posts, pick ten thousand stout workers on one-year rotations so every man knows relief is coming—then they will labor gladly.

sentences.zh: 計一歲有三百六十萬夫，亦不爲少。

translations.literal: Counting one year having three million six hundred thousand corvée days, it is also not few.
translations.idiomatic: That still yields 3.6 million man-days a year—no small force.

sentences.zh: 當一歲成者，聽且三年。

translations.literal: What ought to be finished in one year, permit meanwhile three years.
translations.idiomatic: Work slated for one year may stretch to three.

sentences.zh: 分遣其餘，使皆即農，無窮之計也。

translations.literal: Divide and dispatch the rest, causing all to take up farming—this is the plan without end.
translations.idiomatic: Send the rest back to the fields—that is the inexhaustible policy.

sentences.zh: 倉有溢粟，民有餘力：以此興功，何功不立？

translations.literal: Granaries have overflowing grain, the people have surplus strength—with this to raise works, what work will not stand?
translations.idiomatic: With full bins and rested farmers any project can succeed.

sentences.zh: 以此行化，何化不成？

translations.literal: With this to carry transformation, what transformation will not complete?
translations.idiomatic: With that moral authority any reform will take root.

sentences.zh: 夫信之於民，國家大寶也。

translations.literal: As for trust in the people—it is the state’s great treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The people’s trust is the state’s greatest treasure.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：『自古皆有死，民非信不立。』

translations.literal: Zhongni said, “From antiquity all have death; the people, if without trust, do not stand."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, “Since antiquity death has been inevitable, but a people without trust cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 夫區區之晉國，微微之重耳，欲用其民，先示以信，是故原雖將降，顧信而歸，用能一戰而霸，于今見稱。

translations.literal: As for the petty Jin state, the slight Chong’er, wishing to use his people, first displayed trust to them; therefore though Yuan was about to surrender, he looked to trust and returned, thereby able in one battle to become hegemon—down to today he is praised.
translations.idiomatic: Tiny Jin and exiled Chong’er won the realm only by proving trustworthy—even Yuan’s city opened when the duke kept faith, and one battle made him hegemon.

sentences.zh: 前車駕當幸洛陽，發民爲營，有司命以營成而罷。

translations.literal: Formerly when the imperial carriage was about to favor Luoyang, it raised the people to make camps; the offices ordered that when the camps were finished they would stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved toward Luoyang it drafted peasants for camp labor with a promise to release them when the camps were done.

sentences.zh: 旣成，又利其功力，不以時遣。

translations.literal: Already finished, again they profited from their labor power, not sending them away in due time.
translations.idiomatic: The work finished, officials kept them for further labor instead of letting them go.

sentences.zh: 有司徒營其目前之利，不顧經國之體。

translations.literal: There are ministers who only seek profit before their eyes, not considering the body politic’s wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers eye short-term gain and ignore the health of the state.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲自今已後，儻復使民，宜明其令，使必如期。

translations.literal: Your stupid servant thinks from now on, if again employing the people, it is fitting to clarify the order, making them sure to match the term.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every levy should carry a fixed term announced in advance.

sentences.zh: 若有事以次，寧復更發，無或失信。

translations.literal: If there are affairs in sequence, better again issue a call—do not break trust.
translations.idiomatic: If more labor is needed, issue a fresh order rather than break your word.

sentences.zh: 凡陛下臨時之所行刑，皆有罪之吏，宜死之人也。

translations.literal: Generally the punishments Your Majesty on the moment carries out are all guilty clerks, men who ought to die.
translations.idiomatic: Those you execute on the spot are criminals who deserve death.

sentences.zh: 然衆庶不知，謂爲倉卒。

translations.literal: Yet the multitude does not know, calling it hasty.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd does not know their guilt and calls it rash killing.

sentences.zh: 故願陛下下之於吏而暴其罪。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish Your Majesty to hand them down to the clerks and expose their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Let the judiciary try them publicly and publish their crimes.

sentences.zh: 鈞其死也，無使汙于宮掖而爲遠近所疑。

translations.literal: Even out their death; do not let them be defiled in the palace women’s quarters and become suspected by far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Execute them outside the harem so the palace is not stained with blood and rumor does not spread.

sentences.zh: 且人命至重，難生易殺，氣絕而不續者也，是以聖賢重之。

translations.literal: Moreover human life is utmost weight—hard to live, easy to kill; breath cut off and not continued—therefore sages and worthies value it.
translations.idiomatic: Life is hard to restore and easy to take—sages honor it accordingly.

sentences.zh: 孟軻稱殺一無辜以取天下，仁者不爲也。

translations.literal: Meng Ke said killing one innocent to take the realm—the benevolent man does not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said no benevolent man kills one innocent to win the empire.

sentences.zh: 漢時有犯蹕驚乘輿馬者，廷尉張釋之奏使罰金，文帝恠其輕，而釋之曰：『方其時，上使誅之則已。

translations.literal: In Han times there was one who violated the cordon and startled the imperial carriage’s horses; Commandant of Justice Zhang Shizhi memorialized to have him fined in gold; Emperor Wen thought it light and was strange, but Shizhi said, “At that moment, had the sovereign ordered him executed it would have been done.
translations.idiomatic: When a man startled Emperor Wen’s horses, Zhang Shizhi fined him; Wen thought the fine too light, but Shizhi said, “You could have had him killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 今下廷尉。

translations.literal: Now send him down to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you sent him to me.

sentences.zh: 廷尉，天下之平也，一傾之，天下用法皆爲輕重，民安所措其手足？』

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice is the realm’s balance—once tilted, all punishments under Heaven become light or heavy—where will the people place hands and feet?"
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice is the scale of the law; tip it once and every magistrate skews verdicts—where can the people find safety?"

sentences.zh: 臣以爲大失其義，非忠臣所宜陳也。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks this greatly loses its meaning; it is not what a loyal minister ought to state.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Shizhi twisted the point; that was no loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 廷尉者，天子之吏也，猶不可以失平，而天子之身，反可以惑謬乎？

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice is the Son of Heaven’s clerk—still he may not lose balance—yet the Son of Heaven’s person, on the contrary, may be deluded and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If even the commandant of justice may not bend the law, may the Son of Heaven act on whim?

sentences.zh: 斯重於爲己，而輕於爲君，不忠之甚也。

translations.literal: This values heavily acting for oneself and lightly acting for the lord—utmost disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: That exalts private reputation above the ruler’s duty—profound disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 周公曰：『天子無戲言；

translations.literal: Zhou Gong said, “The Son of Heaven has no jesting words;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou said, “The Son of Heaven does not joke;

sentences.zh: 言則史書之，工誦之，士稱之。』

translations.literal: when he speaks, then the scribe records it, craftsmen chant it, scholars praise it."
translations.idiomatic: when he speaks, scribes record it, artisans chant it, scholars repeat it."

sentences.zh: 言猶不戲，而况行之乎？

translations.literal: Speech still is not jesting—how much more carrying it out!
translations.idiomatic: If mere words may not be idle, how much less deeds!

sentences.zh: 故釋之之言不可不察，周公之戒不可不法也。」

translations.literal: Therefore Shizhi’s words cannot but be examined; Zhou Gong’s warning cannot but be taken as model."
translations.idiomatic: Weigh Shizhi’s argument carefully and heed the Duke of Zhou’s warning."

sentences.zh: 又陳「諸鳥獸無用之物，而有芻穀人徒之費，皆可蠲除。」

translations.literal: Again he stated, “The various birds and beasts—useless things—yet there is fodder-grain and human follower expense; all can be remitted and removed."
translations.idiomatic: Again he stated, “The various birds and beasts—useless things—yet there is fodder-grain and human follower expense; all can be remitted and removed."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問曰：「漢桓帝時，白馬令李雲上書言：『帝者，諦也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked, saying, “In Han Emperor Huan’s time, the magistrate of Baima, Li Yun, submitted a memorial saying, ‘Di means “true insight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked: “Under Emperor Huan, Li Yun of Baima wrote that di means ‘true insight.

sentences.zh: 是帝欲不諦。』

translations.literal: This means the Di does not desire true insight.'
translations.idiomatic: This means that the di wished not to be truly discerning.'

sentences.zh: 當何得不死？」

translations.literal: How could he not have to die?"
translations.idiomatic: Why was he put to death?"

sentences.zh: 肅對曰：「但爲言失逆順之節。

translations.literal: Su replied, saying, “Only because his words lost the rhythm of compliance and opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su answered, “Only because his phrasing broke the rules of respectful remonstrance, though his intent was loyal—to mend the Han throne.

sentences.zh: 原其本意，皆欲盡心，念存補國。

translations.literal: Tracing his original intent, all wished to exhaust heart, thinking to mend the state.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial aimed only to strengthen the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 且帝者之威，過於雷霆，殺一匹夫，無異螻蟻。

translations.literal: Moreover the Di’s awe surpasses thunderclap; killing a common man is no different from ants.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor’s wrath outthunders heaven; killing a commoner is swatting a fly.

sentences.zh: 寬而宥之，可以示容受切言，廣德宇於天下。

translations.literal: If lenient and forgiving him, one can display containing cutting words, broadening virtue’s roof under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To pardon him would show that blunt counsel is welcome and magnanimity fills the realm.

sentences.zh: 故臣以爲殺之未必爲是也。」

translations.literal: Therefore your subject thinks killing him was not necessarily correct."
translations.idiomatic: So I do not think his execution was just."

sentences.zh: 帝又問：「司馬遷以受刑之故，內懷隱切，著史記非貶孝武，令人切齒。」

translations.literal: The Emperor again asked, “Sima Qian because of receiving punishment, within harbored hidden bitterness, wrote the Records slandering Filial Wu, making men gnash teeth."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again asked, “Sima Qian because of receiving punishment, within harbored hidden bitterness, wrote the Records slandering Filial Wu, making men gnash teeth."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「司馬遷記事，不虛美，不隱惡。

translations.literal: He replied, saying, “Sima Qian recorded affairs, not falsely beautifying, not concealing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su replied, “Sima Qian recorded facts without flattery or concealment.

sentences.zh: 劉向、揚雄服其善叙事，有良史之才，謂之實錄。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong admired his good narrating of affairs, having a good historian’s talent, calling it a true record.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong praised his narrative skill and called the work a true record.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝聞其述史記，取孝景及己本紀覽之，於是大怒，削而投之。

translations.literal: Han Emperor Wu heard his narrating the Records, took the annals of Filial Jing and himself and inspected them, thereupon was greatly angry, cut them and threw them away.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu read the annals of Jing and himself he flew into a rage and struck them from the text.

sentences.zh: 於今此兩紀有錄無書。

translations.literal: To this day these two annals have entries but no text.
translations.idiomatic: Those two chapters survive as titles without content.

sentences.zh: 後遭李陵事，遂下遷蠶室。

translations.literal: Later encountering the Li Ling affair, thereupon he sent Qian down to the silkworm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Li Ling case sent him to the castration chamber.

sentences.zh: 此爲隱切在孝武，而不在於史遷也。」

translations.literal: This is hidden bitterness in Filial Wu, not in Historian Qian."
translations.idiomatic: The grudge lay with Emperor Wu, not with Sima Qian."

sentences.zh: 正始元年，出爲廣平太守。公事徵還，拜議郎。頃之，爲侍中，遷太常。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi 1, Wang Su was sent out as Administrator of Guangping. He was summoned back on official business and appointed Consultant Gentleman. Soon afterward he became Palace Attendant and was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 1, Wang Su was sent out as Administrator of Guangping. Summoned back on official business, he was appointed Consultant Gentleman. Soon afterward he became Palace Attendant and was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍曹爽專權，任用何晏、鄧颺等。肅與太尉蔣濟、司農桓範論及時政，肅正色曰：「此輩即弘恭、石顯之屬，復稱說邪！」

translations.literal: At the time Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized power and employed He Yan, Deng Yang, and others. When Wang Su discussed current government with Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and Chamberlain for the National Treasury Huan Fan, he said sternly, “These men are the kind of Hong Gong and Shi Xian; how can they be praised again!”
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized power and employed He Yan, Deng Yang, and others. When Wang Su discussed current government with Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and Chamberlain for the National Treasury Huan Fan, he said sternly, “These men are of the sort of Hong Gong and Shi Xian; how can anyone praise them!”

sentences.zh: 爽聞之，戒何晏等曰：「當共慎之！公卿已比諸君前世惡人矣。」坐宗廟事免。後爲光祿勳。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang heard this, he warned He Yan and the others, saying, “You must all be careful! The dukes and ministers have already compared you gentlemen to evil men of a former age.” Wang Su was dismissed because of an ancestral-temple matter. Later he became Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang heard this, he warned He Yan and the others, saying, “You must all be careful! The dukes and ministers have already compared you gentlemen to evil men of a former age.” Wang Su was dismissed over an ancestral-temple matter. Later he became Chamberlain for Attendants.

sentences.zh: 時有二魚長尺，集于武庫之屋，有司以爲吉祥。肅曰：「魚生於淵而亢於屋，介鱗之物失其所也。邊將其殆有棄甲之變乎？」其後果有東關之敗。

translations.literal: At the time two fish a foot long gathered on the roof of the armory, and the responsible officials considered this auspicious. Wang Su said, “Fish are born in the depths, yet they are raised up on a roof; armored and scaled creatures have lost their proper place. On the frontier, will there perhaps be a change in which armor is abandoned?” Afterward there indeed was the defeat at Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time two fish a foot long appeared on the roof of the armory, and the responsible officials considered this auspicious. Wang Su said, “Fish are born in the depths, yet they are raised up on a roof; armored and scaled creatures have lost their proper place. On the frontier, might there be an upheaval in which armor is abandoned?” Afterward there was indeed the defeat at Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 徙爲河南尹。嘉平六年，持節兼太常，奉法駕，迎高貴鄉公于元城。

translations.literal: He was transferred to become Intendant of Henan. In Jiaping 6, he held the tally as acting Minister of Ceremonies and escorted the imperial carriage to welcome the Duke of Gaogui District at Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to become Intendant of Henan. In Jiaping 6, he held the tally as acting Minister of Ceremonies, accompanied the imperial carriage, and welcomed the Duke of Gaogui District at Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，白氣經天，大將軍司馬景王問肅其故，肅荅曰：「此蚩尤之旗也，東南其有亂乎？君若脩己以安百姓，則天下樂安者歸德，唱亂者先亡矣。」

translations.literal: That year a white vapor crossed the sky. Grand General Sima Jingwang asked Wang Su the reason, and Wang Su answered, “This is Chiyou’s banner. Is there to be disorder in the southeast? If you cultivate yourself and bring peace to the people, then those under Heaven who delight in peace will turn to your virtue, and those who cry out for rebellion will be the first to perish.”
translations.idiomatic: That year a white vapor crossed the sky. Grand General Sima Jingwang asked Wang Su the reason, and Wang Su answered, “This is Chiyou's banner. Will there be disorder in the southeast? If you cultivate yourself and bring peace to the people, then those under Heaven who delight in peace will turn to your virtue, and those who cry out for rebellion will be the first to perish.”

sentences.zh: 明年春，鎮東將軍毌丘儉、揚州刺史文欽反，景王謂肅曰：「霍光感夏侯勝之言，始重儒學之士，良有以也。安國寧主，其術焉在？」

translations.literal: The next spring, General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Yangzhou Inspector Wen Qin rebelled. Sima Jingwang said to Wang Su, “Huo Guang was moved by Xiahou Sheng’s words and thereafter first gave weight to men of classical learning. There was truly a reason for it. Where lies the method for securing the state and calming the ruler?”
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Yangzhou Inspector Wen Qin rebelled. Sima Jingwang said to Wang Su, “Huo Guang was moved by Xiahou Sheng's words and only then gave weight to men of classical learning. There truly was a reason for this. Where does the method lie for securing the state and calming the ruler?”

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「昔關羽率荊州之衆，降于禁於漢濵，遂有北向爭天下之志。後孫權襲取其將士家屬，羽士衆一旦瓦解。今淮南將士父母妻子皆在內州，但急往禦衞，使不得前，必有關羽土崩之勢矣。」

translations.literal: Wang Su said, “Formerly Guan Yu led the forces of Jingzhou, forced Yu Jin to surrender on the Han River, and then conceived the ambition of turning north to contest all under Heaven. Later Sun Quan attacked and seized the families of his officers and soldiers, and Guan Yu’s troops collapsed in a single day. Now the parents, wives, and children of the Huainan officers and soldiers are all in the inner provinces. If you only hurry there to block and guard them, so that they cannot advance, they will certainly have Guan Yu’s crumbling collapse.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said, “Formerly Guan Yu led the forces of Jingzhou, forced Yu Jin to surrender on the Han River, and then conceived the ambition of turning north to contest all under Heaven. Later Sun Quan attacked and seized the families of his officers and soldiers, and Guan Yu's troops collapsed in a single day. Now the parents, wives, and children of the Huainan officers and soldiers are all in the inner provinces. If you simply hurry there to block and guard against them, so that they cannot advance, they will certainly suffer Guan Yu's collapse.”

sentences.zh: 景王從之，遂破儉、欽。後遷中領軍，加散騎常侍，增邑三百，并前二千二百戶。

translations.literal: Sima Jingwang followed this advice and accordingly defeated Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin. Later Wang Su was promoted to Central Leader of the Army, additionally made Regular Mounted Attendant, and granted an increase of three hundred households, making twenty-two hundred households together with his previous fief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jingwang followed this advice and accordingly defeated Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin. Later Wang Su was promoted to Central Leader of the Army, additionally made Regular Mounted Attendant, and granted an increase of three hundred households, making 2,200 households together with his previous fief.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年薨，門生縗絰者以百數。追贈衞將軍，謚曰景侯。子惲嗣。惲薨，無子，國絕。

translations.literal: He died in Ganlu 1. His disciples wearing mourning hemp numbered in the hundreds. He was posthumously presented as General of the Guards and posthumously titled Marquis Jing. His son Yun succeeded him. When Yun died without sons, the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Ganlu 1. His disciples wearing mourning hemp numbered in the hundreds. He was posthumously presented as General of the Guards and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing. His son Yun succeeded him. When Yun died without sons, the state was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 景元四年，封肅子恂爲蘭陵侯。咸熈中，開建五等，以肅著勳前朝，改封恂爲氶子。

translations.literal: In Jingyuan 4, Wang Su’s son Xun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lanling. During Xianxi, when the five ranks of nobility were established, because Wang Su had shown merit in the former court, Xun’s enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyuan 4, Wang Su's son Xun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lanling. During Xianxi, when the five ranks of nobility were established, Xun's enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Cheng because Wang Su had shown merit in the former court.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：恂字良夫，有通識，在朝忠正。歷河南尹、侍中，所居有稱。乃心存公，有匪躬之節。

translations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: Xun’s courtesy name was Liangfu. He had penetrating understanding and was loyal and upright at court. He successively served as Intendant of Henan and Palace Attendant, and in the offices he held he was praised. His heart was fixed on public duty, and he had the integrity of not acting for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Sayings of the Age says: Xun's courtesy name was Liangfu. He had penetrating understanding and was loyal and upright at court. He successively served as Intendant of Henan and Palace Attendant, and was praised in each office he held. His heart was fixed on public duty, and he had the integrity of not acting for himself.

sentences.zh: 鬲令袁毅餽以駿馬，知其貪財，不受。毅竟以黷貨而敗。建立二學，崇明五經，皆恂所建。卒時年四十餘，贈車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi, Magistrate of Ge, presented him with a fine horse; knowing that Yuan Yi was greedy for wealth, Xun did not accept it. Yuan Yi was eventually ruined for corrupt dealing. The establishment of the two schools and the honoring and clarification of the Five Classics were all Xun’s work. When he died he was over forty years old and was presented as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, Magistrate of Ge, presented him with a fine horse; knowing that Yuan Yi was greedy for wealth, Xun refused to accept it. Yuan Yi was eventually ruined by corrupt dealings. The establishment of the two schools and the honoring and clarification of the Five Classics were all Xun's work. He died in his forties and was posthumously presented as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 肅女適司馬文王，即文明皇后，生晉武帝、齊獻王攸。

translations.literal: Wang Su’s daughter married Sima Wenwang; she was Empress Wenming and gave birth to Emperor Wu of Jin and You, Prince Xian of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su’s daughter married Sima Wenwang; she was Empress Wenming and gave birth to Emperor Wu of Jin and You, Prince Xian of Qi.

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：恂兄弟八人。其達者，虔字恭祖，以功幹見稱，位至尚書。

translations.literal: The Eulogies of the Various Lords of Jin says: Xun had eight brothers. Among those who rose, Qian, courtesy name Gongzu, was praised for achievement and ability and reached the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Eulogies of the Various Lords of Jin says: Xun had eight brothers. Of those who rose to prominence, Qian, courtesy name Gongzu, was praised for achievement and ability and reached the post of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弟愷，字君夫，少有才力而無行檢，與衞尉石崇友善，俱以豪侈競於世，終於後將軍。虔子康、隆，仕亦宦達，爲後世所重。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kai, courtesy name Junfu, had talent and strength when young but lacked conduct and restraint. He was friendly with Chamberlain for the Guards Shi Chong, and both competed with the age in extravagance; he ended as General of the Rear. Qian’s sons Kang and Long also rose in office and were valued by later generations.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kai, courtesy name Junfu, had talent and ability when young but lacked discipline in his conduct. He was friendly with Chamberlain for the Guards Shi Chong, and both competed with the age in extravagance; he ended as General of the Rear. Qian's sons Kang and Long also rose in office and were valued by later generations.

sentences.zh: 初，肅善賈、馬之學，而不好鄭氏，采會同異，爲《尚書》、《詩》、《論語》、三禮、《左氏解》，及撰定父朗所作易傳，皆列於學官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Su was skilled in the learning of Jia and Ma but did not favor the Zheng school. He collected and compared agreements and differences, made explanations for the Documents, the Odes, the Analects, the three Rites, and the Zuo Tradition, and edited and fixed the commentary on the Changes written by his father Lang. All were ranked among the official studies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Su was skilled in the learning of Jia and Ma but did not favor the Zheng school. He gathered and compared points of agreement and difference, made explanations for the Shangshu, the Shi, the Lunyu, the Three Rites, and the Zuoshi, and edited and fixed the Yi commentary written by his father Wang Lang. All were listed among the official studies.

sentences.zh: 其所論駮朝廷典制、郊祀、宗廟、喪紀、輕重，凡百餘篇。

translations.literal: His discussions and refutations concerning court institutions, suburban sacrifice, ancestral temples, mourning regulations, and degrees of light and heavy observance amounted in all to more than a hundred essays.
translations.idiomatic: His discussions and refutations concerning court institutions, suburban sacrifices, ancestral temples, mourning regulations, and degrees of light and heavy observance amounted in all to more than a hundred essays.

sentences.zh: 時樂安孫叔然，臣松之按叔然與晉武帝同名，故稱其字。授學鄭玄之門，人稱東州大儒。徵爲秘書監，不就。

translations.literal: At the time there was Sun Shuran of Le’an. Your servant Songzhi notes: Shuran had the same personal name as Emperor Wu of Jin, so he is called by his courtesy name. He received instruction in Zheng Xuan’s school, and people called him the great classicist of the eastern provinces. He was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library but did not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Sun Shuran of Le'an. Your servant Songzhi notes: Shuran had the same personal name as Emperor Wu of Jin, so he is called by his courtesy name. He received instruction in Zheng Xuan's school, and people called him the great classicist of the eastern provinces. He was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library but did not take the post.

sentences.zh: 肅集聖證論以譏短玄，叔然駮而釋之，及作《周易》、《春秋例》，《毛詩》、《禮記》、《春秋》三傳、《國語》、《爾雅》諸注，又著書十餘篇。

translations.literal: Wang Su compiled the Shengzheng lun to criticize Zheng Xuan’s shortcomings; Sun Shuran refuted it and explained Zheng’s position. He also wrote the Zhouyi, the Chunqiu li, commentaries on the Mao Odes, the Rites Record, the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Discourses of the States, and the Erya, and more than ten further works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su compiled the Shengzheng lun to criticize Zheng Xuan's shortcomings; Sun Shuran refuted it and explained Zheng's position. He also wrote works on the Zhouyi and the Chunqiu li, as well as commentaries on the Mao Odes, the Record of Rites, the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Discourses of the States, and the Erya, along with more than ten other works.

sentences.zh: 自魏初徵士燉煌周生烈，臣松之按此人姓周生，名烈。何晏《論語集解》有烈《義例》，餘所著述，見晉武帝《中經簿》。

translations.literal: From early Wei there was the recruited scholar Zhousheng Lie of Dunhuang. Your servant Songzhi notes: this man’s surname was Zhousheng and his personal name was Lie. He Yan’s Collected Explanations of the Analects includes Lie’s Principles and Examples; his other writings are seen in Emperor Wu of Jin’s Central Classics Register.
translations.idiomatic: From early Wei there was the recruited scholar Zhousheng Lie of Dunhuang. Your servant Songzhi notes: this man's surname was Zhousheng and his personal name was Lie. He Yan's Collected Explanations of the Analects includes Lie's Principles and Examples; his other writings appear in Emperor Wu of Jin's Central Classics Register.

sentences.zh: 明帝時大司農弘農董遇等，亦歷注經傳，頗傳於世。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming’s time, Grand Minister of Agriculture Dong Yu of Hongnong and others also successively annotated classics and commentaries, and their works circulated considerably in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's time, Grand Minister of Agriculture Dong Yu of Hongnong and others also annotated classics and commentaries in succession, and their works circulated widely in the world.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：遇字季直，性質訥而好學。興平中，關中擾亂，與兄季中依將軍段煨。采梠負販，而常挾持經書，投閑習讀。其兄笑之而遇不改。

translations.literal: The Weilue says: Dong Yu’s courtesy name was Jizhi. By nature he was plain and slow of speech, but fond of study. During Xingping, when Guanzhong was disturbed, he and his elder brother Jizhong relied on General Duan Wei. He gathered rough grain and carried goods for sale, yet always kept the classics under his arm and, whenever he found free moments, studied and read. His elder brother laughed at him, but Dong Yu did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue says: Dong Yu's courtesy name was Jizhi. By nature he was plain and slow of speech, but fond of study. During Xingping, when Guanzhong was in turmoil, he and his elder brother Jizhong depended on General Duan Wei. He gathered rough grain and carried goods for sale, yet always kept the classics under his arm and studied whenever he found a spare moment. His elder brother laughed at him, but Dong Yu did not change.

sentences.zh: 及建安初，王綱小設，郡舉孝廉，稍遷黃門侍郎。是時，漢帝委政太祖，遇旦夕侍講，爲天子所愛信。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian’an, when royal order had been slightly established, the commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt, and he was gradually promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates. At this time the Han emperor entrusted government to Grand Progenitor, and Dong Yu attended and lectured morning and evening, being loved and trusted by the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jian'an, when royal order had been somewhat restored, the commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt, and he was gradually promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates. At this time the Han emperor entrusted government to Taizu, and Dong Yu attended and lectured morning and evening, earning the Son of Heaven's affection and trust.

sentences.zh: 至二十二年，許中百官矯制，遇雖不與謀，猶被錄詣鄴，轉爲冗散。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the hundred officials in Xu falsely issued an order, although Dong Yu had not participated in the plot, he was still arrested and sent to Ye, then transferred to a supernumerary post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, when the hundred officials in Xu falsely issued an imperial order, Dong Yu had not participated in the plot, but he was still arrested and sent to Ye, then transferred to a supernumerary post.

sentences.zh: 常從太祖西征，道由孟津，過弘農王冢。太祖疑欲謁，顧問左右，左右莫對，遇乃越第進曰：「春秋之義，國君即位未踰年而卒，未成爲君。弘農王即阼旣淺，又爲暴臣所制，降在藩國，不應謁。」太祖乃過。

translations.literal: He once accompanied Grand Progenitor on a western campaign. The road passed by Mengjin and crossed the tomb of the Prince of Hongnong. Grand Progenitor hesitated, wishing to pay respects, and turned to ask those around him, but none answered. Dong Yu then came forward out of order and said, “According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a ruler dies before a full year has passed after accession, he has not yet fully become ruler. The Prince of Hongnong had only briefly ascended the throne and was also controlled by violent ministers, then reduced to a regional principality; one should not pay respects.” Grand Progenitor then passed by.
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied Taizu on a western campaign. The road went by Mengjin and passed the tomb of the Prince of Hongnong. Taizu hesitated, wishing to pay respects, and turned to ask those around him, but none answered. Dong Yu then stepped forward out of order and said, “According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a ruler dies before a full year has passed after accession, he has not yet fully become ruler. The Prince of Hongnong had only briefly ascended the throne and was also controlled by violent ministers, then reduced to a regional principality; one should not pay respects.” Taizu then passed by.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，出爲郡守。明帝時，入爲侍中、大司農。數年，病亡。

translations.literal: During Huangchu, Dong Yu was sent out as a commandery governor. In Emperor Ming’s time he entered court as Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Agriculture. After several years, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu, Dong Yu was sent out as a commandery governor. In Emperor Ming's time he entered court as Palace Attendant and Grand Minister of Agriculture. After several years, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 初，遇善治《老子》，爲《老子》作訓注。又善《左氏傳》，更爲作朱墨別異。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dong Yu was skilled in studying the Laozi and made explanatory annotations for it. He was also skilled in the Zuo Tradition and further made red-and-black distinctions for it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dong Yu was skilled in studying the Laozi and made explanatory annotations for it. He was also skilled in the Zuo Tradition and further prepared red-and-black distinctions for it.

sentences.zh: 人有從學者，遇不肯教，而云：「必當先讀百徧」。言「讀書百徧而義自見」。從學者云：「苦渴無日。」遇言：「當以三餘」。或問三餘之意，遇言：「冬者，歲之餘；夜者，日之餘，陰雨者，時之餘也」。

translations.literal: When people wished to study under him, Dong Yu would not teach them, but said, “You must first read it a hundred times.” He said, “When a book has been read a hundred times, its meaning appears of itself.” Those wishing to study said, “We suffer from lack of days.” Dong Yu said, “You should use the three remainders.” Someone asked what the three remainders meant, and Dong Yu said, “Winter is the remainder of the year; night is the remainder of the day; cloudy and rainy weather is the remainder of the season.”
translations.idiomatic: When people wished to study under him, Dong Yu would not teach them, but said, “You must first read it a hundred times.” He said, “When a book has been read a hundred times, its meaning appears of itself.” Those wishing to study said, “We suffer from having no days.” Dong Yu said, “You should use the three remainders.” Someone asked what the three remainders meant, and Dong Yu said, “Winter is the remainder of the year; night is the remainder of the day; cloudy and rainy weather is the remainder of the season.”

sentences.zh: 由是諸生少從遇學，無傳其朱墨者。《世語》曰：遇子綏，位至祕書監，亦有才學。齊王冏功臣董艾，即綏之子也。

translations.literal: For this reason few students studied under Dong Yu, and no one transmitted his red-and-black distinctions. The Sayings of the Age says: Dong Yu’s son Sui reached the post of Director of the Palace Library and also had talent and learning. Dong Ai, a meritorious follower of Jiong, Prince of Qi, was Sui’s son.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, among the students, few followed Dong Yu in study, and no one transmitted his red-and-black distinctions. The Shiyu says: Dong Yu's son Sui reached the post of Mishu Jian, Director of the Palace Library, and also had talent and learning. Dong Ai, a meritorious follower of Prince Jiong of Qi, was the son of Sui.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》以遇及賈洪、邯鄲淳、薛夏、隗禧、蘇林、樂詳等七人爲儒宗，其序曰：「從初平之元，至建安之末，天下分崩，人懷苟且，綱紀旣衰，儒道尤甚。

translations.literal: The Weilue treated Dong Yu, Jia Hong, Handan Chun, Xue Xia, Wei Xi, Su Lin, and Yue Xiang, seven men in all, as masters of classicism. Its preface says, “From the beginning of Chuping to the end of Jian’an, all under Heaven split apart, men harbored expedience, and once the bonds of order had declined, the way of the classicists suffered even more.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilue treated Dong Yu, Jia Hong, Handan Chun, Xue Xia, Wei Xi, Su Lin, and Yue Xiang, seven men in all, as masters of classicism. Its preface says, “From the beginning of Chuping to the end of Jian'an, all under Heaven split apart, people lived for expediency, and once the bonds of order had declined, the way of the classicists suffered even more.

sentences.zh: 至黃初元年之後，新主乃復，始掃除太學之灰炭，補舊石碑之缺壞，備博士之員錄，依漢甲乙以考課。申告州郡，有欲學者，皆遣詣太學。

translations.literal: After Huangchu 1, the new ruler then restored it, first sweeping away the ashes and charcoal of the Imperial Academy, repairing the damage to the old stone steles, completing the roster of Erudites, and examining performance according to the Han first and second grades. He repeatedly notified the provinces and commanderies that all who wished to study should be sent to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Huangchu 1, the new ruler restored it, first sweeping away the ashes and charcoal of the Imperial Academy, repairing the damage to the old stone steles, completing the roster of Erudites, and evaluating performance according to the Han first and second grades. He repeatedly notified the provinces and commanderies that all who wished to study should be sent to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 太學始開，有弟子數百人。至太和、青龍中，中外多事，人懷避就。雖性非解學，多求詣太學。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Academy first opened, it had several hundred disciples. By the Taihe and Qinglong periods, there were many affairs inside and outside the court, and people had avoidance and pursuit in mind. Even those whose natures were not suited to understanding study often sought to go to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Academy first opened, it had several hundred students. By the Taihe and Qinglong periods, affairs were numerous both inside and outside the court, and people were thinking about what to avoid and what to pursue. Even those whose natures were not suited to learning often sought to enter the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 太學諸生有千數，而諸博士率皆麄踈，無以教弟子。弟子本亦避役，竟無能習學，冬來春去，歲歲如是。

translations.literal: The students of the Imperial Academy numbered in the thousands, but the various Erudites were generally crude and careless, with no way to teach the disciples. The disciples themselves had originally come to avoid service, and in the end none could practice learning. Winter came and spring went; year after year it was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The students of the Imperial Academy numbered in the thousands, but the various Erudites were generally crude and careless, with no means of teaching them. The students themselves had originally come to avoid service, and in the end none could pursue learning. Winter came and spring went; year after year it was like this.

sentences.zh: 又雖有精者，而臺閣舉格太高，加不念統其大義，而問字指墨法點注之間，百人同試，度者未十。

translations.literal: Even when there were those who were refined in learning, the standards raised by the offices were too high; moreover, they did not think to command the great meaning, but asked about characters, pointing to ink rules, punctuation, and annotations. When a hundred men took the same examination, fewer than ten passed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when there were those who were refined in learning, the standards set by the offices were too high. Moreover, they did not think to master the larger meaning, but asked about characters, scribal rules, punctuation, and annotations. When a hundred men took the same examination, fewer than ten passed.

sentences.zh: 是以志學之士遂復陵遲，而末求浮虛者各競逐也。

translations.literal: For this reason men committed to learning again declined, while those who sought superficial emptiness in minor things all competed in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason men committed to learning again declined, while those who sought superficial emptiness in minor things all competed in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 正始中，有詔議圜丘，普延學士。時郎官及司徒領吏二萬餘人，雖復分布，見在京師者尚且萬人，而應書與議者略無幾人。

translations.literal: During Zhengshi, there was an edict to deliberate on the Round Mound, and scholars were invited broadly. At the time, gentlemen officials and clerks under the Minister over the Masses numbered more than twenty thousand. Although they were distributed in various places, those currently in the capital still numbered ten thousand, yet among those who answered the letter and joined the deliberation there were almost no more than a few.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, there was an edict to deliberate on the Round Mound, and scholars were invited broadly. At the time, gentlemen officials and clerks under the Minister over the Masses numbered more than twenty thousand. Although they were distributed in various places, those actually present in the capital still numbered ten thousand, yet only a handful answered the written summons and joined the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 又是時朝堂公卿以下四百餘人，其能操筆者未有十人，多皆相從飽食而退。嗟夫！學業沈隕，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Also at that time, among more than four hundred men in the court hall from dukes and ministers downward, fewer than ten could take up a brush; most merely followed one another, ate their fill, and withdrew. Alas! The sinking and fall of learning had come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Also at that time, among more than four hundred men in the court hall, from dukes and ministers downward, fewer than ten could take up a brush; most merely followed one another in, ate their fill, and withdrew. Alas! The sinking collapse of learning had come to this.

sentences.zh: 是以私心常區區貴乎數公者，各處荒亂之際，而能守志彌敦者也。」

translations.literal: Therefore in my private heart I have always earnestly valued these several gentlemen, because each lived amid devastation and disorder yet could keep his commitment all the more firmly.”
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in my private heart I have always earnestly valued these several gentlemen, because each lived amid devastation and disorder yet kept his commitment all the more firmly.”

sentences.zh: 賈洪字叔業，京兆新豐人也。好學有才，而特精於春秋左傳。建安初，仕郡，舉計掾，應州辟。

translations.literal: Jia Hong, courtesy name Shuye, was from Xinfeng in Jingzhao. He loved learning and had talent, and was especially expert in the Spring and Autumn Annals and Zuo Tradition. At the beginning of Jian’an he served in his commandery, was recommended as Accounts Clerk, and responded to a provincial summons.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hong, courtesy name Shuye, was from Xinfeng in Jingzhao. He loved learning and had talent, and was especially expert in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Zuo Tradition. At the beginning of Jian'an he served in his commandery, was recommended as Accounts Clerk, and responded to a provincial summons.

sentences.zh: 時州中自參軍事以下百餘人，唯洪與馮翊嚴苞交通，材學最高。

translations.literal: At the time, among the more than one hundred men in the province from Military Affairs Aide downward, only Hong and Yan Bao of Fengyi associated with one another, and their talent and learning were highest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, among the more than one hundred men in the province from Military Affairs Aide downward, only Hong and Yan Bao of Fengyi kept company with one another, and their talent and learning were the highest.

sentences.zh: 洪歷守三縣令，所在輒開除廄舍，親授諸生。後馬超反，超劫洪，將詣華陰，使作露布。洪不獲已，爲作之。

translations.literal: Hong successively served as acting magistrate of three counties; wherever he was, he opened and cleared out stables and lodgings and personally instructed students. Later Ma Chao rebelled, seized Hong, and was about to go to Huayin; he made Hong write a proclamation. Hong could not avoid it and wrote it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong successively served as acting magistrate of three counties. Wherever he was, he opened and cleared out stables and lodging houses and personally instructed students. Later Ma Chao rebelled, seized Hong, and was about to go to Huayin; he made Hong write a proclamation. Hong could not avoid it and wrote it for him.

sentences.zh: 司隷鍾繇在東，識其文，曰：「此賈洪作也。」及超破走，太祖召洪署軍謀掾。猶以其前爲超作露布文，故不即叙。晚乃出爲陰泉長。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao, Colonel Director of Retainers, was in the east, recognized the style, and said, “This was written by Jia Hong.” When Ma Chao was defeated and fled, Grand Progenitor summoned Hong to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk. Still, because he had earlier written a proclamation for Ma Chao, he was not immediately appointed in regular order. Only later was he sent out as Chief of Yinquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao, Colonel Director of Retainers, was in the east, recognized the style, and said, “This was written by Jia Hong.” When Ma Chao was defeated and fled, Taizu summoned Hong to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk. Still, because he had earlier written a proclamation for Ma Chao, he was not immediately appointed in regular order. Only later was he sent out as Chief of Yinquan.

sentences.zh: 延康中，轉爲白馬王相。善能談戲。王彪亦雅好文學，常師宗之，過於三卿。數歲病亡，亡時年五十餘，時人爲之恨仕不至二千石。

translations.literal: During Yankang he was transferred to be Chancellor of the Prince of Baima. He was good at conversation and wit. Prince Biao also elegantly loved literature and learning, and constantly took him as teacher and model, more than the three ministers. After several years Hong died of illness. He was over fifty when he died, and people of the time regretted for him that his office had not reached two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: During Yankang he was transferred to be Chancellor of the Prince of Baima. He was good at conversation and wit. Prince Biao also had an elegant love of literature and learning, and constantly honored him as teacher and model above the three ministers. After several years Hong died of illness. He was over fifty when he died, and people of the time regretted on his behalf that his office had not reached two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 而嚴苞亦歷守二縣，黃初中，以高才入爲秘書丞，數奏文賦，文帝異之。出爲西平太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Yan Bao also successively served as acting magistrate of two counties. During Huangchu, because of his high talent, he entered as Assistant Director of the Palace Library. He repeatedly submitted writings and rhapsodies, and Emperor Wen considered him extraordinary. He was sent out as Administrator of Xiping and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao also successively served as acting magistrate of two counties. During Huangchu, because of his high talent, he entered court as Assistant Director of the Palace Library. He repeatedly submitted writings and rhapsodies, and Emperor Wen considered him extraordinary. He was sent out as Administrator of Xiping and died in office.

sentences.zh: 薛夏字宣聲，天水人也。博學有才。天水舊有姜、閻、任、趙四姓，常推於郡中，而夏爲單家，不爲降屈。

translations.literal: Xue Xia, courtesy name Xuansheng, was from Tianshui. He was broadly learned and talented. Tianshui had long had the four surnames Jiang, Yan, Ren, and Zhao, who were always honored in the commandery, but Xia came from an isolated family and would not lower himself before them.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xia, courtesy name Xuansheng, was from Tianshui. He was broadly learned and talented. Tianshui had long had the four surnames Jiang, Yan, Ren, and Zhao, who were always honored in the commandery, but Xia came from a solitary family and would not lower himself before them.

sentences.zh: 四姓欲共治之，夏乃游逸，東詣京師。太祖宿聞其名，甚禮遇之。

translations.literal: The four surnames wished jointly to deal with him, so Xia wandered away and went east to the capital. Grand Progenitor had long heard his name and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The four surnames wished jointly to punish him, so Xia wandered away and went east to the capital. Taizu had long heard his name and treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 後四姓又使囚遙引夏，關移潁川，收捕繫獄。時太祖已在兾州，聞夏爲本郡所質，撫掌曰：「夏無罪也。漢陽兒輩直欲殺之耳！」乃告潁川使理出之，召署軍謀掾。

translations.literal: Later the four surnames again had prisoners implicate Xia from afar, sent official documents to Yingchuan, and had him arrested and imprisoned. At the time Grand Progenitor was already in Jizhou. Hearing that Xia had been held by his home commandery, he clapped his hands and said, “Xia is without guilt. Those youths of Hanyang simply want to kill him!” He then notified Yingchuan to review the case and release him, and summoned him to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later the four surnames again had prisoners implicate Xia from afar, sent official documents to Yingchuan, and had him arrested and imprisoned. At the time Taizu was already in Jizhou. Hearing that Xia had been taken hostage by his home commandery, he clapped his hands and said, “Xia is without guilt. Those youths of Hanyang simply want to kill him!” He then notified Yingchuan to examine the case and release him, and summoned him to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk.

sentences.zh: 文帝又嘉其才，黃初中爲祕書丞，帝每與夏推論書傳，未嘗不終日也。每呼之不名，而謂之薛君。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also admired his talent. During Huangchu he became Assistant Director of the Palace Library. Whenever the Emperor discussed documents and commentaries with Xia, it always lasted the whole day. Whenever he addressed him, he did not use his personal name, but called him Lord Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also admired his talent. During Huangchu he became Assistant Director of the Palace Library. Whenever the Emperor discussed documents and commentaries with Xia, it always lasted the whole day. When addressing him, he did not use his personal name, but called him Lord Xue.

sentences.zh: 夏居甚貧，帝又顧其衣薄，解所御服袍賜之。其後征東將軍曹休來朝，時帝方與夏有所咨論，而外啟休到，帝引入。

translations.literal: Xia lived in great poverty, and the Emperor, noticing that his clothing was thin, took off a robe he had been wearing and bestowed it on him. Later General Who Campaigns East Cao Xiu came to court. At the time the Emperor was consulting and discussing something with Xia; when those outside reported that Xiu had arrived, the Emperor brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Xia lived in great poverty, and the Emperor, noticing that his clothing was thin, took off a robe he had been wearing and bestowed it on him. Later General Who Campaigns East Cao Xiu came to court. At the time the Emperor was consulting with Xia; when those outside reported that Xiu had arrived, the Emperor brought him in.

sentences.zh: 坐定，帝顧夏言之於休曰：「此君，祕書丞天水薛宣聲也，宜共談。」其見遇如此。

translations.literal: When they were seated, the Emperor looked at Xia and spoke of him to Xiu, saying, “This gentleman is Assistant Director of the Palace Library Xue Xuansheng of Tianshui. You should converse together.” Such was the treatment he received.
translations.idiomatic: When they were seated, the Emperor looked at Xia and introduced him to Xiu, saying, “This gentleman is Xue Xuansheng of Tianshui, Assistant Director of the Palace Library. You should converse together.” Such was the treatment he received.

sentences.zh: 尋欲用之，會文帝崩。至太和中，嘗以公事移蘭臺。蘭臺自以臺也，而祕書署耳，謂夏爲不得移也，推使當有坐者。

translations.literal: Soon the Emperor wished to employ him further, but Emperor Wen died. During Taihe, Xia once transferred a public matter to the Censorate. The Censorate considered itself a bureau, while the Palace Library was merely an office, and said that Xia was not permitted to transfer matters to it, pressing that someone should be held responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Emperor wished to employ him further, but Emperor Wen died. During Taihe, Xia once transferred an official matter to the Censorate. The Censorate considered itself a bureau, while the Palace Library was merely an office, and said that Xia was not permitted to transfer matters to it, pressing for someone to be held responsible.

sentences.zh: 夏報之曰：「蘭臺爲外臺，祕書爲內閣，臺、閣，一也，何不相移之有？」蘭臺屈無以折。自是之後，遂以爲常。後數歲病亡，勑其子無還天水。

translations.literal: Xia replied, “The Censorate is the outer bureau; the Palace Library is the inner cabinet. Bureau and cabinet are one thing, so how can there be any not transferring between them?” The Censorate was defeated and had no way to refute him. After this, it became standard practice. Several years later he died of illness, instructing his son not to return to Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Xia replied, “The Censorate is the outer bureau; the Palace Library is the inner cabinet. Bureau and cabinet are one thing, so how could transfer between them be impermissible?” The Censorate yielded and had no way to refute him. After this, it became standard practice. Several years later he died of illness, instructing his son not to return to Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 隗禧字子牙，京兆人也。世單家。少好學。初平中，三輔亂，禧南客荊州，不以荒擾，擔負經書，每以採梠餘日，則誦習之。

translations.literal: Wei Xi, courtesy name Ziya, was from Jingzhao. His family had for generations been isolated. He loved learning when young. During Chuping, when the Three Adjuncts were in disorder, Xi sojourned south in Jingzhou. He was not deterred by devastation and disturbance, but carried the classics on his back; whenever there were days left over from gathering rough grain, he recited and studied them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi, courtesy name Ziya, was from Jingzhao. His family had been solitary for generations. He loved learning when young. During Chuping, when the Three Adjuncts were in disorder, Xi sojourned south in Jingzhou. Undeterred by devastation and disturbance, he carried the classics on his back; whenever he had time left after gathering rough grain, he recited and studied them.

sentences.zh: 太祖定荊州，召署軍謀掾。黃初中，爲譙王郎中。王宿聞其儒者，常虛心從學。禧亦敬恭以授王，由是大得賜遺。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor pacified Jingzhou, he summoned Xi to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk. During Huangchu, Xi became Gentleman of the Prince of Qiao. The Prince had long heard that he was a classicist and always studied under him with an open mind. Xi also respectfully instructed the Prince, and because of this he received many gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Jingzhou, he summoned Xi to serve temporarily as Military Planning Clerk. During Huangchu, Xi became Gentleman of the Prince of Qiao. The Prince had long heard that he was a classicist and always studied under him with an open mind. Xi also respectfully instructed the Prince, and because of this received many gifts.

sentences.zh: 以病還，拜郎中。年八十餘，以老處家，就之學者甚多。

translations.literal: He returned because of illness and was appointed Gentleman of the Interior. When he was over eighty years old, he remained at home because of age, and those who went to study with him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He returned because of illness and was appointed Gentleman of the Interior. When he was over eighty, he remained at home because of his age, and those who came to study with him were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 禧旣明經，又善星官，常仰瞻天文，歎息謂魚豢曰：「天下兵戈尚猶未息，如之何？」

translations.literal: Xi both understood the classics and was skilled in the star offices. He often looked up and observed the celestial patterns, and sighing he said to Yu Huan, “The weapons of war under Heaven have still not ceased; what is to be done?”
translations.idiomatic: Xi understood the classics and was also skilled in the star offices. He often looked up to observe the celestial patterns, and with a sigh said to Yu Huan, “The weapons of war under Heaven have still not ceased; what is to be done?”

sentences.zh: 豢又嘗從問《左氏傳》，禧荅曰：「欲知幽微莫若易，人倫之紀莫若禮，多識山川草木之名莫若詩，左氏直相斫書耳，不足精意也。」

translations.literal: Yu Huan also once asked him about the Zuo Tradition, and Xi answered, “If you wish to know the hidden and subtle, nothing is like the Changes; for the order of human relations, nothing is like the Rites; for broadly knowing the names of mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees, nothing is like the Odes. The Zuo is merely a book of mutual hacking and killing, not worth concentrating your mind on.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan also once asked him about the Zuo Tradition, and Xi answered, “If you wish to know the hidden and subtle, nothing is like the Changes; for the order of human relations, nothing is like the Rites; for broadly knowing the names of mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees, nothing is like the Odes. The Zuo is merely a book of people hacking at one another, not worth concentrating your mind on.”

sentences.zh: 豢因從問詩，禧說齊、韓、魯、毛四家義，不復執文，有如諷誦。

translations.literal: Yu Huan therefore asked him about the Odes, and Xi explained the meanings of the four schools of Qi, Han, Lu, and Mao, no longer holding to the text, as if reciting from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan therefore asked him about the Odes, and Xi explained the meanings of the four schools of Qi, Han, Lu, and Mao without again taking up the text, as if reciting from memory.

sentences.zh: 又撰作諸經解數十萬言，未及繕寫而得聾，後數歲病亡也。

translations.literal: He also composed explanations of the various classics amounting to several hundred thousand words. Before they could be copied cleanly, he became deaf, and after several years he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed explanations of the various classics amounting to several hundred thousand words. Before they could be copied out cleanly, he became deaf, and after several years he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 其邯鄲淳事在〈王粲傳〉，蘇林事在〈劉邵〉〈高堂隆傳〉，樂詳事在〈杜畿傳〉。

translations.literal: The affairs of Handan Chun are in the Biography of Wang Can; the affairs of Su Lin are in the Biographies of Liu Shao and Gao Tanglong; the affairs of Yue Xiang are in the Biography of Du Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of Handan Chun are in the Biography of Wang Can; those of Su Lin are in the Biographies of Liu Shao and Gao Tanglong; those of Yue Xiang are in the Biography of Du Ji.

sentences.zh: 魚豢曰：學之資於人也，其猶藍之染於素乎！故雖仲尼，猶曰「吾非生而知之者」，況凡品哉！

translations.literal: Yu Huan said: Learning’s aid to a person is like blue dye coloring plain silk. Therefore even Zhongni still said, “I am not one born knowing it”; how much more ordinary men!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan said: The aid learning gives a person is like blue dye coloring plain silk. Therefore even Zhongni still said, “I am not one born knowing it”; how much more is this true of ordinary men!

sentences.zh: 且世人所以不貴學者，必見夫有「誦詩三百而不能專對於四方」故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason people of the age do not value learning must be that they see those who “recite the three hundred Odes but cannot respond independently to the four quarters.”
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reason people of the age do not value learning must be that they see those who “recite the three hundred Odes but cannot respond independently in missions to the four quarters.”

sentences.zh: 余以爲是則下科耳，不當顧中庸以上，材質適等，而加之以文乎！

translations.literal: I think this is only the lower category. Should one not look instead to those from the mean upward, whose native quality is suitable and equal, and add culture to it?
translations.idiomatic: I think this is only the lower category. Should one not look instead to those from the mean upward, whose native quality is adequate and balanced, and add culture to it?

sentences.zh: 今此數賢者，略余之所識也。檢其事能，誠不多也。但以守學不輟，乃上爲帝王所嘉，下爲國家名儒，非由學乎？

translations.literal: Now these several worthies are roughly those I know of. If one examines their affairs and abilities, they truly were not many. Yet because they kept to learning without ceasing, above they were admired by emperors and kings, and below they became famous classicists of the state. Was this not because of learning?
translations.idiomatic: Now these several worthies are roughly those I know of. If one examines their affairs and abilities, they truly were not numerous. Yet because they kept to learning without ceasing, above they were admired by emperors and kings, and below they became famous classicists of the state. Was this not because of learning?

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，學其胡可以已哉！

translations.literal: Viewed from this, how can learning ever be stopped!
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, how can learning ever be stopped!

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】 (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：鍾繇開達理幹，華歆清純德素，王朗文博富贍，誠皆一時之俊偉也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Zhong Yao was open, penetrating, and capable in management; Hua Xin was pure in virtue; Wang Lang was broad in culture and rich in endowment—truly all were outstanding heroes of their age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhong Yao was open and capable, Hua Xin incorrupt and plain, Wang Lang learned and ample—each was a leading talent of his day.

sentences.zh: 魏氏初祚，肇登三司，盛矣夫！

translations.literal: When the Wei house first received the mandate, they first ascended the Three Dukes—how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: At Wei’s founding they rose together to the Three Excellencies—no small glory.

sentences.zh: 王肅亮直多聞，能析薪哉！

translations.literal: Wang Su was bright, straight, and learned much—able to split firewood indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was candid, learned, and sharp enough to “split the firewood” of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 〈劉寔以爲肅方於事上而好下佞己，此一反也。

translations.literal: 〈Liu Shi thought Su was square in serving superiors yet fond of inferiors flattering himself—this is one contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Liu Shi said Wang Su was stiff toward superiors yet loved flattery from below—the first contradiction.

sentences.zh: 性嗜榮貴而不求苟合，此二反也。

translations.literal: His nature craved glory and nobility yet did not seek improper alliance—this is two contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: He hungered for rank yet would not curry favor—the second contradiction.

sentences.zh: 吝惜財物而治身不穢，此三反也。〉

translations.literal: He was stingy with goods and wealth yet ordering his person was not foul—this is three contradictions.〉
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded coin yet kept his person clean—the third contradiction.〉
